sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: Which class of highway uses the red, white, and blue route shield?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: The red, white and blue shield identifies an interstate highway.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: Which compass directions do one-digit or two-digit even-numbered interstates generally run?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Even-numbered interstates with one or two digits generally run east and west.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: Which compass directions do one-digit or two-digit odd-numbered interstates generally run?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: Odd-numbered interstates with one or two digits generally run north and south.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: How do east-west interstate route numbers climb across the national map?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: For east-west interstate numbering, the national pattern increases from I-ten in the south toward I-ninety-four in the north.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: How do north-south interstate route numbers climb across the national map?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: For north-south interstate numbering, the pattern increases from I-five in the west toward I-ninety-five in the east.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: Where in Pennsylvania does the handbook locate I-seventy-six versus I-eighty and I-eighty-four?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: The handbook places I-seventy-six in southern Pennsylvania and I-eighty-four and I-eighty in northern Pennsylvania.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: Where in Pennsylvania does the handbook locate I-seventy-nine versus I-ninety-five?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: The handbook places I-seventy-nine in western Pennsylvania and I-ninety-five in eastern Pennsylvania.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: What general function do three-digit interstate highways serve?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Interstates with three-digit numbers connect to other major highways.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: What route pattern does a three-digit interstate with an even first digit usually form?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: A three-digit interstate whose first digit is even usually connects with interstates at both ends and may form a loop or beltway.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Which Philadelphia route does the handbook give as an even-first-digit three-digit interstate?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: I-two hundred seventy-six in Philadelphia is the handbook's example of a route with an even first digit.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: What route pattern does a three-digit interstate with an odd first digit usually form?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: A three-digit interstate whose first digit is odd is usually a spur connecting to an interstate at only one end.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: Which Williamsport highway does the handbook cite as an odd-first-digit spur?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: I-one hundred eighty in Williamsport is the handbook's example of a spur that may lead into a city center.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: From what two starting points do Pennsylvania highway mile markers measure distance?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: Mile markers measure from a route's entry into the state, or from its beginning when the route does not reach a state border.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: At which compass ends does mile-marker numbering start at zero?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: Mile-marker numbering starts from zero at the west for east-west roads and at the south for north-south roads.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: When do highway mile-marker numbers rise, and when do they fall?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: Mile-marker values rise when traveling east or north and fall when traveling west or south.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: What mile markers do you pass first when entering Pennsylvania from the west on I-eighty?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: In the handbook's I-eighty example, entering Pennsylvania from the west encounters Mile one before higher markers farther east.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: How does reading roadside mile markers help during a vehicle breakdown or emergency?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: Reading mile markers helps locate the vehicle when requesting roadside assistance.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: Which highway does a black-and-white United States shield displaying twenty-two identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: A U.S. route shield displaying twenty-two identifies U.S. Traffic Route twenty-two.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: Which highway does a keystone-shaped marker displaying thirty-nine identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: A keystone route marker displaying thirty-nine identifies Pennsylvania Traffic Route thirty-nine.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: What does a JCT plate mounted above a numbered route marker announce?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: A JCT plate above a route marker announces an approaching intersection with that route.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: What does a WEST plate mounted above a U.S. Route twenty-two shield tell you?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: A WEST plate above a U.S. Route twenty-two marker indicates westbound travel on that route.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: What does a right-turn arrow placed beneath a WEST U.S. Route twenty-two assembly mean?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: A right-turn arrow below a WEST U.S. Route twenty-two assembly warns that continuing on that route requires the upcoming right turn.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: What does a TO plate with a U.S. Route twenty-two shield and upward arrow direct?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: A TO plate with a U.S. Route twenty-two marker and an upward arrow directs continued straight travel to reach that route.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What colors and shapes do motorist service signs use, and what do they identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: Service signs use blue backgrounds with white letters or symbols, have square or rectangular shapes, and identify services at the next exit.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: Which six traveler needs can blue motorist service symbols identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Service symbols can identify a hospital, telephone, food, gasoline, diesel or lodging.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: What shapes and color combinations do tourist directional signs use?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: Tourist directional signs are squares or rectangles with white lettering on blue or brown.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: What kinds of destinations do tourist directional signs guide motorists toward?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: Tourist directional signs guide traffic to attractions such as museums, historic landmarks and state or national parks.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: What four roadway features do permanent pavement markings identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: Permanent pavement markings identify road centers, lanes, edges and special lane uses.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.front: What traffic separation does yellow pavement paint always indicate?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.expected_back: Yellow pavement lines separate opposing directions of traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.front: Where do yellow lines sit on two-lane roads versus divided highways, one-way streets, and ramps?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.expected_back: Yellow lines mark the center of two-lane roads and the left edge of divided highways, one-way streets and ramps.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.front: What two boundaries do solid white pavement lines mark?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.expected_back: Solid white pavement lines separate same-direction lanes and also mark a roadway's right edge.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.front: What is the general crossing rule for broken traffic lines versus solid traffic lines?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.expected_back: As a general rule, broken traffic lines may be crossed and solid lines may not, except when making a turn.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.front: When does a single broken yellow centerline on a two-lane road allow passing?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.expected_back: A single broken yellow centerline on a two-way, two-lane road permits passing from either side only when conditions are safe.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.front: Which lane does your vehicle occupy while passing across a broken yellow centerline?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.expected_back: Passing across a broken yellow centerline uses the lane for oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.front: What passing rule applies at a double solid yellow centerline when no sign is posted?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.expected_back: A double solid yellow centerline prohibits passing in either direction even without a NO PASSING sign.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.front: When a centerline pairs one solid and one broken yellow stripe, who may pass?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.expected_back: With one solid and one broken yellow centerline, passing is allowed from the broken-line side only when conditions are safe.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.front: What is the rule for the driver on the solid-line side of a mixed yellow centerline?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.expected_back: With one solid and one broken yellow centerline, the driver on the solid-line side may not pass.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.front: How may drivers use a shared center lane framed by solid outer and broken inner yellow lines?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.expected_back: A shared center turn lane bordered by solid outer and broken inner yellow lines is reserved for left turns from either direction and cannot be used for passing.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.front: When may you cross broken white lane lines on an undivided multilane road?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.expected_back: On an undivided multilane road, broken white lane lines may be crossed to pass when the passing lane is clear.

sec06-card-sec06-R23.front: What rule and hazard apply to the double yellow centerline on an undivided multilane road?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.expected_back: On an undivided multilane road, a double yellow centerline cannot be crossed for passing and opposing traffic lies beyond it.

sec06-card-sec06-R24.front: Which paint colors mark the right and left edges of each roadway on a divided highway?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.expected_back: On the usual divided limited-access highway pattern, solid white marks the right edge and solid yellow marks the left edge of each roadway.

sec06-card-sec06-R25.front: May drivers cross broken white lines separating same-direction lanes on a divided limited-access highway?
sec06-card-sec06-R25.expected_back: Broken white lines between same-direction lanes on a divided limited-access highway may be crossed.

sec06-card-sec06-R26.front: How do painted pavement words and arrows work alongside roadside signs?
sec06-card-sec06-R26.expected_back: Pavement words and arrows supplement regulatory and warning signs.

sec06-card-sec06-R27.front: What upcoming traffic control does STOP AHEAD pavement wording announce?
sec06-card-sec06-R27.expected_back: STOP AHEAD pavement wording announces a stop-sign intersection ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-R28.front: What duty do YIELD pavement letters or a row of white triangles across your lane indicate?
sec06-card-sec06-R28.expected_back: YIELD wording or white triangles across a lane indicate that the driver must yield to approaching traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R29.front: What zone does large SCHOOL wording painted on the roadway announce?
sec06-card-sec06-R29.expected_back: SCHOOL pavement wording warns of a school zone ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-R30.front: What hazard does R X R lettering painted on the lane announce?
sec06-card-sec06-R30.expected_back: R X R pavement lettering marks an approaching railroad crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-R31.front: What does BIKE LANE wording painted on a roadway lane identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R31.expected_back: BIKE LANE pavement wording identifies a lane reserved for bicyclists.

sec06-card-sec06-R32.front: What rule applies when ONLY is painted with a left or right lane arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-R32.expected_back: ONLY combined with a left or right pavement arrow reserves the lane for that turn.

sec06-card-sec06-R33.front: Where do large white pavement arrows show legal travel direction?
sec06-card-sec06-R33.expected_back: Large white pavement arrows indicate travel direction on one-way roads and highway exit ramps.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: What two tire conditions should you verify before getting behind the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Before driving, check that the tires have sufficient tread and the correct air pressure.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Where do you find the recommended tire pressure for your vehicle, and how should you measure it?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Use the tire-pressure value in the owner's manual or driver-side door jamb and check it with a pressure gauge.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: When are tires considered cold enough for an accurate air-pressure reading?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Check tire pressure when the tires are cold, before driving or at least three hours after driving.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: How should you correct tire pressure when your gauge reads higher or lower than the specified number?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: If measured pressure is above the specified value, release air until it matches; if below, add air or seek tire-professional help.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: How often should you inspect your tires for wear and visible damage?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Inspect tires for wear and damage once a month or before a long road trip.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: How do you position a penny when checking tire tread depth?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: For the penny tread check, hold Lincoln's body and insert his head into a groove where the tread appears lowest.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: What visual result on the penny test tells you your tire still has a safe amount of tread?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: In the handbook's penny test, tread covering any part of Lincoln's head indicates the stated safe amount of tread.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: What happens to vehicle handling when tire tread wears below the penny-test threshold?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Tread below the penny-test level greatly reduces tire grip in adverse conditions.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: What roadside tools and gear should stay in your vehicle in case you get a flat tire?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: Keep tire-changing equipment in the vehicle, including a spare, lug wrench, jack, flashlight, warning devices, wheel wedges, repair kit and gloves.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Which three vehicle fluids should you routinely check and top off according to the owner's manual?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Check oil, washer fluid and fuel, and refill as the owner's manual directs.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: How should you position the driver's seat before shifting out of park?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: Set the driver's seat so the pedals and controls are easy to reach and the windshield view is clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: Which parts of the seat belt system must you wear every time you drive?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: Wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt on every trip.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: Why are unrestrained items inside the cabin dangerous during a sudden collision?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Loose objects can become projectiles in a crash while continuing at the vehicle's pre-impact speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: Where should you stow heavy items, and what should you do if they must ride in the cabin?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: Put heavy objects in the trunk when possible, or secure them with seat belts.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: Why should you keep the rear window shelf completely clear of stored items?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Do not place stored objects on the rear window deck.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: Which cabin adjustment must come first: setting the mirrors or positioning the driver's seat?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: Adjust the seat before setting the mirrors.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: What view should your inside rearview mirror frame once you finish adjusting it?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Set the rearview mirror to show traffic directly behind the vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: How far outward should you angle your side mirrors to minimize blind spots?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Set side mirrors so the vehicle's side is barely visible when leaning toward that side.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: Why can you not rely on the previous driver's mirror angles when sharing a car?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: Mirror settings may need to differ between drivers to remove blind spots.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: What is the rule on hanging air fresheners, charms, or other items from the rearview mirror while driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Do not hang objects from the rearview mirror while the vehicle is moving.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: When is it legal to hang parking tags, permits, or placards from your rearview mirror?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: Tags, permits and placards may hang from the rearview mirror only while the vehicle is parked.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: What restriction applies to mounts, stickers, or accessories placed on the windshield?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: Nothing may be attached to the windshield where it obstructs the driver's road view.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: What two hazards does keeping fresh air circulating inside the cabin help prevent?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: Maintain fresh air in the vehicle to support alertness and guard against exhaust-related carbon monoxide poisoning.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: How high should you set the top of your head restraint?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: Set the head restraint so its top reaches at least the height of the top of the driver's ears.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: What specific protection does a properly adjusted head restraint provide in a collision?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: A properly positioned head restraint can prevent or reduce neck-injury severity in a crash.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: When must you wear your prescription glasses or contact lenses behind the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: Always use prescription glasses or contacts while driving if you normally wear corrective lenses.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: Why must you avoid sunglasses and tinted contact lenses when driving after dark?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: Do not use sunglasses or tinted contact lenses for night driving.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: How do locked doors work together with your seat belt during a serious crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: Locking the doors and wearing a seat belt help prevent being thrown out during a crash.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: Besides crash protection, how does locking your doors protect you at red lights and parking lots?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: Locked doors also reduce the likelihood of victimization when stopped at an intersection or parking area.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: What three core things can a driving distraction pull away from operating the vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: A driving distraction takes attention from driving, eyes from the road or hands from the wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: How do eating, drinking, or smoking behind the wheel affect your ability to handle sudden hazards?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: Eating, drinking or smoking can draw hands and eyes away from driving and slow the response to hazards.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: How does the Pennsylvania handbook classify tuning the radio or changing playlists while moving?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: Adjusting audio equipment is a driving distraction.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: Under what strict limits may a Pennsylvania driver wear an earpiece or headphone while driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: Headphones or earpieces may be used in only one ear and only for communication.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: Does switching a phone call to speaker or Bluetooth eliminate driver distraction?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: A phone conversation can distract a driver even when the phone is hands-free.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: How can friends or other passengers riding in the car hurt your driving performance?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: Interacting with passengers can distract the driver.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: Why should you pull over instead of reaching for a dropped or sliding item while driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: Searching for or moving an item inside the vehicle is a distraction.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.front: Why must tasks like texting, reading notes, or fixing hair wait until the car is parked?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.expected_back: Reading, writing, texting and personal grooming can divert attention from driving.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.front: What danger comes from rubbernecking at a roadside crash, work crew, or activity off the roadway?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.expected_back: Staring at a crash, work zone or an off-road event can distract a driver.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.front: Which three essential driving abilities deteriorate when you drive tired?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.expected_back: Tiredness slows reactions and impairs judgment and vision.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: To what well-known form of impairment does the handbook compare drowsy driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: Fatigued driving can affect a driver in ways similar to alcohol impairment.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: Staying awake for eighteen straight hours produces driving impairment comparable to what blood alcohol level?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.memory_hook: Eighteen hours equals point zero five
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: The handbook compares eighteen hours awake with about the driving impairment associated with a point zero five percent blood alcohol level.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: Going twenty-four straight hours without sleep impairs a driver roughly like what blood alcohol concentration?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.memory_hook: Twenty-four hours equals point one zero
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: The handbook compares twenty-four continuous hours awake with impairment associated with a point one zero percent blood alcohol level.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: Can an exhausted driver always tell the exact moment they are about to nod off?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: A sufficiently tired driver may fall asleep without realizing it.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: How long does a driver need to doze off for a crash to turn deadly?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: Even a few seconds asleep at the wheel can be fatal.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Below how many hours of nightly sleep do teen drivers see a higher crash risk?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: Teenagers sleeping less than eight hours nightly face increased vehicle-crash risk.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: What does the handbook say to do if you start feeling drowsy behind the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: If tiredness develops while driving, the handbook recommends stopping driving.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: How often does the handbook recommend having your eyesight professionally checked?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.memory_hook: Eye check one to two years
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: Vision should be checked every one or two years.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: Which three visual skills can health conditions or aging quietly degrade without you realizing it?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Disease and aging can worsen side vision, distance judgment and low-light vision without the driver noticing.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: If your license carries a corrective-lens requirement, how often must you wear your glasses or contacts?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: Use required glasses or contact lenses every time the vehicle is driven.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: What critical road warnings can your sense of hearing catch before you ever see them?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: Hearing can reveal unseen hazards, approaching emergency vehicles and trains at crossings.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.front: How can everyday aches like a stiff neck or sore knee affect your driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.expected_back: Medical problems, including a stiff neck or sore knee, can interfere with effective vehicle control.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.front: Which three major medical conditions does the handbook highlight as serious risks for safe driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.expected_back: Seizure disorders involving loss of consciousness, diabetes and heart conditions are among the serious driving-related health problems identified by the handbook.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.front: What legal duty do Pennsylvania doctors have when they diagnose a patient with a driving-impairing condition?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.expected_back: Pennsylvania physicians must report to PennDOT people they diagnose with a condition that could impair safe driving.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.front: At what blood alcohol concentration is a driver under age twenty-one legally considered under the influence in Pennsylvania?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.memory_hook: Under twenty-one limit point zero two
sec07-card-sec07-R15.expected_back: Drivers younger than twenty-one are considered to be driving under the influence at a blood alcohol concentration of point zero two percent or higher.

sec07-card-sec07-R16.front: How much alcohol does it take to start weakening your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.expected_back: Even a small amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment and memory and impair driving skills.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.front: What happens to your driving mistakes and core control skills as blood alcohol concentration climbs?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.expected_back: As blood alcohol rises, driving errors increase while vision, judgment, reactions and vehicle control deteriorate.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.front: What dangerous mismatch does alcohol create between how capable a driver feels and how well they actually drive?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.expected_back: Alcohol can produce dangerous confidence while reducing the driver's actual skills.

sec07-card-sec07-R19.front: What is Pennsylvania's legal blood alcohol limit for adult drivers aged twenty-one and older?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.expected_back: The handbook describes point zero eight percent as the legal blood alcohol limit for an adult aged twenty-one or older.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.front: Does staying under the legal blood alcohol limit guarantee that you are safe to drive?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.expected_back: Alcohol in the blood can make driving dangerous even below the legal limit.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.front: According to the Pennsylvania handbook, how much alcohol is genuinely safe to drink before driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.expected_back: The handbook states that the safe amount of alcohol before driving is zero.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.front: What personal and situational factors change how high your blood alcohol level rises from drinking?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.expected_back: Age, weight, gender, physical condition, food and drugs or medication affect blood alcohol levels.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.front: Why can two people who each have one drink still consume very different amounts of pure alcohol?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.expected_back: Drinks can contain different amounts of alcohol, so their alcohol content matters.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.front: What serving sizes of eighty-proof liquor, regular beer, and wine each count as one standard drink?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.expected_back: The handbook's standard-drink examples are one point five ounces of eighty-proof liquor, twelve ounces of regular beer or five ounces of wine.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.front: Roughly how long does it take an average-weight person's body to process the alcohol in a single standard drink?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.expected_back: For a person of average weight, the handbook says processing the alcohol in one drink takes at least one hour.

sec07-card-sec07-R26.front: What caution does the handbook attach to the one-drink-per-hour pacing rule for legal-age drinkers?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.expected_back: The handbook advises legal-age drinkers not to exceed one drink per hour, while warning that this guideline does not work for everyone and does not make driving after drinking safe.

sec07-card-sec07-R27.front: How does smaller body size affect alcohol concentration in the bloodstream?
sec07-card-sec07-R27.expected_back: Alcohol is more concentrated in smaller people.

sec07-card-sec07-R28.front: If a woman and a man weigh the same and drink identically over the same timeframe, how can their blood alcohol levels compare?
sec07-card-sec07-R28.expected_back: A woman may reach a higher blood alcohol level than a same-weight man after equal alcohol intake over the same time.

sec07-card-sec07-R29.front: Do strong coffee, energy drinks, or a cold shower actually lower your blood alcohol concentration?
sec07-card-sec07-R29.expected_back: Only time lowers blood alcohol concentration; coffee, other caffeine drinks and cold showers do not reduce it.

sec07-card-sec07-R30.front: What dual responsibility do you have regarding driving after drinking—both for yourself and for others?
sec07-card-sec07-R30.expected_back: Do not drive after consuming any alcohol, and prevent a person who has been drinking from driving.

sec07-card-sec07-R31.front: Which categories of drugs and medications are capable of impairing your driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R31.expected_back: Illegal drugs, prescription medicines and over-the-counter products can all impair driving.

sec07-card-sec07-R32.front: What happens when someone mixes medications or other drugs with alcohol before driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R32.expected_back: Combining drugs with alcohol intensifies side effects and greatly increases crash risk.

sec07-card-sec07-R33.front: How does marijuana impair the specific skills needed to control a vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R33.expected_back: Marijuana can slow reactions, impair time and distance judgment and reduce coordination.

sec07-card-sec07-R34.front: How can stimulants like cocaine or methamphetamine alter a driver's behavior in traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-R34.expected_back: Cocaine or methamphetamine can make a driver aggressive and reckless.

sec07-card-sec07-R35.front: What two side effects from sedative medications make driving dangerous?
sec07-card-sec07-R35.expected_back: Certain sedatives can cause dizziness and drowsiness.

sec07-card-sec07-R36.front: How can opioid pain medications affect a driver behind the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-R36.expected_back: Opioids can cause drowsiness and slower reactions.

sec07-card-sec07-R37.front: Which common household or pharmacy remedies can unexpectedly hurt your driving skills?
sec07-card-sec07-R37.expected_back: Sleeping pills, cough medicines, antihistamines and decongestants can affect driving skills.

sec07-card-sec07-R38.front: What quick check should you perform on any medication container before getting in the driver's seat?
sec07-card-sec07-R38.expected_back: Read medicine warning labels for side effects before driving.

sec07-card-sec07-R39.front: Who should you consult before driving if you are unsure how a medicine might affect you?
sec07-card-sec07-R39.expected_back: Ask a doctor or pharmacist about uncertain medication side effects before driving.

sec07-card-sec07-R40.front: What does a medication label warning against operating heavy machinery mean for drivers?
sec07-card-sec07-R40.expected_back: A warning against operating heavy machinery applies to driving a vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-R41.front: What precaution should you take with your doctor whenever you start a brand-new prescription?
sec07-card-sec07-R41.expected_back: When starting a new medication, consult the doctor and learn its potential side effects.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: Why should you drop your speed before starting a turn rather than braking mid-corner?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Before turning, slow enough to control the vehicle, stay in its lane and react to unexpected hazards.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: What should you scan for on the street you are turning onto, and what lane directions must you obey?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Watch for pedestrians and traffic on the road being entered, and follow signs or markings specifying turn lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Where within your lane should you position your car for a left turn versus a right turn on a two-lane, two-way road?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: On a two-lane, two-way road, begin a left turn as near the centerline as possible and a right turn near the right edge.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: Which lanes must you start from when turning left or right on a multilane road without special turn-lane arrows?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: On a multilane road, start left turns from the left lane and right turns from the right lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: Which lane must you enter first when turning onto a road that has multiple lanes moving your way?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: When entering a road with several lanes in the intended direction, turn into the nearest lane for that direction.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: When is it safe to move over into a different lane after making a turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Complete the turn safely before changing into another lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: What is the sole legal use of a center lane bordered by solid yellow outer lines and broken inner lines?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: A center lane with solid outer and broken inner lines on both sides is for left turns only.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: Which directions of traffic are allowed to pull into a shared center turn lane to start a left turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Drivers in either direction use the shared center lane to begin a left turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: How may a driver turning left out of a side street legally use a shared center turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: A driver turning left from a cross street may end the turn in the shared center lane before joining through traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: Which two sources of conflicting vehicles must you watch for as you pull into a shared center turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: When entering a center turn lane, watch for opposing center-lane traffic and vehicles entering from driveways or streets on the left.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: What traffic streams must you check before turning left out of a driveway into a shared center turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: When turning left from a driveway into a center lane, watch through traffic from the left and center-lane vehicles preparing turns from either direction.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: How many seconds ahead should you signal left before moving into a shared center turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: Signal left at least three to four seconds before entering a center turn lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: Why is it dangerous to pull into a shared center turn lane far ahead of your turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Avoid entering a center turn lane too early because traveling in it longer increases head-on conflict risk.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: How should your vehicle sit inside the center turn lane while waiting to turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Enter the center turn lane completely without leaving the vehicle's rear in a through lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: What two checks must be clear before you complete your left turn out of a shared center lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Turn from the center lane only when safe, after checking opposing lane users and a sufficiently large gap across traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: What four steps summarize executing a clean, legal turn from start to finish?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: For a safe turn, signal three to four seconds ahead, use the proper starting lane, control speed and finish in the proper lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: What overarching safety condition must always be met before making a U-turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: A U-turn is permitted only where it does not endanger other traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: How far away must approaching vehicles be—and what visibility is required—to make a legal U-turn in Pennsylvania?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: For a U-turn, approaching drivers from every direction must be at least five hundred feet away and able to see you clearly.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: At which three road locations or posted zones are U-turns strictly prohibited?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Do not make a U-turn on a curve, near or approaching a hillcrest, or where a NO U-TURN sign prohibits it.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: What conditions must you satisfy before turning right at a steady red light?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: A right turn on red requires stopping, yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic, a clear path and no NO TURN ON RED restriction.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: When is turning left at a steady red light legal in Pennsylvania?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: A left turn on red between one-way streets is allowed after stopping if traffic is clear and no NO TURN ON RED sign prohibits it.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: Which three real-time conditions determine how big a traffic gap you need to cross a roadway safely?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: The traffic gap needed to cross depends on road conditions, weather and approaching traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: Under what single condition is it safe to stop halfway while crossing a divided street?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Stopping partway across a street is safe only if a center-median turning lane can hold the entire vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: What should you confirm about your exit path before committing to cross or turn through an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: Before crossing or turning, make sure vehicles or pedestrians will not block the path.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: What must you do at a green light if backed-up traffic ahead would trap you inside the intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: Even with green, wait outside a blocked intersection until the vehicle can clear it.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: Why should you wait before pulling out in front of an approaching car that has its turn signal on?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: Before pulling out ahead of a signaling vehicle, wait until its driver actually begins turning.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: Why do intersections near hillcrests or curves require extra caution before pulling across?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Use added caution when crossing near hills or curves that restrict seeing or being seen.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: What do you need in the highway lane beside you before merging into moving traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: A highway merge requires enough open space to join the traffic stream safely.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: What two purposes do highway acceleration lanes serve for entering drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: Acceleration lanes run beside through lanes so entering traffic can approach traffic speed and be seen before merging.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: Are you allowed to overtake a slower car ahead of you while still inside a highway acceleration lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Passing a vehicle ahead within an acceleration lane is illegal.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: What four actions take you cleanly from an acceleration lane into highway traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: To merge from an acceleration lane, signal, find a gap, reach traffic speed and enter that gap.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: Why must you use extra caution if passing near crossroads or shopping-center entrances?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: When passing, use extra care near crossroads and shopping access points where vehicles or pedestrians may enter.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: Why is overtaking on a two-lane, two-way road one of the highest-risk maneuvers in driving?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Passing on a two-lane road uses the opposing lane and requires judgment to avoid a head-on collision.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: At forty-five miles per hour, how much clear road ahead do you need to safely pass a slower vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: At forty-five miles per hour, the handbook calls for a quarter mile of clear road to pass a slower vehicle safely.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: What must you confirm ahead of a line of slower cars before trying to pass multiple vehicles?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: Before passing several vehicles, identify enough open space ahead of the last one to return safely.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: How does darkness distort your perception of oncoming vehicles when passing at night?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Night passing makes distance judgment harder, and oncoming headlights may seem farther away than they are.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: What road layout allows you to legally pass another vehicle on the right?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Passing on the right is allowed on a road with at least two marked traffic lanes in each direction.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: How close to an intersection or railroad crossing is passing banned unless traffic controls specifically allow it?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: Do not pass within one hundred feet of or across an intersection or railroad crossing unless an official traffic-control device permits it.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: Within what distance of a bridge, elevated roadway, or tunnel must you stay in your lane instead of passing?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: Do not pass within one hundred feet of a bridge, elevated structure or tunnel.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: Why is passing illegal on or near a curve or hillcrest with limited forward visibility?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: Do not pass on or approaching a curve or hillcrest that blocks the view of opposing traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: May you use the paved shoulder of a multilane highway to pass slower traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Passing on the shoulder of a multilane highway is prohibited.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: What legal controls and roadside hazards should you check ahead before starting a pass?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: Before passing, check signs and pavement markings for permission and scan for hazards such as entering driveways.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: Why must you check both your mirrors and blind spot right before pulling out to pass?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: Check mirrors and blind spots before passing to ensure another vehicle is not already starting to pass you.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: Once behind you is clear, what two steps come right before moving into the passing lane?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: Verify that the passing lane is clear and signal the lane change early enough for others to understand.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: What mirror landmark tells you that you have cleared a passed vehicle far enough to return to your lane?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: After passing, signal before returning and wait until both headlights of the passed vehicle are visible in the rearview mirror.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Does Pennsylvania intersection law grant an absolute right to go, or define who must yield?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Intersection law specifies who must yield rather than granting an unconditional right to proceed.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: What must you do if another driver fails to yield when traffic law says they should?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Even if another driver should yield, stop or yield as needed to prevent a crash.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: When must you yield to pedestrians crossing at an intersection without traffic signals?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: At an unsignalized intersection, yield to crossing pedestrians whether or not a crosswalk is marked.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: Must you yield to pedestrians inside a marked crosswalk located between intersections?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk, even away from an intersection.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: Who goes first when your vehicle crosses a sidewalk to enter or leave an alley or driveway?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Yield when a pedestrian on a sidewalk crosses a driveway or alley.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Who has priority when you turn across a crosswalk where pedestrians are crossing with the signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: A turning driver must yield to pedestrians crossing with the light.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: What is your yielding duty toward a blind pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Always yield to a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: Without a turn arrow or police direction, who must a left-turning driver yield to?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: Without contrary directions from traffic controls or police, a left-turning driver yields to oncoming traffic continuing straight.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: Who holds priority at the entrance of a roundabout?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: A roundabout entrant yields to vehicles already circulating.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: When two drivers on different roads reach an uncontrolled intersection at roughly the same time, who yields?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Without other traffic-control directions, drivers arriving from different roads at about the same time yield to vehicles on their right.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What must you wait for before pulling onto a public highway from a driveway, alley, or private road?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: From an alley, driveway or private road, wait for a clear public highway before entering.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: How is the order of movement decided at a four-way stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: At a four-way stop, every vehicle stops and the earliest arrival should proceed first.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Who yields when two vehicles stop at a four-way intersection at the exact same moment?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: At a four-way stop, simultaneous arrivals yield to the vehicle on the right.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: Can two opposing vehicles at a four-way stop move at the same time?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: Opposing vehicles at a four-way stop may proceed cautiously together while watching for turns.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Why should you scan lane-assignment signs and pavement arrows well ahead of an intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Read lane-assignment signs and markings early enough to choose the proper intersection lane in advance.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: What must you do if you end up in a marked turn-only lane when you meant to go straight?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: A driver mistakenly in a turn-only lane must make the marked turn rather than continue straight.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: What must you do if you want to turn at an intersection while occupying a through-only lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: A driver wanting a turn but occupying a through-only lane must continue straight.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: How must you steer when turning from one of two side-by-side left-turn lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: When adjacent lanes both permit left turns, remain in the selected lane during the turn because the neighboring driver may turn simultaneously.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: What visual clue from parked cars suggests a cross street is one-way?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: Cars parked on both sides facing one direction can be a clue that a street is one-way.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: What makes up a divided highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: A divided highway consists of opposing one-way roadways, usually separated by a physical barrier.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: From which direction do you need a safe gap when turning right onto a divided highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: For a right turn onto a divided highway, select a safe gap in traffic approaching from the left.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: How do you check gaps step-by-step when turning left onto a divided highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: For a left turn onto a divided highway, cross the first roadway through a safe gap from the left, then turn beyond the divider through a safe gap from the right.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: What happens if you turn left before passing the median divider at a divided highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: Turning left before reaching the divider can put the vehicle into opposing traffic; heed WRONG WAY and DO NOT ENTER signs.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: Roughly how big a gap in both directions does crossing a thirty-mile-per-hour street from a two-way stop take?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: At a two-way stop, crossing a thirty miles per hour road takes about a six-second gap in both directions, or about a clear block each way.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: What scan order and time gap from the left do you need before turning right onto a cross street?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: Before a right turn, scan left, ahead, right and left again, allowing about eight seconds to a vehicle approaching from the left.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: What two traffic conditions must you confirm before starting a left turn at an intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Before a left turn, make sure oncoming traffic leaves a clear gap and cross-street traffic is stopped.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: How many seconds of clearance from the right do you need when turning left from a minor road onto a major road?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: Turning left from a minor road onto a major road calls for a nine-second gap to traffic approaching from the right.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: How do two opposing drivers both turning left avoid tangling paths in the intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: Opposing left-turning drivers avoid tangling by turning before the center crossing point and entering the lane nearest the centerline.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: When is it safe to start turning left across multiple oncoming lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: Do not begin a left turn until every lane to be crossed is visibly clear and the turn can be completed safely.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How does a jughandle ramp let you complete a left turn off a major road?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: A jughandle makes a left turn by following a right-side curved lane back to a signalized crossing of the main road.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: In which direction does traffic move around a roundabout, and how do drivers enter and exit?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Traffic circulates counterclockwise through roundabouts and traffic circles, entering and leaving with right turns.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Which two traffic controls mark the entrance to a roundabout?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Roundabout entries have yield signs and pavement yield lines.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: How do most roundabouts help approaching drivers identify which leg leads to their route?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: Most roundabouts have approach destination signs identifying the exit roads.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: How should you approach a roundabout before reaching the circular roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: Approach a roundabout slowly and prepare to yield to people in the crosswalk.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: Which direction do you check at a roundabout yield line, and when may you enter?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: At the yield line, look left, yield to circulating traffic and enter only through an adequate gap.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: How should you travel once inside a roundabout until reaching your street?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: Inside a roundabout, continue counterclockwise toward the intended exit.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: Which turn signal should you activate as your roundabout exit comes up?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Use the right turn signal as the roundabout exit approaches.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: At which two points of a roundabout trip must you yield to pedestrians?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians when entering and leaving a roundabout.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches before you enter a roundabout?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: If an emergency vehicle approaches before entry, do not enter the roundabout and pull aside.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: What should you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already circulating inside a roundabout?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: If already circulating when an emergency vehicle approaches, leave the roundabout and pull aside rather than stopping inside.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: Which two ways may a bicyclist navigate a roundabout, and what rules govern riding in the lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: A bicyclist may use a roundabout as a vehicle or pedestrian; the vehicle role follows the same traffic rules.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.front: Are you allowed to pass a bicyclist riding in the travel lane inside a roundabout?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.expected_back: Do not overtake a bicyclist operating as a vehicle inside a roundabout.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.front: Which two roundabout features help pedestrians cross each approach leg safely?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.expected_back: Pedestrians use crosswalks and splitter islands to cross the roundabout's legs.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.front: What can happen to your vehicle if you enter a curve going too fast?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.expected_back: Entering a curve too fast can carry a vehicle straight ahead instead of along the bend.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.front: Which combination of road geometry and surface conditions requires the biggest drop in speed?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.expected_back: The greatest speed reductions are needed on sharp curves with wet or icy surfaces.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.front: When should you reduce speed for an upcoming curve?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.expected_back: Reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain control.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.front: How do standard curve warning signs differ from warnings for a sharp ninety-degree turn?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.expected_back: Curve warnings are usually yellow diamonds, while a ninety-degree bend may have a large arrow on a yellow rectangle.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.front: How do roadside chevron signs help drivers along sharp bends?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.expected_back: Chevron signs along sharp curves help show the direction of the bend, especially at night or in poor visibility.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.front: Where in your lane should you position your vehicle on a right curve versus a left curve?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.expected_back: On a right curve, stay slightly right of lane center; on a left curve, stay centered.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.front: How should your speed change as a curve gets sharper?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.expected_back: Reduce speed more as curve sharpness increases.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.front: Why must you keep a close eye on opposing traffic while rounding a curve?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.expected_back: Watch opposing traffic in a curve because a speeding driver may enter your lane.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.front: Where should your eyes look to steer smoothly through a curve or series of S-bends?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.expected_back: Look ahead along the curve's inside edge for steering guidance, checking each bend in a sequence as far ahead as visible.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: Which three signs help keep you from mistaking a highway exit ramp for an entrance ramp?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Before entering a highway, avoid mistaking the exit ramp for the entrance; watch ONE WAY, WRONG WAY and DO NOT ENTER signs.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: What optional green sign sometimes marks a highway entrance ramp?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: A green HIGHWAY ENTRANCE sign may identify an entrance ramp, but is not always present.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: How should white and yellow pavement edge lines sit relative to your car on a highway ramp?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: A white edge line on the right and yellow on the left indicate the proper direction of travel on the ramp.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: Who yields when entering and exiting drivers share the same highway weaving lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: In a shared weaving lane, an entering driver yields to the exiting driver.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: How should you use an acceleration lane and check traffic before merging onto a highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Use an acceleration lane to build toward traffic speed, checking the side mirror and looking over the shoulder for a gap.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: When should you move into a highway exit lane, and when should you start slowing down?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Move into the exit lane early and slow only after entering that lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: What is the only safe and legal choice if you overshoot your highway exit?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: If the exit is missed, use the next exit rather than stopping, reversing, crossing multiple lanes suddenly or crossing the median.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: What does a yellow warning speed sign posted along an exit ramp tell you?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Exit-ramp warning signs indicate the maximum safe ramp speed.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Roughly how many feet per second does a vehicle cover at sixty-five miles per hour?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: At sixty-five miles per hour, a vehicle covers almost one hundred feet per second.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: How should you handle lane changes and turn signals when passing on a multi-lane highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: When passing on a highway, change only one lane at a time and signal each lane change well ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: How can a highway driver safely help someone merging from an entrance ramp?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: A through driver may help a highway entrant by changing lanes courteously, but must first verify space is clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: What visual habit triggers highway hypnosis on long drives?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Highway hypnosis develops when prolonged staring replaces scanning ahead, behind and around the vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: What is the maximum legal distance from the curb when parking parallel along a Pennsylvania street?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: Along a curb, park as close as possible and no farther than twelve inches away.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: Where should you position your vehicle when parking along a road that has no curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Without a curb, park as far off the roadway as possible.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: What three precautions are required if you have no choice except to leave a vehicle on the roadway?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: When roadway parking is necessary, use hazard flashers, allow passing room and remain visible for at least five hundred feet in both directions.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: Which way must your parked vehicle face, and what else must you ensure before walking away?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Park facing the direction of traffic and secure the vehicle against movement.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Which brake and gear settings secure automatic versus manual vehicles when parked?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: When parking, set the parking brake and select Park for an automatic transmission, or Reverse or First for a manual.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking downhill next to a curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: For downhill parking with a curb, turn the wheels fully right.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking uphill beside a curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: For uphill parking with a curb, turn the wheels left.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: Which way must your front wheels point when parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: On a hill without a curb, point the wheels right whether facing uphill or downhill.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: May you stop or park in the street alongside a vehicle already parked at the curb?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Unless an emergency or police direction requires otherwise, do not double park beside a stopped or parked roadside vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Are stopping, standing, or parking allowed on sidewalks, on crosswalks, or inside intersections?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, do not stop, stand or park on a sidewalk, crosswalk or within an intersection.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: What rule governs stopping, standing, or parking beside or across from street excavations or roadwork?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, do not stop, stand or park along or opposite road excavation or work areas.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Where is stopping, standing, or parking prohibited on bridges, elevated highways, and tunnels?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, do not stop, stand or park on a bridge, elevated structure or in a highway tunnel.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: How far must you stay from the nearest rail when parking near a railroad crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, do not stop, stand or park on railroad tracks or within fifty feet of the nearest rail at a crossing.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: May ordinary drivers stop, stand, or park in the median or crossovers of a divided highway?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, do not stop, stand or park between divided-highway roadways, including crossovers.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: When may you disregard official signs prohibiting stopping or parking?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, obey official signs prohibiting stopping or parking.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: What stopping, standing, and parking rule applies across public or private driveways?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, do not stop, stand or park in front of a public or private driveway.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: How many feet of clearance must you leave when parking near a fire hydrant in Pennsylvania?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, do not stop, stand or park within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: Within how many feet of an intersection crosswalk are stopping, standing, and parking banned?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, do not stop, stand or park within twenty feet of an intersection crosswalk.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: How far back must you park from a stop sign, yield sign, flashing beacon, or roadside signal?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, do not stop, stand or park within thirty feet of a roadside flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign or traffic-control device.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: How close may you park to the driveway entrance of a fire station?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, do not stop, stand or park within twenty feet of a fire-station driveway entrance.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.front: What parking rule protects urban streetcar and trolley routes?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.expected_back: Except for emergencies or police direction, do not stop, stand or park where a streetcar's movement would be blocked.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.front: When are stopping, standing, or parking allowed along a limited-access expressway?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.expected_back: On a limited-access highway, stopping, standing and parking are prohibited unless an emergency, police direction or official traffic-control device allows them.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.front: Where do you line up beside the front car to begin parallel parking at a right-hand curb?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.expected_back: To parallel park at a right curb, begin beside the vehicle ahead, level with it and two feet away.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.front: How should your front wheels be turned as you start backing slowly into a right-curb parallel spot?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.expected_back: Begin backing slowly toward the rear vehicle with the wheels turned sharply right.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.front: At what visual landmark do you straighten your wheels and back straight during a parallel park?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.expected_back: As the front door passes the leading vehicle's rear bumper, straighten the wheels and continue backing straight.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.front: Which way do you steer once your front end clears the leading vehicle's rear bumper?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.expected_back: Once clear of the front vehicle, steer sharply left and continue backing slowly toward the rear vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.front: How do you finish and center your vehicle inside a parallel-parking space?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.expected_back: Finish the parallel park by steering sharply right and pulling forward toward the space's center.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.front: What steps secure your vehicle and protect passing traffic right before you step out street-side?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.expected_back: Before leaving the vehicle, turn the engine off, remove the key and lock the doors, checking rear traffic before stepping out.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: What three types of road operations and what color traffic controls mark a Pennsylvania work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Work zones contain construction, maintenance or utility operations and use orange channelizers or temporary traffic controls.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: At least how far ahead of the work area might warning signs, vehicles, or message boards start appearing?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Work-zone warnings, vehicles or message boards may be positioned at least two hundred feet before the work area.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Once you pass the very first work-zone warning, which four things demand your close attention?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: From the first work-zone warning, attend closely to the roadway, vehicles, equipment and people.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: When are you allowed to pass a moving road-work operation?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Do not pass a moving road-work operation unless directed to do so.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: What makes a work zone active, and which three roadway changes might you encounter inside one?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: An active work zone has workers on or near the road and may have narrow lanes, rough pavement or abrupt lane shifts.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: Who gets the right-of-way inside a Pennsylvania work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Yield to workers and construction vehicles in work zones.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Why are daytime running lights not enough when driving through a Pennsylvania work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Use actual headlights in work zones rather than daytime running lights alone.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: How do fines and license consequences escalate for speeding or certain violations inside an active work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Certain active-work-zone fines, including speeding penalties, are doubled and some violations can suspend the license.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: What simple route choice does the handbook suggest to dodge work-zone backups?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: Consider another route to avoid work-zone delays.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: Should you use cruise control while driving through a work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Do not use cruise control in a work zone.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: How should you adjust your normal following distance inside a work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Double the normal following gap in work zones.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: When should you get ready to move over if a work-zone lane is closing ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: Prepare to change lanes when the first message announces the lane closure.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: What lane rule applies when you see a solid white line inside a work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Stay in the lane and do not cross a solid white work-zone line.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: How should you keep moving past active road work instead of slowing down to watch?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Continue cautiously at a safe speed rather than stopping or slowing just to watch the work.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: Why must you never pull up and stop inside a work zone to ask road crews for directions?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: Do not stop within a work zone to ask workers for directions.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: Whose instructions win when a work-zone flagger contradicts a regular traffic light or sign?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: Follow flagger directions, which take precedence over conventional traffic-control devices.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: How can a flagger trigger police enforcement against an aggressive, speeding, or unsafe driver?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: Flaggers may report unsafe driving, speeding and aggression to police using a Police Arrest Form.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: How should you check railroad tracks as you approach, even when the crossing lights stay dark?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Look left, right and left again approaching tracks even if installed signals are not flashing.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: After one train clears a crossing with multiple tracks, when is it safe to pull forward?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: After a train clears multiple tracks, wait for a clear view along both tracks before crossing.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: What check should you still make at a single railroad track right after a train passes?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: Even at a single track, check for another train before crossing after the first passes.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: Are you allowed to pass another vehicle as you approach or cross railroad tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Do not pass another vehicle while approaching or entering a rail crossing.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: When traffic ahead is backed up beyond a railroad crossing, where must you hold your car?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Enter tracks only when there is room to clear them completely, waiting if traffic ahead is backed up.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: What should you do right away if your car gets trapped on railroad tracks with a train coming?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: If trapped on tracks with a train approaching, leave the vehicle quickly and move as far from the track as possible.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: Where must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians at intersections and crosswalks.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: What must you do before making a permitted right turn on a red light?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Before a right turn on red, stop and scan all directions, allowing pedestrians time to clear the crossing.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: How should you adjust your driving whenever children are near the roadway?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: Slow down and take extra care near children.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: How should you respond when older adults or pedestrians with disabilities are crossing the street?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: Allow older pedestrians and people with disabilities extra time to cross.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: Who must you specifically check for before shifting into reverse and backing up?

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: How must you react when you spot a blind pedestrian with a cane, guide dog, or human guide?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Slow and prepare to stop for a blind pedestrian using a cane, guide dog or another person's guidance.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: What should you do before passing a vehicle stopped ahead of you in traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: Before passing a stopped vehicle, slow and verify no pedestrian is crossing ahead of it.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: Why should you avoid waving a pedestrian across the street, especially mid-block or at unmarked crossings?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: Do not wave a pedestrian into traffic, especially at unmarked or mid-block crossings.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: On flat pavement, how much longer does passing a large truck take compared with passing a car?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: On level roads, passing a truck takes three to five seconds longer than passing a passenger vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: How do uphill climbs and downhill grades change a large truck's speed when you plan a pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: A truck may slow uphill or gain momentum downhill, changing the passing situation.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: How should you position your car, pace your pass, and grip the wheel while overtaking a truck?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: Leave room ahead in the passing lane, pass without lingering beside the truck and hold the wheel with both hands against turbulence.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: When is it safe to pull back in front of a truck you just passed, and what should your speed do?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.memory_hook: See headlights in rearview, hold speed
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: Return after passing a truck only when its front or headlights can be seen in the rearview mirror, then maintain speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.front: At highway speeds, up to how long can a complete, safe pass around a large truck take?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.expected_back: At highway speed, safely passing a truck can take as long as thirty seconds.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.front: What speed adjustment should you make as you approach or pass someone riding a bicycle?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.expected_back: Slow to a safe speed when approaching or passing a cyclist.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.front: What braking mistake must you avoid right after overtaking a bicyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.expected_back: Avoid abrupt slowing or stopping immediately after passing a bicycle.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.front: When is the only time you should sound your horn close to a bicyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.expected_back: Do not sound the horn close to a cyclist unless needed to avert a crash.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.front: How much lane width are motorcycles and mopeds entitled to use on the road?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.expected_back: Give a motorcycle or moped the use of a complete lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.front: Why shouldn't you pull out in front of a motorcycle just because its turn signal is blinking?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.expected_back: Wait for a motorcycle or moped to actually begin turning rather than relying on its flashing indicator.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.front: Why might a motorcycle or moped change speed or lane position without warning ahead of you?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.expected_back: Be ready for a motorcycle or moped to change speed or lane suddenly to avoid a road hazard.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.front: What minimum following time cushion belongs behind a motorcycle or moped, and when should you add more?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.expected_back: Follow motorcycles or mopeds by at least four seconds and increase the gap in bad weather or road conditions.

sec12-card-sec12-F44.front: How should you position your car and manage your speed while a large truck overtakes you?
sec12-card-sec12-F44.memory_hook: Keep right, hold steady, never speed
sec12-card-sec12-F44.expected_back: When a truck passes, stay toward the far side of your lane, ease speed slightly if helpful and keep it steady without accelerating.

sec12-card-sec12-F45.front: What should you do if a truck starts merging into your lane while you are in its blind spot?
sec12-card-sec12-F45.expected_back: If a truck begins merging while you occupy its blind spot, stay calm, judge position and choose slowing or accelerating to avoid collision, considering a side escape.

sec12-card-sec12-F46.front: How should you place your car and spacing when meeting an oncoming truck on an undivided road?
sec12-card-sec12-F46.expected_back: When meeting an oncoming truck, keep as far to the side as possible and preserve a forward cushion.

sec12-card-sec12-F47.front: How far behind a large truck should you stay so the driver knows you are back there?
sec12-card-sec12-F47.expected_back: Follow far enough back that the truck driver can see the vehicle in the truck's side mirrors.

sec12-card-sec12-F48.front: What does it mean if you cannot see the side mirrors on a truck or bus ahead of you?
sec12-card-sec12-F48.expected_back: If a truck's or bus's side mirrors cannot be seen, its driver cannot see the following vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-F49.front: Why should you leave extra room when stopping behind a large truck on an uphill grade?
sec12-card-sec12-F49.expected_back: Leave extra stopping room behind a truck uphill because it may roll backward.

sec12-card-sec12-F50.front: How must you set your headlights when following behind a truck or any other vehicle after dark?
sec12-card-sec12-F50.expected_back: Dim headlights when following a truck or another vehicle at night.

sec12-card-sec12-F51.front: What minimum time cushion should you hold behind a truck, and how do you measure it?
sec12-card-sec12-F51.expected_back: Keep at least four seconds behind a truck, timing its passage of a fixed object until the front bumper reaches that point.

sec12-card-sec12-F52.front: Why must you hold back instead of passing a turning truck before it finishes the corner?
sec12-card-sec12-F52.expected_back: Do not pass a turning truck until the turn is complete; it may need adjoining space to clear the corner.

sec12-card-sec12-F53.front: Why should you never try to squeeze between the curb and a truck signaling or making a right turn?
sec12-card-sec12-F53.expected_back: Do not squeeze between a right-turning truck and the curb; its driver may be unable to see the vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How should you drive when you spot pilot cars with warning signs and flashing lights escorting an oversized load?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Treat oversized loads like trucks and use extra caution when pilot vehicles with warning signs and lights appear.
