sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: Why might an oversized load cross over a painted lane line ahead of you?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: An oversized load may cross a lane line to avoid roadside obstructions because of its width.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: What should you never do when a truck is lining up to back into a loading dock or bay?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Never cross close behind a truck preparing to reverse into a loading area.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: At sixty-five miles per hour on clear dry pavement, how many feet does a loaded truck need to stop versus a passenger car?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.memory_hook: Six hundred feet versus four hundred
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: On a clear dry road at sixty-five miles per hour, a loaded truck with good tires and adjusted brakes needs at least six hundred feet to stop, compared with four hundred feet for a passenger vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: Why is pulling out or changing lanes right in front of a large vehicle so dangerous?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: Avoid entering or changing lanes immediately in front of a large vehicle because its stopping distance is longer.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: Who are runaway escape ramps on steep downhill highways reserved for?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Escape ramps on long descents are reserved for large vehicles out of control or unable to stop through brake failure.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: Where must you never park or stop along a steep mountain descent?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: Do not park or stop near an escape ramp.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: Which road-sharing rules apply when you drive near transit or tour buses?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: Use the same road-sharing precautions around buses as around trucks.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: What do flashing amber lights on a school bus tell surrounding drivers?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: A school bus flashes amber lights as it prepares to stop.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: Unless separated by a physical highway divider, how far must you stop from a school bus with red flashers and stop arm out, and from which approaches?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: Except from the opposite side of a physically divided highway, stop at least ten feet from a stopped school bus showing red flashers and an extended stop arm, whether following, meeting on its roadway or approaching its intersection.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: Which three things must happen before you move again after stopping for a school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.memory_hook: Lights off, arm in, kids safe
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: Stay stopped for the school bus until its red flashers cease, its arm retracts and the children reach safety.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: What rule applies to oncoming drivers across a physical highway median from a stopped school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: Opposite-direction traffic beyond a physical highway divider need not stop for the school bus but should slow and proceed cautiously.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.front: What three penalties hit your record and wallet for illegally passing a stopped school bus with red lights and arm out?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.expected_back: An unlawful failure to stop for a bus with red flashers and an extended arm carries a sixty-day license suspension, five points and a fine.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.front: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches from any direction using a siren or red or red-and-blue lights?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction with a siren or flashing red or red-and-blue lights, pull parallel to the curb or road edge and stop clear of intersections.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.front: Where should you pull over and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle on a one-way street?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.expected_back: On a one-way road, move to the nearest roadside and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.front: Once an emergency vehicle passes you, what distance and safety check apply as you pull back out?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.expected_back: Resume after the emergency vehicle passes, remain at least five hundred feet behind it and check for another responder.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.front: Whose traffic directions must you obey at an emergency scene?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.expected_back: During emergencies, follow directions from uniformed officers, sheriffs, constables or properly attired responders including fire police.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.front: What lane action is required when approaching an emergency-response area or a marked disabled vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.expected_back: Move into a nonadjacent lane when approaching an emergency-response area or marked disabled vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.front: Can you get cited for a Move Over violation if no police officer is parked at the scene?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.expected_back: Road workers and emergency responders may report Move Over violations even without police present, and police may issue citations from those reports.

sec12-card-sec12-R21.front: What maximum fines does the handbook list for first, second, and third or later Move Over offenses?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.expected_back: The handbook lists maximum Move Over fines of five hundred dollars for a first offense, one thousand for a second and two thousand for a third or later offense.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.front: How many points go onto your Pennsylvania driving record for a Move Over conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.expected_back: A Move Over conviction adds two points to the driver record.

sec12-card-sec12-R23.front: Why should you leave plenty of room behind horse-drawn carriages or buggies?
sec12-card-sec12-R23.expected_back: Leave generous space behind horse-drawn traffic because it may roll back and its driver may have trouble seeing a close follower.

sec12-card-sec12-R24.front: How should you pass horses or horse-drawn buggies and merge back into the lane?
sec12-card-sec12-R24.memory_hook: Easy speed, zero horn, wide return
sec12-card-sec12-R24.expected_back: Pass horses or horse-drawn vehicles without excessive speed or horn use, and leave room before returning right to avoid frightening the animal.

sec12-card-sec12-R25.front: Why should you hang well back when following a working snowplow?
sec12-card-sec12-R25.expected_back: Follow snowplows from a safe distance because their rear visibility is limited and they spread material that can damage nearby vehicles.

sec12-card-sec12-R26.front: Why must you never try to pass a snowplow on either the left or the right?
sec12-card-sec12-R26.expected_back: Do not attempt to pass a snowplow on either side because wing plows can extend beyond it.

sec12-card-sec12-R27.front: How should you respond when another driver cuts you off or drives aggressively?
sec12-card-sec12-R27.expected_back: Do not retaliate against or try to teach a lesson to another driver after a perceived aggressive act.

sec12-card-sec12-R28.front: How should you handle lane position and speed when an aggressive driver wants past you?
sec12-card-sec12-R28.memory_hook: Let pass, never block or race
sec12-card-sec12-R28.expected_back: Let an aggressive driver pass, avoid blocking the passing lane and do not accelerate to challenge the driver.

sec12-card-sec12-R29.front: How should you handle eye contact and rude hand gestures from an angry motorist?
sec12-card-sec12-R29.expected_back: Avoid eye contact and ignore hostile gestures without gesturing back.

sec12-card-sec12-R30.front: What is the safe way to report an aggressive driver to police or nine one one while traveling?
sec12-card-sec12-R30.expected_back: If safely possible with a hands-free device, call police or nine one one about an aggressive driver, or ask a passenger to call.

sec12-card-sec12-R31.front: Where should you drive—and where must you avoid going—if an aggressive driver follows your car?
sec12-card-sec12-R31.expected_back: If pursued by an aggressive driver, go to a police station, store or another place with help and witnesses rather than home.

sec12-card-sec12-R32.front: When choosing between braking or steering to dodge a crash—especially above twenty-five miles per hour—which usually works better?
sec12-card-sec12-R32.expected_back: When choosing braking or steering to avoid a collision, steering is usually preferable if feasible, especially above twenty-five miles per hour

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: How should you hold the steering wheel so you are ready for sudden emergency maneuvers?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Hold the steering wheel with both hands, especially when rapid emergency steering may be needed.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: How does higher road speed affect how much steering input you need to move sideways?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: At higher speeds, less steering movement is needed to shift the vehicle sideways.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: Which two clock-face hand positions and thumb placement does the Pennsylvania handbook recommend?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: The handbook recommends hands at nine and three or eight and four on the wheel, with thumbs along its face rather than inside the rim.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: Even though ten-and-two is still acceptable, what injury risk rises when your hands sit that high?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: The ten-and-two hand position is described as acceptable but increases airbag-related arm and hand injury risk.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: How do your hands move across the wheel during hand-over-hand steering?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Hand-over-hand steering reaches across to grasp the opposite rim and pull across the top repeatedly as needed.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: How do your two hands alternate during push-pull steering?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Push-pull steering alternates one hand pushing upward with the other sliding up and pulling down.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: Besides buckled seat belts and adjusted head restraints, how far should your chest sit from the airbag?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Crash-injury protection includes proper belts, adjusted head restraints and sitting at least ten inches from the airbag.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: How should you find out ahead of time whether your car has conventional brakes or ABS?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: Know from the owner's manual whether the vehicle uses conventional brakes or ABS before an emergency occurs.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: How should you work the brake pedal during an urgent stop in a car without ABS?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: For urgent braking without ABS, repeatedly press and release the pedal rather than slamming hard enough to lock the wheels.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: How do you use the brake pedal for an urgent stop when your car has ABS?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: For urgent braking with ABS, keep firm continuous pedal pressure and do not pump.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: What should you make of grinding noises and slight pedal pulsing during hard ABS braking?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Mechanical noise and mild pedal pulses during ABS braking are not reasons to become alarmed.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: Where should you look and turn the wheel when your rear tires skid sideways on wet or icy pavement?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: On a wet- or ice-road skid, look and steer toward the intended path; turn left if the rear slides left and right if it slides right.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: What secondary slide must you stay ready for right after correcting an initial skid?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Be ready for an opposite skid after a correction and counter it by steering in the new rearward-slide direction.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: Why must you stay off the brake pedal while steering out of a skid?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Do not apply the brakes while correcting a skid because wheel lock can remove steering control.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: How little standing or moving floodwater does it take to make small cars lose control or float?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: Even six inches of floodwater can cause loss of control and float some small vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: What depths of moving floodwater can float many sedans and sweep away most SUVs and pickups?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.memory_hook: Twelve inches cars, two feet trucks
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: Twelve inches of moving water can float many cars, and two feet can move most SUVs and pickups.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: What must you do when you reach a flooded road or a flood closure barricade?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: Do not attempt a flooded road; choose another route and never drive through or around a flood closure barrier.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: What road-surface dangers can muddy floodwater hide underneath, especially after dark?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Floodwater may conceal missing pavement or bridges and can weaken the roadway; darkness makes the hazard harder to see.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: What is your immediate priority if your vehicle stalls and gets stuck in floodwater?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: If stuck in floodwater, leave the vehicle quickly and move to higher ground.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: If your accelerator sticks down, how may you try freeing it while keeping your eyes up—and what must you never do?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: For a stuck accelerator, keep watching the road and try tapping or lifting the pedal with a toe, never reaching down by hand.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: What gear and brake move should you make immediately if tapping fails to free a stuck gas pedal?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: If the accelerator remains stuck, shift immediately to neutral and brake; the engine may race while wheel power is removed.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: Once you slow down under control from a stuck accelerator, what four steps finish the stop safely?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.memory_hook: Pull off, stop, shut engine, hazards
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: After slowing safely from a stuck accelerator, steer off the road, stop, turn off the engine and activate hazards.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: If a stuck accelerator forces an immediate stop while moving, which ignition setting do you use and what changes?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.memory_hook: Switch OFF never LOCK, push harder
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: If a stuck accelerator requires an immediate stop, use ignition OFF rather than LOCK, then brake, expecting greater steering and braking effort.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: What braking capability and pedal changes remain when a split-system brake warning light comes on?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: A split-system brake warning can leave braking on two of four wheels, probably a front and a rear, while increasing pedal travel, effort and stopping distance.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: How should you slow down and where should you head if half of your split brake system fails?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: With partial brake failure, use a lower gear to help slow and pull into a safe roadside place or service station.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: What are your first two moves if the brakes fail completely in an older vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: With sudden brake failure in an older vehicle, select a low gear and look for a place to stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: Why should you pump the brake pedal rapidly when brakes fail in an older vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: For an older vehicle's failed brakes, pumping the pedal quickly may rebuild pressure.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: If pumping fails to bring back hydraulic brakes, how must you apply the parking brake safely?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: If pumping fails, use the parking brake while holding its release so pressure can be eased if the rear wheels lock or skid.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: When an older brakeless car still faces an imminent crash, what last-resort ignition and gear sequence applies?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: If an older vehicle still cannot stop and a crash threatens, use ignition OFF as a last resort, never LOCK, then the lowest gear despite possible transmission damage.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: What must you do—and refuse to do—once you get a car with failed brakes stopped?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: After stopping for brake failure, call for help and do not continue driving.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: What routine upkeep lowers your chance of suffering a highway tire blowout?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: Maintain tires and correct inflation to reduce blowout risk.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: How does a front-tire blowout feel from the driver's seat compared with a rear-tire failure?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: A front-tire blowout may shake the steering wheel and pull the vehicle sideways; rear-tire failure may drop a corner and make the rear wobble.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: How should you handle the wheel and gas pedal the moment a tire blows out?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.memory_hook: Grip firm, ease gas, steer smooth
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: During a blowout, grip the wheel, ease off the accelerator and steer smoothly without abrupt large movements.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: How should you treat the brake pedal during a tire blowout as you work toward the shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: Avoid braking during a blowout; if braking is necessary, use gentle pressure while slowing to a safe off-road stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: When is it okay to keep rolling slowly on a flat tire instead of stopping immediately?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: Continue on a flat tire only as needed to reach a safe place off the road before changing it.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.front: Because jack points and spare setups differ across models, what should you check and keep in the trunk?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.expected_back: Tire-changing steps vary by vehicle, so consult the owner's manual and retain the needed tools.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.front: What kind of surface and location do you need before jacking up a car to change a tire?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.expected_back: For the basic tire change, park on flat ground away from traffic and as far off the roadway as possible.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.front: Before lifting the car with a jack, how do you stop the remaining tires from rolling?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.expected_back: Set the parking brake and chock both the front and back of a remaining good tire.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.front: What trim step comes first if your wheel has a hubcap or lug cover?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.expected_back: If fitted, remove the hubcap or cover carefully before working on the wheel.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.front: When should you crack the lug nuts loose, and how far do you unscrew them at first?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.expected_back: Loosen wheel nuts while the vehicle is still on the ground, without fully removing them.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.front: Where must the jack sit under the car, and roughly how high do you lift the flat tire?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.expected_back: Place the jack on solid ground at the manufacturer's proper frame or suspension point and raise the tire about six inches.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.front: Once the tire is raised off the ground, how do you handle the lug nuts and remove the wheel?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.expected_back: After raising the vehicle, remove and safely store the nuts, then pull the damaged wheel straight off with both hands.

sec13-card-sec13-R18.front: After sliding the spare onto the studs, how should you start and snug the lug nuts?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.expected_back: Fit the spare and hand-thread every nut correctly before using only light wrench pressure.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.front: How do you bring the vehicle down before giving the lug nuts their final tightening?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.expected_back: Lower the vehicle slowly to the ground before final tightening, keeping the jack in place at that step.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.front: Where do you find the proper lug-nut tightening order and torque rating for your vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.expected_back: Use the owner's manual for the correct wheel-nut tightening sequence and torque specification.

sec13-card-sec13-R21.front: What should you do with the flat wheel, jack, wrench, and roadside triangles once the spare is tight?
sec13-card-sec13-R21.expected_back: Stow the jack, wheel, tools and warning equipment securely after changing the tire.

sec13-card-sec13-R22.front: What last check applies to hubcaps or center caps before pulling back onto the road?
sec13-card-sec13-R22.expected_back: Refit wheel covers or center caps as the manual directs and verify they are secure before driving.

sec13-card-sec13-R23.front: If an oncoming car drifts into your lane, what warning and escape side should you use?
sec13-card-sec13-R23.expected_back: For an oncoming vehicle in your lane, sound the horn and try a right-side escape if the other driver does not correct.

sec13-card-sec13-R24.front: Why must you never swerve into the left lane to dodge an oncoming car in your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R24.expected_back: Do not evade a head-on threat by swerving left, because the opposing driver may return to that lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R25.front: If a head-on crash is unavoidable, how should you brake in the final moments?
sec13-card-sec13-R25.expected_back: If a head-on collision cannot be avoided, brake firmly and steadily to reduce impact speed.

sec13-card-sec13-R26.front: What is your immediate pedal and steering move if your right tires drop off the pavement edge?
sec13-card-sec13-R26.expected_back: After the right wheels drop off pavement, ease off the accelerator and avoid abrupt braking or steering.

sec13-card-sec13-R27.front: If a mailbox or guardrail ahead forces you to brake with tires off the road, how do you press the pedal?
sec13-card-sec13-R27.expected_back: If braking is necessary to avoid a shoulder hazard, use gradual controlled pressure rather than locking the wheels.

sec13-card-sec13-R28.front: How should you steer while rolling with two wheels on pavement and two on the shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-R28.expected_back: With two wheels on and two off the road, hold the wheel firmly and steer parallel without scraping the pavement edge.

sec13-card-sec13-R30.front: Once slowed and clear behind, how do you signal and steer your right wheels back onto the road?
sec13-card-sec13-R30.expected_back: Before reentry, check rear traffic and signal left; when clear, ease the right wheels onto pavement and steer gently right to straighten.

sec13-card-sec13-R31.front: After a shoulder drop-off recovery, when should you accelerate back up to traffic speed?
sec13-card-sec13-R31.expected_back: Match traffic speed only after safely regaining the pavement and full control.

sec13-card-sec13-R32.front: How must outside drivers treat a funeral procession, and when is cutting through allowed?
sec13-card-sec13-R32.expected_back: Yield to a funeral procession and avoid cutting through it unless police or an authorized funeral representative directs otherwise.

sec13-card-sec13-R33.front: Which lights and markers identify vehicles traveling in a Pennsylvania funeral procession?
sec13-card-sec13-R33.expected_back: Procession vehicles must show headlights, hazard flashers and a flag or identifying insignia; a purple warning light may also be used.

sec13-card-sec13-R34.front: How may cars inside a funeral procession proceed through red traffic lights or stop signs?
sec13-card-sec13-R34.expected_back: A funeral procession may follow its lead vehicle through a signal after the lead entered on green, or through a stop after the lead fully stopped.

sec13-card-sec13-R35.front: Who outranks even an active funeral procession at intersections and along the road?
sec13-card-sec13-R35.expected_back: Funeral processions must yield to emergency vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: What agency maintains each licensed Pennsylvania motorist's record, and what reports go into it?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: PennDOT keeps a driving record for each licensed Pennsylvania driver, including offense and conviction reports from police and courts.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: At how many accumulated record points does PennDOT start corrective action?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: Certain guilty findings add points, and PennDOT begins corrective action at six or more points.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: What happens the very first time your driving record reaches six or more points?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: The first accumulation of at least six points brings written notice requiring a special written point examination.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: What is required if your record drops below six points and later climbs to six again?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: After dropping below six and reaching at least six again, the driver must attend a Departmental hearing.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: What consequences can follow additional accumulations of six or more points?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: Further accumulations of six or more points can bring additional hearings or suspensions.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: Which two triggers automatically suspend a Pennsylvania driver younger than eighteen?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: A driver younger than eighteen is suspended for reaching six points or being convicted of exceeding the limit by at least twenty-six miles per hour

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: How long are the first and later suspensions for those under-eighteen point or speeding triggers?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: For those under-eighteen triggers, the first suspension is ninety days and later occurrences are one hundred twenty days.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: How many points come off your record for each clean twelve-month stretch, and what keeps it clean?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: Three points are removed after each twelve consecutive months without a point-assigning violation or suspension or revocation.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: How is a future point accumulation treated once your record stays at zero for twelve consecutive months?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: After a record remains at zero for twelve consecutive months, a new accumulation is treated as the first.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: Which impaired, violent, or aggressive driving convictions directly cause suspension or revocation?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: DUI, vehicle-related felony or homicide, reckless driving and highway racing are among convictions causing suspension or revocation.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: Which four evasion, flight, or invalid-driving convictions bring license sanctions?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Fleeing police, driving while suspended or revoked, lights-off identification evasion and hit-and-run are listed sanctionable convictions.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: When does driving without a license trigger a suspension or revocation?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: A second or later unlicensed-driving offense within five years is listed as a suspension or revocation trigger.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: What license suspension follows failing to stop for a school bus with red flashers and stop arm?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: Failure to stop for a school bus with red flashers and an extended arm brings a sixty-day suspension.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: How long is your license suspended for disregarding a railroad crossing gate or barrier?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: Disregarding a rail-crossing gate or barrier brings a thirty-day suspension.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: What does a mailed sanction notice specify, and what items must be returned by that date?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: A sanction notice is mailed with its starting date, and the listed license, permit or camera card must be returned by that date.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: When does a Pennsylvania driving sanction officially take effect?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: A sanction begins on the notice's effective date, regardless of when the license or acknowledgment is surrendered.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Does turning in your license ahead of time make a suspension start earlier?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Early surrender does not begin the sanction early.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: Where and within how many days must a driver file an appeal of a sanction notice?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: A sanction appeal goes to the county Court of Common Pleas Civil Division within thirty days of the notice's mailing.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: What two conditions must you satisfy to restore suspended driving privileges?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: Restoration requires completing the sanction and all applicable restoration requirements.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: How many points normally remain on a restored record, and which two suspensions are exceptions?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: A restored record normally carries five points, except a fifteen-day second-six-point suspension or suspension for not responding to a citation.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: What insurance obligation applies to every registered Pennsylvania vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: Keep liability insurance continuously on a registered vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: What suspensions result from a thirty-one-day insurance lapse or letting an uninsured car be driven?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: An insurance lapse of at least thirty-one days brings a three-month registration suspension; operating or permitting use uninsured also brings three months of driving suspension.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: What two items are required to restore privileges lost for an uninsured vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: Restoring uninsured-vehicle privileges requires proof of current coverage and the restoration fees.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: What core rule governs your behavior during a police traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: At a police traffic stop, follow the officer's directions.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: How and where should you pull over when signaled for a police stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: Signal and stop as close to the right edge as safely possible, parking away from traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: What three vehicle steps should you take right after coming to a stop for police?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: After stopping, turn off the engine and radio and lower the window to communicate.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: What extra step should you take during a nighttime traffic stop before the officer walks up?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: At night, turn the interior light on before the officer approaches.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: How should the driver and passengers manage movements and hands during a traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: Keep movements limited, do not reach for items and keep driver and passenger hands visible.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: What must you tell the officer right away if a firearm is inside the vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: Immediately tell the officer if any firearm is being transported.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: What should you do with your doors and seat belt when pulled over by police?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: Remain inside with doors closed unless asked to exit, and keep the belt fastened until the officer observes it.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: When should you reach for documents, and how should you hand them to the officer?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: Wait for a request before retrieving license, registration or insurance documents; hand over the requested items rather than the wallet.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: How should you handle a traffic citation that you believe is unfair?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: Remain polite and contest a disputed citation through a court hearing rather than arguing at the scene.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: Where can you report a concern about an officer's conduct during a stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: A concern about officer conduct can be raised later with a police-department supervisor.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: What should you do if you are unsure whether a vehicle signaling you to stop is genuine police?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: If uncertain about a stopping vehicle's police identity, acknowledge with hazards and reduced speed while proceeding to the nearest well-lit populated place.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.front: When should you request official identification during a traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.expected_back: Ask for identification if the stopping person is not uniformed or uses an unmarked vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.front: Which flashing light colors identify Pennsylvania police versus a blue-only light?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.expected_back: Police vehicles may display red and blue or red alone when unmarked, with white lights in addition; blue alone does not identify a police officer.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: When should you avoid stopping at a roadside crash scene?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: Do not stop at a crash unless involved or emergency help has not arrived, and do not obstruct responders.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: Where must you stop and position your vehicle if you are involved in a crash?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: If involved in a crash, stop at or near the scene and move off the road if possible.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: Which three crash conditions require calling police, and what must witnesses do if drivers are hurt?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Call police for an injury, death or vehicle requiring a tow; witnesses must seek help if injured drivers cannot call.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: What five pieces of driver, vehicle, and insurance information must be exchanged after a crash?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: Exchange driver names, addresses, phone numbers, registration numbers and insurance-company and policy details.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: Whose names and addresses should you write down besides the other drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: Record names and addresses of other involved people and crash witnesses.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: What steps are required if you damage unattended parked property and cannot find the owner?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: For damage to parked property, stop and seek the owner; if absent, leave a visible note with date, time, name and reachable phone number, and call police.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: What must you file if police do not investigate a crash involving injury, death, or towing?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: If police do not investigate a crash involving injury, death or a tow, submit AA-six hundred within five days.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: At what blood alcohol concentration does a driver twenty-one or older meet the DUI threshold?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: For a driver aged twenty-one or older, a BAC of zero point zero eight or higher constitutes DUI under the handbook's rule.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: Can an adult driver be convicted of DUI with a BAC below zero point zero eight?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: DUI conviction may also occur below that adult BAC threshold when erratic driving supplies evidence of impairment.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: What blood alcohol concentration triggers DUI for a driver younger than twenty-one?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: Drivers younger than twenty-one meet the handbook's DUI threshold at BAC zero point zero two or higher.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: What testing agreement comes automatically with holding a Pennsylvania driver's license?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: Pennsylvania licensure carries implied consent to chemical alcohol or drug testing.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.front: How does refusing a breath or blood test after a DUI arrest affect your license?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.expected_back: Refusing breath or blood testing after a DUI arrest can suspend driving independently of a DUI conviction.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.front: What happens to a first chemical-test refusal suspension if you win a not-guilty verdict on DUI?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.expected_back: A first test refusal can bring a one-year suspension even when the DUI charge ends in a not-guilty result.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.front: Which three factors make Pennsylvania DUI sanctions escalate in severity?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.expected_back: DUI sanctions become more severe with higher BAC, greater crash harm and more convictions.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.front: When is Alcohol Highway Safety School mandatory in Pennsylvania DUI cases?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.expected_back: First or second DUI offenses require alcohol highway safety school at any impairment tier.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.front: What treatment orders and maximum community-service hours can courts impose for DUI at any tier?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.expected_back: Courts may order alcohol screening and treatment for DUI at any tier and may impose up to one hundred fifty community-service hours.

sec14-card-sec14-R17.front: What does an ignition-interlock restricted license generally require regarding vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.expected_back: A restricted-license interlock requirement generally means equipping every vehicle to be operated, or certifying no owned, registered or operated vehicles under PennDOT regulations.

sec14-card-sec14-R18.front: Which diversion program may a first DUI at high or highest impairment still qualify for?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.expected_back: A first DUI offense at high or highest impairment may qualify for Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition.

sec14-card-sec14-R19.front: Which four alcohol actions are illegal for anyone under twenty-one, including inside their car?
sec14-card-sec14-R19.expected_back: People under twenty-one may not buy, consume, possess or transport alcohol, including in the vehicle they drive.

sec14-card-sec14-R20.front: Does police chemical testing of an arrested minor require parental consent, and are parents told?
sec14-card-sec14-R20.expected_back: Underage chemical testing after arrest and detention does not require parental consent, but police notify parents of the arrest.

sec14-card-sec14-R21.front: What follow-up programs may courts order after an underage drinking offense?
sec14-card-sec14-R21.expected_back: Courts may require alcohol evaluation and education, intervention or counseling for underage drinking.

sec14-card-sec14-R22.front: Who can face legal penalties for knowingly and intentionally supplying alcohol to a minor?
sec14-card-sec14-R22.expected_back: Knowingly and intentionally supplying alcohol to a minor can expose an adult, including a parent, to penalties.

sec14-card-sec14-R23.front: What jurisdictions cooperate under the Driver's License Compact, and why?
sec14-card-sec14-R23.expected_back: The Driver's License Compact coordinates member states and the District of Columbia to enforce licensing rules.

sec14-card-sec14-R24.front: What happens to your out-of-state license under the compact's one-license concept when moving?
sec14-card-sec14-R24.expected_back: Under the compact's one-license concept, an out-of-state license is surrendered when applying in another state.

sec14-card-sec14-R25.front: What does the compact's one-record concept maintain in your home state?
sec14-card-sec14-R25.expected_back: The compact's one-record concept keeps a complete record in the home state for resident and nonresident eligibility.

sec14-card-sec14-R26.front: What events do compact jurisdictions report back to a driver's home licensing agency?
sec14-card-sec14-R26.expected_back: Member jurisdictions report out-of-state driver convictions and license suspensions or revocations to the home licensing agency.

sec14-card-sec14-R27.front: How does Pennsylvania treat specified compact offenses committed in another member jurisdiction?
sec14-card-sec14-R27.expected_back: Specified offenses in another member jurisdiction are treated as if committed in Pennsylvania for home-state sanctions.

sec14-card-sec14-R28.front: Which three major violations are examples of specified offenses under the Driver's License Compact?
sec14-card-sec14-R28.expected_back: DUI preventing safe driving, failure to stop and aid after an injury or fatal crash, and a felony using a vehicle are among the compact's specified offenses.

sec14-card-sec14-R29.front: What happens to your Pennsylvania license if you ignore an out-of-state traffic citation?
sec14-card-sec14-R29.expected_back: Ignoring an out-of-state citation suspends Pennsylvania driving indefinitely until the required response is made to the cited location.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: Within how many days must you report a name or address change, including moving out of state, to PennDOT?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: Notify PennDOT within fifteen days after a name or address change, including a move out of state.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: Does Pennsylvania issue driver-license products to nonresidents?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: Pennsylvania does not issue driver-license products to nonresidents.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: Which PennDOT form requests a non-commercial license name change, correction, or replacement?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: Use Form DL-eighty to request a non-commercial license name change, correction or replacement.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: What must you carry alongside your plastic license after receiving a license update card?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: Carry the license update card with the driver license.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: Who must wear seat belts in the front seats of cars, light trucks, and motorhomes?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: Drivers and front-seat passengers in cars, light trucks and motorhomes must wear seat belts.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: Which passenger age group must buckle up in every seating position, front or rear?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: Passengers aged eight through seventeen must wear belts in every seating position.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: How do working seat belts limit passenger count for a driver younger than eighteen?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: A driver under eighteen may not carry more passengers than the available seat belts can accommodate.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: What happens to an unrestrained occupant's body the instant a crashing vehicle stops?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: During a crash, an unrestrained body continues moving after the vehicle stops.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: How do seat belts protect your body from rapid deceleration during a collision?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: Belts spread rapid-deceleration force over the chest, hips and shoulders instead of hard vehicle surfaces.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: Do factory airbags eliminate the need to buckle your seat belt?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: Wear a seat belt even when the vehicle has airbags.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: Where do seat belts help keep vehicle occupants during a violent crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: Belts help keep occupants inside the vehicle during a crash.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: How must a child younger than two ride, and when may they outgrow that orientation?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: A child under two rides rear-facing until outgrowing the seat manufacturer's maximum height and weight limits.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: Where must a rear-facing child safety seat never be installed?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: Never place a rear-facing child seat in front of an airbag.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: How should required child seats or boosters for children under eight be installed and fitted?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: For required child seats or boosters under age eight, follow the vehicle and seat instructions to secure the seat tightly and the child snugly.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: May you leave a child or pet alone inside a parked car if the windows are cracked open?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: Never leave a child or pet alone inside a vehicle, even with partly open windows.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: What rule applies to letting children play inside an unattended parked vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: Do not let children play in an unattended vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: What two simple habits help prevent accidentally forgetting a quiet child in the rear seat?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.expected_back: Place a needed item in the rear seat or move a reminder toy forward when placing a child in the seat to avoid forgetting the child.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: Why are bulky winter coats risky inside a child-seat harness, and how must straps fit?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: Bulky winter coats can compress in a crash and leave excessive slack, so the child-seat harness must be snug against the body.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: What restraint and anchoring methods are required for children younger than four in any seat?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: Children under four require a federally approved child restraint secured by a seat belt or LATCH, regardless of seating position.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.front: What restraint setup is required for children aged four up to under eight in any seat?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.expected_back: Children from four to under eight require an approved booster secured using lap and shoulder belts wherever seated.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.front: What restraint rule covers ages eight to under eighteen, and who carries legal responsibility?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.expected_back: Children from eight to under eighteen require a belt wherever seated, and the driver is responsible for securing minors properly.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.front: Where should the lap belt and shoulder strap rest across your body?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.expected_back: Wear the lap belt snugly across the hips and the shoulder strap across the chest away from the neck.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.front: How far back from the steering wheel and airbag should a driver sit?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.expected_back: Sit as far from the airbag as practical while maintaining access to pedals and controls, at least ten inches from the steering wheel.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.front: Which clock hand positions and thumb placement does the handbook recommend on the steering wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.expected_back: Hold the wheel at nine and three or eight and four, with thumbs on the top or outer rim rather than inside.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.front: Up through what age does the handbook recommend that children ride in the rear seat?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.expected_back: The handbook recommends rear-seat travel for children twelve and younger.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.front: Why do lap and shoulder belts stay necessary in vehicles equipped with airbags?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.expected_back: Airbags are supplemental restraints, so lap and shoulder belts remain necessary.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.front: What testing accommodations does PennDOT provide for applicants with hearing impairments?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.expected_back: PennDOT describes accessible testing centers and sign-language interpreter assistance for applicants with hearing impairments.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.front: What should applicants requesting sign-language assistance specify in advance?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.expected_back: Applicants needing sign-language assistance should state their preferred form, such as ASL, PSE, SEE or oral interpretation.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: What testing option can applicants who have difficulty reading request at PennDOT?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: Voice knowledge tests are available on request for applicants who have difficulty reading.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: What two conditions must both be met to park legally in a reserved disability space?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: Disability parking requires an authorized disability or disabled-veteran plate or placard and use of the vehicle by or to transport the eligible beneficiary.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: What can happen to a vehicle parked unlawfully in a reserved disability space?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: An unlawfully parked vehicle in a disability space may be towed, with towing costs required to reclaim it.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: Where is discarding trash or waste from a vehicle prohibited?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: Do not discard waste from a vehicle onto a highway, unconsenting public or private property, or state waters.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: Who can be fined if a passenger throws trash out of a moving car?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: A driver may be fined for vehicle-occupant littering as well as the driver's own conduct.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: How often does a Pennsylvania vehicle need an authorized safety inspection, and what marks the due date?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: A vehicle needs an authorized safety inspection every twelve months, with the sticker showing the next due date.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: How early before expiration may you complete your vehicle's next safety inspection?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: Safety inspection may be completed up to ninety days before expiration.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: How many days may an officer give you to repair faulty vehicle equipment and avoid a citation?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: An officer noticing faulty equipment may require repair within five days to avoid a citation.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: What check and minimum side clearance are required before overtaking a bicyclist?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: Before passing a bicycle, check for oncoming traffic and maintain at least four feet of clearance.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.front: May you cross a double solid yellow centerline to give a cyclist four feet of passing space?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.expected_back: If necessary and safe to preserve four feet of bicycle clearance, a driver may cross a double yellow centerline.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.front: When is a slower cyclist's normal keep-right rule waived on a roadway?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.expected_back: A slower cyclist normally keeps right unless turning left, but this keep-right rule is waived where each direction has only one lane.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.front: Why may a cyclist ride in any part of a single travel lane?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.expected_back: With one travel lane, a cyclist may use any portion to avoid hazards and stay clear of parked cars.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.front: What turning mistake must you avoid near a cyclist riding straight on the road or shoulder?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.expected_back: Do not turn across the path of a cyclist continuing straight on the road or shoulder.

sec15-card-sec15-R14.front: What legal consequence can follow forcing a bicyclist off the roadway?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.expected_back: Forcing a cyclist off the road can lead to criminal charges.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.front: How do traffic laws and minimum-speed rules apply to bicyclists?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.expected_back: Cyclists must follow traffic laws but may travel below a posted minimum without an impeding-traffic citation.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.front: Must bicyclists ride on a paved shoulder or berm when one exists?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.expected_back: Cyclists may ride on a shoulder or berm but are not required to use it.

sec15-card-sec15-R17.front: What is prohibited at a hazardous-road closure sign or traffic-control barrier?
sec15-card-sec15-R17.expected_back: Do not drive through or around a hazardous-road closure sign or traffic-control device.

sec15-card-sec15-R18.front: What points and maximum fine apply for driving past a hazardous-road closure?
sec15-card-sec15-R18.expected_back: A hazardous-road-closure conviction adds two points and can bring a fine up to two hundred fifty dollars.

sec15-card-sec15-R19.front: How do penalties jump if bypassing a road closure triggers an emergency rescue response?
sec15-card-sec15-R19.expected_back: If bypassing a closure brings an emergency response, the fine can reach five hundred dollars and the driver is liable for response costs.

sec15-card-sec15-R20.front: What mirror checks and hand choice should precede opening a parked car's street-side door?
sec15-card-sec15-R20.expected_back: Before opening a door, check the rearview and side mirrors, then use the hand farther from the door.

sec15-card-sec15-R21.front: What two safety benefits does the Dutch Reach technique create when exiting a parked car?
sec15-card-sec15-R21.expected_back: The Dutch Reach turns the body toward approaching cyclists and helps prevent the door opening too fast.

sec15-card-sec15-R22.front: How much clearance should cyclists keep beside parked cars to stay out of the door zone?
sec15-card-sec15-R22.expected_back: Cyclists should stay at least three feet from parked cars, with or without bike lanes, to avoid opening doors.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.front: Which toxic gas do gasoline-powered vehicles emit from their exhaust pipe?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.expected_back: Gasoline-powered vehicles release carbon monoxide through the exhaust pipe.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.front: Why is carbon monoxide so dangerous to detect with your senses?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.expected_back: Carbon monoxide is deadly and has no detectable smell.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.front: What sleepy state behind the wheel can warn of carbon monoxide poisoning?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.expected_back: Drowsiness inside a vehicle can be a warning of carbon monoxide poisoning.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.front: Which two energy-draining body sensations appear on the handbook's carbon monoxide symptom list?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.expected_back: The handbook includes fatigue or weakness among carbon monoxide exposure symptoms.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.front: Which lightheaded, room-spinning sensation is listed as a carbon monoxide symptom?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.expected_back: Dizziness appears in the handbook's carbon monoxide symptom list.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.front: What painful head symptom is a listed indicator of carbon monoxide exposure?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.expected_back: Headache is a listed possible sign of carbon monoxide exposure.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.front: Which two stomach-related reactions can indicate carbon monoxide exposure inside a vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.expected_back: Nausea or vomiting can indicate carbon monoxide exposure.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.front: What change in heart rhythm appears among the handbook's carbon monoxide exposure symptoms?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.expected_back: A rapid heart rate is included among the handbook's exposure symptoms.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.front: What change in your breathing pattern is included among carbon monoxide symptoms?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.expected_back: Irregular breathing is included among the handbook's carbon monoxide symptoms.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.front: Which two mental-clarity warning states can signal carbon monoxide exposure?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.expected_back: Confusion or disorientation can be a sign of carbon monoxide exposure.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.front: Which airway irritation reflex is included on the handbook's carbon monoxide warning list?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.expected_back: Coughing is included in the handbook's carbon monoxide exposure warning list.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.front: What upper-body pain symptom appears on the handbook's carbon monoxide exposure list?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.expected_back: Chest pain is among the handbook's listed exposure symptoms.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.front: Which underside vehicle parts should be inspected and maintained regularly to prevent carbon monoxide leaks?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.expected_back: Inspect and maintain the exhaust system and mufflers regularly to help prevent vehicle carbon monoxide poisoning.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.front: What should you do right away if you notice exhaust holes or defects?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.expected_back: Have an automotive professional inspect known exhaust holes or other defects immediately.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.front: What precaution is critical when parking a keyless-ignition vehicle inside an attached garage?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.expected_back: Always turn a keyless vehicle fully off when leaving it in an attached garage.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.front: What exterior check must you perform on snowy days to prevent cabin exhaust buildup?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.expected_back: On snowy days, inspect the tailpipe and remove blocking snow or ice.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.front: What portable device does the handbook suggest adding inside your vehicle for extra protection?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.expected_back: Consider a battery-powered carbon monoxide detector for the vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.front: When each year should you test or replace batteries in a carbon monoxide detector?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.expected_back: Check or replace detector batteries when clocks change in spring and fall each year.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.front: What must you do with the vehicle right away if carbon monoxide poisoning is suspected?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.expected_back: If carbon monoxide poisoning is suspected in the vehicle, leave it immediately.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.front: What environment do you need immediately when vehicle carbon monoxide poisoning is suspected?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.expected_back: Get fresh air immediately when vehicle carbon monoxide poisoning is suspected.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.front: What medical follow-up is required right away for suspected carbon monoxide poisoning?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.expected_back: Seek emergency medical attention right away for suspected carbon monoxide poisoning.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: What three driver shortcomings does Pennsylvania highlight as common contributors to traffic crashes?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Poor vehicle understanding, inattention and poor decisions can contribute to crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: How many surrounding space areas must you manage around your vehicle, and where should you keep a buffer?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Manage six surrounding space areas and keep a cushion on every side of the vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: On dry asphalt, how many seconds of following distance give enough space to steer or brake past a highway hazard?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: On dry pavement, a four-second following gap provides room to steer or brake around a highway hazard.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: What happens to your crash-avoidance options if you follow too closely and the lead vehicle suddenly slows or stops?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Following too closely can leave no way to avoid a crash if the leading vehicle suddenly slows or stops.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: How does keeping a safe forward following gap protect you from being struck from behind?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: A safe following gap allows a response without a panic stop that could trigger a rear-end collision.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: How do you measure your following time using a fixed roadside object, and what count means you are too close?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Measure the gap by timing from the leading vehicle's rear bumper passing a fixed point until your vehicle reaches it; less than four seconds is too close.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Why must you stretch your following gap beyond four seconds on wet, slippery, or unpaved surfaces?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Increase the following gap on wet, slippery or unpaved roads because stopping takes longer.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: How should you adjust your forward space when a vehicle behind you wants to pass?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Leave a larger forward gap when a driver behind wants to pass, so that driver has room to return ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: Why should you drop farther back behind a driver whose rearward view is blocked?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Increase the gap behind a driver whose rearward view is blocked, because that driver may slow without seeing you.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: Why do you need extra following distance behind a large truck or bus that blocks your view ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Leave extra room behind a large vehicle that blocks the view of the road ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: How should you adjust following space behind a heavily loaded vehicle or one pulling a trailer?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Increase the gap behind a heavily loaded vehicle or one towing a trailer.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: How should your following cushion change when approaching slow-moving road users, including bicycles?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Allow extra following room when approaching slow vehicles, including bicycles.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: Why must you keep extra room behind school buses, transit buses, taxis, and hazardous-material trucks?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Leave additional room behind school buses, taxis, other buses and hazardous-material trucks because they stop at rail crossings or unexpectedly.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Why should you open a larger following space on downhill grades, especially at high speeds?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Increase following space downhill, where slowing is harder, especially at high speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: Why must you stop with extra space behind the vehicle ahead when waiting on an uphill slope?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: When stopped uphill, leave room for the vehicle ahead to roll backward as traffic starts.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: What safety advantage does keeping open space beside your vehicle give you in traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Side space provides an escape route if another vehicle abruptly enters your lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: Why should you avoid driving directly alongside other vehicles on multilane highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Avoid traveling alongside other vehicles on multilane roads, where views and escape routes are blocked and blind spots are likely.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: How much room should you keep between your car and oncoming traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Keep as much separation as possible from oncoming vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: How should you make room for vehicles entering a highway from an on-ramp when conditions allow?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: Make room for highway entrants by signaling and moving to an inside lane only if safe.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: Which three sudden curbside hazards require keeping extra side space next to parked vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Leave space beside parked vehicles for opening doors, emerging people or vehicles pulling out.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: How wide must a usable side escape path be, and how do you compensate if neither side offers one?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: If neither side offers an escape path at least eight feet wide, increase the forward following gap.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: Where do you normally steer inside a lane, and how do you adjust when parked cars line your right and oncoming cars approach left?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Normally drive near lane center; with parked cars on the right and oncoming traffic on the left, slow and choose a middle course.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: What two speed and signaling habits help you preserve a safe cushion behind your vehicle before turning?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Help preserve rear space by holding a steady speed and signaling before slowing for a turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: When a driver tailgates you on a multilane road, what lane choice solves the problem first?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: If someone tailgates, move into the right lane when possible.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: If there is no right lane to move into, how should you encourage a tailgater to pass?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: With no right lane, wait for a clear road ahead, then gently tap the brakes to reduce speed gradually and encourage a tailgater to pass.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: What should you look for beside your vehicle before slowing down or stopping?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Look for a side escape route before slowing or stopping.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: What two details should you track in rear-quarter traffic, and how must you verify blind spots before changing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: Monitor rear-quarter traffic speed and distance, and turn your head to check those blind spots before changing lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: How does the Pennsylvania driver's manual define a blind spot?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: A blind spot is an area the driver cannot see without moving the head.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: Which position near another vehicle puts you in its blind spot, and what two speed choices move you clear?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: Avoid lingering beside and slightly behind another vehicle; accelerate or fall back to leave its blind spot.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: While overtaking another vehicle, how should you handle time spent in that driver's blind spot?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: When passing, clear the other driver's blind spot as quickly as safety permits.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: How many seconds ahead — and roughly how far in city versus highway driving — should you search for trouble?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: Look for problems twelve to fifteen seconds ahead, about a city block or a quarter mile at highway speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: Where should your eyes roam as you drive instead of fixing only on the middle of your lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: Scan the whole road and its sides instead of staring only at the center.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: Which four traffic and sign clues should you actively watch for when scanning down the road?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: Scan ahead for slower entrants, stopped turning vehicles, hazard warnings and destination signs.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: Which three roadside junctions require extra side-to-side scanning because traffic streams converge?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: Check the sides wherever traffic streams meet, including intersections, driveways and highway access points.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: Why must you look left, right, and left again before pulling into an intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: At an intersection, look left, right and left again before pulling out because left-side traffic is closer and a later check may reveal missed traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.front: After you begin entering an intersection, why should you check both sides one more time?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.expected_back: After entering an intersection, check both sides again rather than assuming other traffic will stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.front: How should you proceed at an intersection when shrubs, buildings, or parked vehicles hide cross-street traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.expected_back: If buildings, shrubs or parked vehicles block the cross-street view, edge forward slowly until the view clears.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.front: Besides routine mirror sweeps, before which two maneuvers is checking rear traffic especially important?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.expected_back: Check rear traffic frequently, especially before changing lanes or reversing.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.front: How does Pennsylvania treat entering a highway from a ramp or pulling onto a road from a curb or shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.expected_back: Entering a highway from a ramp or joining the road from a curb or shoulder counts as a lane change.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.front: Before shifting lanes, what signal, mirror, and overtaking checks must you complete?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.expected_back: Before a lane change, signal, check rear and side mirrors and make sure no vehicle is about to pass.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.front: Along with mirrors or blind-spot sensors, what physical check is still required before moving lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F41.expected_back: Use quick shoulder checks as well as mirrors or sensors to check blind spots before moving lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F42.front: How long at most should a blind-spot shoulder check take your eyes away from the road ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-F42.expected_back: A blind-spot check should not take the eyes off the road ahead for more than one second.

sec08-card-sec08-F43.front: On a road with three or more lanes, why must you scan across every lane before moving into an open gap?
sec08-card-sec08-F43.expected_back: On roads with three or more lanes, check every lane before changing because another driver may target the same gap.

sec08-card-sec08-F44.front: Before climbing into your vehicle to back up, what check should you make behind the rear bumper?
sec08-card-sec08-F44.expected_back: Before getting into the vehicle to reverse, inspect behind it for children or small objects.

sec08-card-sec08-F45.front: Before backing up, how should you position your view rather than trusting only mirrors or backup sensors?
sec08-card-sec08-F45.expected_back: Before backing, turn to look through the rear window rather than depending only on mirrors or sensors.

sec08-card-sec08-F46.front: Which four factors must guide your speed choice since no single speed stays safe all the time?
sec08-card-sec08-F46.expected_back: Choose speed using the posted limit, road condition, visibility and traffic flow because no speed is always safe.

sec08-card-sec08-F47.front: What responsibility do you have toward nearby drivers whenever you plan to change speed?
sec08-card-sec08-F47.expected_back: Communicate planned speed changes to other drivers.

sec08-card-sec08-F48.front: What driving conditions does a posted maximum speed sign assume?
sec08-card-sec08-F48.expected_back: A posted maximum assumes ideal road, traffic and weather conditions.

sec08-card-sec08-F49.front: What is Pennsylvania's highest posted speed limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F49.expected_back: Pennsylvania's maximum posted speed limit is seventy miles per hour

sec08-card-sec08-F50.front: Where along an interstate highway does Pennsylvania post maximum-speed signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F50.expected_back: Interstate maximum-speed signs are posted after each interchange.

sec08-card-sec08-F51.front: Approximately how often do maximum-speed signs appear along non-interstate Pennsylvania highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F51.expected_back: On other highways, maximum-speed signs appear at approximately half-mile intervals.

sec08-card-sec08-F52.front: What is Pennsylvania's school-zone speed limit when warning lights flash or during posted hours?
sec08-card-sec08-F52.expected_back: School-zone speed is limited to fifteen miles per hour while warning lights flash or during the signed times.

sec08-card-sec08-F53.front: How must you adjust speed in wet, slick, or low-visibility conditions — and can police ticket you below the posted limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F53.expected_back: Drive below the posted limit in wet, slippery, poorly visible or otherwise less-than-ideal conditions; a ticket is possible even below the limit.

sec08-card-sec08-F54.front: Which two aggressive pedal habits should you skip for economical driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F54.expected_back: For economical driving, avoid rapid starts and hard braking.

sec08-card-sec08-F55.front: Why can avoiding trips during the hottest hours of the day help fuel mileage?
sec08-card-sec08-F55.expected_back: Avoiding the hottest part of the day can improve mileage because cooler, denser air can help power and efficiency.

sec08-card-sec08-F56.front: Why should you consult your dealer when the dashboard onboard-diagnostics lamp turns on?
sec08-card-sec08-F56.expected_back: If the onboard-diagnostics lamp comes on, ask the dealer because fuel economy may be falling and emissions may be rising.

sec08-card-sec08-F57.front: Which three engine and climate functions does a vehicle's ECO button adjust to boost efficiency?
sec08-card-sec08-F57.expected_back: Use an available ECO setting to smooth throttle inputs, optimize shifting and reduce air-conditioning load on the engine.

sec08-card-sec08-F58.front: What does the Pennsylvania manual advise about idling — and which gears reduce engine load if you must wait running?
sec08-card-sec08-F58.expected_back: Avoid unnecessary idling; when idling is needed, the handbook advises neutral or park to reduce engine load.

sec08-card-sec08-F59.front: Which five travel or trip-planning habits cut total driving miles, fuel burn, and travel costs?
sec08-card-sec08-F59.expected_back: Reduce driving through transit, cycling, walking, carpooling or combined errands to save travel costs and fuel.

sec08-card-sec08-F60.front: Alongside reduced visibility, what glare and driver-condition risks grow more common after dark?
sec08-card-sec08-F60.expected_back: Night driving reduces vision and can expose the driver to headlight glare and more tired or impaired road users.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: Which three visual abilities drop in dim light and make unexpected walkers or cyclists harder to notice?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Low light reduces distance judgment, color recognition and side vision, making unexpected road users harder to notice.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: What two-sided visibility job do your headlights perform on the road?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Headlights help the driver see and help others see the vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: How frequently at minimum does Pennsylvania recommend cleaning your headlights?

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: When should you turn on headlights during gloomy daylight or against gray roadside backgrounds?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Use headlights when poor light or blending into gray surroundings makes the vehicle hard to see.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: During storms like rain, snow, sleet, or hail — plus fog, smoke, or smog — what must be on and which beam belongs?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Use headlights in rain, snow, sleet, hail, fog, smoke or smog, and use low beams in bad weather.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: At what forward visibility distance for spotting people or vehicles does Pennsylvania require headlights?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Headlights are required when pedestrians or vehicles cannot be seen one thousand feet ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: Between which two daily sun events must your headlights remain on in Pennsylvania?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Headlights must be on between sunset and sunrise.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: What headlight rule applies whenever you travel through a Pennsylvania work zone?

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: What does Pennsylvania law require whenever weather forces continuous or intermittent windshield-wiper use?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Weather-related continuous or intermittent windshield-wiper use requires headlights.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Why aren't daytime running lamps legal substitutes when headlights are required, and what rear lights must glow?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Daytime running lamps are insufficient when headlights are required, and the taillights must also be illuminated.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: What starting fine and total cost with fees does the manual note for Pennsylvania headlight violations?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: The handbook lists headlight-use fines starting at twenty-five dollars and approaching one hundred dollars with associated costs.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: Within what distance of an oncoming vehicle — or behind a vehicle ahead — must you switch to low beams at night?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: At night, dim to low beams on noticing oncoming traffic; the law requires low beams within five hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle or three hundred feet behind another vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.front: Where should you look if an oncoming driver leaves high beams on despite a few brief reminder flashes?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.expected_back: If oncoming high beams persist after a few brief flashes, look toward the road's right side until the vehicle passes.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.front: How should you treat your high-beam switch if another driver refuses to dim glaring headlights?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.expected_back: Do not keep high beams on to retaliate against another driver.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.front: What adjustment tames uncomfortable glare from bright headlights directly behind your vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.expected_back: Switch the inside mirror to its night setting if following headlights create uncomfortable glare.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.front: What rule links your nighttime travel speed to the stretch of road lit by your headlights?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.expected_back: Do not drive faster than a speed that allows stopping within the road illuminated by the headlights.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.front: Roughly how far ahead do standard low-beam headlights illuminate the road?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.expected_back: Low beams illuminate about two hundred fifty feet ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.front: At fifty-five miles per hour on dry pavement, how does total stopping distance compare to two hundred fifty feet?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.expected_back: At fifty-five miles per hour, stopping requires more than two hundred fifty feet even on dry pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.front: To avoid outrunning your headlights on a dark road at night, what top speed does the Pennsylvania manual advise?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.expected_back: To avoid outrunning headlight visibility on a dark road at night, the handbook advises no more than forty-five miles per hour

sec08-card-sec08-R20.front: How should you adjust speed over poor pavement and when taking slippery curves or turns?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.expected_back: Reduce speed on poor road surfaces and take slippery turns or curves more slowly.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.front: During which minutes of a rainfall does pavement often turn most slippery?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.expected_back: Pavement may be especially slippery during the first ten to fifteen minutes of rain.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.front: What substance does rain lift to the top of asphalt, and how does hot weather affect that hazard?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.expected_back: Rain can bring asphalt oil to the surface, and hot weather makes that slippery-road problem worse.

sec08-card-sec08-R23.front: In cold, wet conditions, how do tree-shaded or hillside-shaded spots compare with sunlit pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.expected_back: In cold wet weather, shaded roads can freeze sooner and dry later.

sec08-card-sec08-R24.front: What happens to your tires when your vehicle begins hydroplaning?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.expected_back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose road grip and ride on a film of water.

sec08-card-sec08-R25.front: At how low a speed and in what water depth can hydroplaning begin?
sec08-card-sec08-R25.expected_back: Hydroplaning can occur at only thirty-five miles per hour in water one tenth of an inch deep.
