sec08-card-sec08-R26.front: What tire condition raises hydroplaning danger, and what driver adjustment lowers it?
sec08-card-sec08-R26.expected_back: Worn tires worsen hydroplaning risk, while slower driving reduces it.

sec08-card-sec08-R27.front: If your tires start hydroplaning, what should you do with the wheel and gas pedal — and what must you avoid?
sec08-card-sec08-R27.expected_back: When hydroplaning, keep both hands on the wheel and slowly release the accelerator; avoid hard braking or sudden turns.

sec08-card-sec08-R28.front: While hydroplaning, how should you steer to stay on the road and how should you brake if forced to?
sec08-card-sec08-R28.expected_back: While hydroplaning, steer slowly only as needed to remain on the road and brake gently if braking is necessary.

sec08-card-sec08-R29.front: How do snow and ice affect road grip and your two main vehicle controls?
sec08-card-sec08-R29.expected_back: Snow and ice reduce traction and seriously affect steering and braking.

sec08-card-sec08-R30.front: Why does rain or sleet near thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit create pavement slicker than dry, solid ice?
sec08-card-sec08-R30.expected_back: Near thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit, rain or sleet can put water over ice, creating a surface more slippery than ice alone.

sec08-card-sec08-R31.front: What combination of road sheen and tire spray warns you that black ice may coat the lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R31.expected_back: A wet-looking road with no tire spray from other vehicles may indicate black ice.

sec08-card-sec08-R32.front: What pre-trip winter cleanup does PennDOT urge before driving after snowfall or freezing rain?
sec08-card-sec08-R32.expected_back: PennDOT urges clearing all snow and ice off the vehicle before travel.

sec08-card-sec08-R34.front: How much should you reduce your speed when driving on packed snow?
sec08-card-sec08-R34.expected_back: On packed snow, reduce speed by half.

sec08-card-sec08-R35.front: What pace should you drop down to when driving on ice?
sec08-card-sec08-R35.expected_back: On ice, reduce speed to a crawl.

sec08-card-sec08-R36.front: About how many times your normal following space should you leave on snow-covered or icy roads?
sec08-card-sec08-R36.expected_back: On snow- or ice-covered roads, leave about ten times the normal following space.

sec08-card-sec08-R37.front: Why must you never engage cruise control on slippery pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-R37.expected_back: Do not use cruise control on slippery roads because continued power can maintain wheelspin.

sec08-card-sec08-R38.front: How can smart speed pacing lower crash risk near slippery shaded patches or frosty bridges?
sec08-card-sec08-R38.expected_back: Adjust speed to avoid meeting other vehicles at slippery shaded sections or frosty bridges.

sec08-card-sec08-R39.front: How should you approach a red signal on icy or packed-snow roads so you preserve traction?
sec08-card-sec08-R39.expected_back: On icy or packed-snow roads, coast toward an intersection to reach it after green appears and the vehicles ahead begin moving.

sec08-card-sec08-R40.front: Why must you leave a generous gap before starting up a wintry hill behind another vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R40.expected_back: On a wintry uphill, leave enough distance to avoid slowing or stopping behind the leading vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-R41.front: What gear choice before cresting a wintry downhill helps hold your vehicle under control?
sec08-card-sec08-R41.expected_back: Select a lower gear before descending a wintry hill for better control.

sec08-card-sec08-R42.front: What should you do before leaving if fog outside is so dense that you cannot see?
sec08-card-sec08-R42.expected_back: Do not begin a trip when fog is so dense that you cannot see.

sec08-card-sec08-R43.front: Where should you pull over and wait if blinding fog closes in after your trip is underway?
sec08-card-sec08-R43.expected_back: If dense fog catches you, pull completely off the road, preferably into a parking lot, and wait for it to clear.

sec08-card-sec08-R44.front: While parked off-road waiting for dense fog to clear, what two safety items must remain engaged?
sec08-card-sec08-R44.expected_back: While parked waiting out fog, keep the seat belt fastened and hazard lamps on.

sec08-card-sec08-R45.front: How slow should you drive in fog, and why must you watch your speedometer closely?
sec08-card-sec08-R45.expected_back: In fog, slow enough to stop within visible distance and check the speedometer to avoid unrecognized acceleration.

sec08-card-sec08-R46.front: Which lights should you use in daytime or nighttime fog — and why are high beams the wrong choice?
sec08-card-sec08-R46.expected_back: In fog during day or night, use low beams and available fog lamps rather than high beams, which reflect glare back toward the driver.

sec08-card-sec08-R47.front: Which four glass and body panels must you clear before snowy travel so neither your view nor trailing windshields get blocked?
sec08-card-sec08-R47.expected_back: Before snowy travel, clear the windows, hood, trunk and roof so snow does not block your view or the following driver's windshield.

sec08-card-sec08-R48.front: Which three sets of exterior lights must you brush free of snow, ice, and road grime?
sec08-card-sec08-R48.expected_back: Clear snow, ice and dirt from headlights, taillights and direction indicators.

sec08-card-sec08-R49.front: Why should you let your engine warm before driving off in snowy, icy conditions?
sec08-card-sec08-R49.expected_back: Before snowy driving, let the engine warm so the defroster can warm the windshield and melt remaining ice.

sec08-card-sec08-R50.front: What wiper habit and reservoir fluid rule keep your windshield clean during snowy drives?
sec08-card-sec08-R50.expected_back: In snow, use the wipers and keep the washer reservoir full of fluid that will not freeze.

sec08-card-sec08-R51.front: How do you prevent steamed-up windows in cold weather, and what guide explains your car's exact controls?
sec08-card-sec08-R51.expected_back: Keep the defroster on for steamed windows and follow the owner's manual for the vehicle's settings.

sec08-card-sec08-R52.front: Why should you switch on low-beam headlights during snowy weather even in the middle of the day?
sec08-card-sec08-R52.expected_back: Use low beams in snowy conditions even in daylight to make the vehicle visible.

sec08-card-sec08-R53.front: How quickly can a snow squall strike dry pavement, and what twin visibility and surface dangers appear?
sec08-card-sec08-R53.expected_back: A snow squall can turn clear, dry conditions into near-zero visibility and a slick road within seconds.

sec08-card-sec08-R54.front: Which two forecast and roadside tools help you spot snow-squall hazards early?
sec08-card-sec08-R54.expected_back: Monitor weather forecasts and transportation message signs for snow-squall hazards.

sec08-card-sec08-R55.front: How should you adjust trip timing or routing around snow squalls, and which roads pose the highest danger?
sec08-card-sec08-R55.expected_back: Change travel time, route or both to avoid snow squalls, particularly high-speed interstate exposure.

sec08-card-sec08-R56.front: What action should you take if a snow squall is approaching or reported nearby?
sec08-card-sec08-R56.expected_back: If a squall is approaching or known to be nearby, leave the roadway and wait for it to pass.

sec08-card-sec08-R57.front: If a snow squall overtakes you on the road, how should you handle speed, hazard lights, and the brake pedal?
sec08-card-sec08-R57.expected_back: If caught in a snow squall, slow gradually, activate hazard lights and avoid slamming the brakes.

sec08-card-sec08-R58.front: After a collision during a snow squall, where should you stay whenever possible?
sec08-card-sec08-R58.expected_back: After a collision in a snow squall, remain in the vehicle whenever possible.

sec08-card-sec08-R59.front: What trip decision does an active snow-squall warning along your route call for?
sec08-card-sec08-R59.expected_back: A snow-squall warning for the travel route calls for delaying or altering travel plans.

sec08-card-sec08-R60.front: When rain or snow requires continuous or intermittent wipers, which front and rear lights must be on instead of daytime running lamps?
sec08-card-sec08-R60.expected_back: When weather requires continuous or intermittent wipers, use headlights and illuminated taillights rather than daytime running lamps alone.

sec08-card-sec08-R61.front: What base fine and approximate total with fees apply to a Pennsylvania wiper-and-headlight violation?
sec08-card-sec08-R61.expected_back: The handbook lists a possible twenty-five-dollar wiper-and-headlight violation fine, with fees bringing the total toward one hundred dollars.

sec08-card-sec08-R62.front: How should you match surrounding traffic speed without breaking Pennsylvania speed law?
sec08-card-sec08-R62.expected_back: Match traffic flow while staying within the posted limit.

sec08-card-sec08-R64.front: When a bicyclist rides ahead on your right while oncoming traffic approaches, what order of moves is safest?
sec08-card-sec08-R64.expected_back: With a cyclist on the right and oncoming traffic, slow to let the oncoming vehicle pass before moving left to pass the cyclist.

sec08-card-sec08-R65.front: At an emergency scene, police stop, or recovery tow truck, what lane move must you make — or how much below the limit must you slow?
sec08-card-sec08-R65.expected_back: At an emergency scene, police stop or vehicle-recovery tow truck, move to a nonadjacent lane; if unable, slow at least twenty miles per hour below the posted limit.

sec08-card-sec08-R66.front: Which three heavy, agricultural, or animal-powered road users build speed slowly when entering traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-R66.expected_back: Large trucks, farm equipment and horse-drawn vehicles may accelerate slowly when joining traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R67.front: How do large trucks typically warn trailing drivers that they have slowed way down on long or steep upgrades?
sec08-card-sec08-R67.expected_back: On long or steep climbs, trucks typically use flashers to warn they are moving slowly.

sec08-card-sec08-R68.front: Which vehicles display an orange rear triangle, and what maximum design speed does it signify?
sec08-card-sec08-R68.expected_back: An orange rear triangle identifies farm or horse-drawn vehicles designed for speeds of twenty-five miles per hour or less.

sec08-card-sec08-R69.front: How should you follow farm tractors and horse-drawn vehicles, and what horn rule applies before passing?
sec08-card-sec08-R69.expected_back: Stay well behind tractors and horse-drawn vehicles and do not sound the horn to pass.

sec08-card-sec08-R70.front: When drivers behind may not expect you to slow or stop, how should you use your brake pedal to grab their attention?
sec08-card-sec08-R70.expected_back: Brake lights signal slowing or stopping; if other drivers may not expect braking, quickly tap the pedal three or four times.

sec08-card-sec08-R71.front: Below what speed on a limited-access highway must Pennsylvania drivers switch on hazard flashers?
sec08-card-sec08-R71.expected_back: When required to travel below forty miles per hour on a limited-access highway, use hazard flashers to warn following drivers.

sec08-card-sec08-R72.front: What does a turn signal communicate to nearby traffic — and does it give you priority to turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R72.expected_back: A turn signal communicates the intended turn but does not give the driver priority to make it.

sec08-card-sec08-R73.front: When driving below thirty-five miles per hour, at least how many feet before a turn must you signal?
sec08-card-sec08-R73.expected_back: When driving below thirty-five miles per hour, signal at least one hundred feet before turning.

sec08-card-sec08-R74.front: When traveling thirty-five miles per hour or faster, how many feet before turning must you activate your signal?
sec08-card-sec08-R74.expected_back: When driving at thirty-five miles per hour or faster, signal at least three hundred feet before turning.

sec08-card-sec08-R75.front: What must you use to communicate turns and stops if your vehicle's electric turn indicators fail?
sec08-card-sec08-R75.expected_back: Use hand signals if the vehicle's turn indicators fail.

sec08-card-sec08-R76.front: Which three maneuvers does the Pennsylvania manual's hand-signal chart cover when electric indicators fail?
sec08-card-sec08-R76.expected_back: The manual's hand-signal chart covers three maneuvers when turn indicators fail: a left turn, slowing or stopping, and a right turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R77.front: What real-world pedestrian example does the manual give for sounding your horn when someone may not see your car?
sec08-card-sec08-R77.expected_back: A child starting to run into the street is given as an example of sounding the horn when a pedestrian may not see your vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-R78.front: How do you separate simultaneous hazards when an oncoming car meets you right behind a bicyclist?
sec08-card-sec08-R78.expected_back: When an oncoming vehicle and a bicyclist ahead coincide, handle one condition at a time by slowing behind the cyclist until oncoming traffic passes.

sec08-card-sec08-R79.front: What four actions secure your vehicle and signal for help during a highway breakdown?
sec08-card-sec08-R79.expected_back: For a highway breakdown, signal and pull off carefully, park well clear where others can see, switch on hazards and raise the hood.

sec08-card-sec08-R80.front: Which two visibility or collision situations justify sounding your vehicle's horn?
sec08-card-sec08-R80.expected_back: Use the horn when a pedestrian or driver may not see you or a vehicle appears about to strike you.

sec08-card-sec08-R81.front: What should you sound immediately to warn nearby traffic if you lose control of your vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R81.expected_back: If vehicle control is lost, sound the horn to warn other drivers.

sec08-card-sec08-R82.front: After oncoming traffic clears, at least how many feet of side space must Pennsylvania drivers leave when passing a cyclist?
sec08-card-sec08-R82.expected_back: When passing a cyclist after oncoming traffic has cleared, leave at least four feet of passing space.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What document does a brand-new driver have to get before practicing on Pennsylvania roads?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Practicing behind the wheel before securing proper state authorization counts as unlicensed driving and can delay your path to a license.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Which three evaluations do you have to pass to earn a Pennsylvania driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Exam questions often leave out the eyesight screening to trick you into picking just the written and driving portions.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: How long does your learner application form stay good once your doctor completes the physical?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Waiting past twelve months after your physical forces you to schedule and pay for a brand-new medical checkup.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: How soon ahead of your sixteenth birthday can you get the medical physical for your permit form?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Getting your doctor visit done too early makes the paperwork unusable when you finally turn sixteen and head in.
sec01-card-sec01-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Physical up to six months early

visual_sync.text_span: Physical up to six months early

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: How old do you have to be before submitting a non-commercial learner permit application in Pennsylvania?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Even though you can finish the doctor checkup early, clerks turn away anyone applying a single day before sixteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: Which part of the learner application form does your health care provider have to fill out?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Showing up with a blank back page means an automatic rejection at the counter before you even test.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: What can the examiner do if it is unclear whether your application satisfies Pennsylvania medical standards?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Screeners prioritize road safety when health details look uncertain, holding issuance until specialists confirm you can drive safely.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: What special permit and training setup might PennDOT require if an applicant has a seriously impairing condition?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Passenger-side pedals and professional coaching keep training safe while evaluating how well adaptive techniques work in traffic.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: Who is allowed to complete the parent or guardian consent form for an applicant under eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Older siblings or friends cannot sign unless they hold legal guardianship or loco parentis authority over the minor.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: What has to happen if the consenting adult cannot come with a minor applicant to the center?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: An unnotarized signature from an absent parent gets rejected at check-in to prevent forged teen applications.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: Along with valid identification, what extra proof is needed for consent paperwork when last names do not match?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Bringing marriage, adoption, or birth records prevents a wasted trip when a parent and teen have different surnames.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: How many residency documents does an applicant over age eighteen need to bring?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Showing up with only one piece of address mail stalls adult permit processing right at the counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: How do you submit your finished learner application form once the physical is complete?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Mailing your application delays everything because vision screening and testing happen in person at the licensing center.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: What additional signed form does an applicant under eighteen have to carry in on testing day?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Forgetting the signed parental consent sheet stops a teen from sitting for the computer exam that day.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Why do your birth-date and identity records have to be original documents at the licensing center?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Paper copies or phone photos lack security seals and get turned away immediately during identity verification.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Which federal number card belongs in your folder when visiting for the knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Memorizing your nine digits is not enough when staff ask to verify the physical card in person.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: How should you prepare to pay the required fee when heading in for your permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Licensing counters restrict certain payment types, so checking the form beforehand saves you from a last-minute scramble.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: Where can you find the list of accepted birth-date IDs and exact permit fees?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Reviewing the reverse side before leaving home ensures your ID combination and payment amount match current rules.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: When does the Driver License Center run a vision screening during your visit?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Unless an eye doctor or medical provider already recorded your sight results, staff verify your vision before testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: What should you pack for your test visit if you normally wear glasses or contacts?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Leaving corrective eyewear at home can cause you to fail the counter vision check and miss testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: Once you pass the knowledge test, how long is the newly issued learner permit valid?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Tracking your twelve-month window keeps your permit active while you log hours and wait for road-test eligibility.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: At what exact point are you legally allowed to start behind-the-wheel driving practice?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Passing a medical checkup alone grants zero driving privileges until the examiner actually issues your permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: When does PennDOT advise young drivers to book their road test, and what date rule applies?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Testing slots fill up weeks ahead, so reserving right away locks in a date once your waiting period ends.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: How many total behind-the-wheel practice hours must a driver under eighteen finish before taking the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Test questions frequently swap in fifty or sixty hours to catch teens who mix up state practice totals.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Out of the required teen practice hours, at least how many have to take place at night?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Headlight glare and reduced depth perception make nighttime driving tricky, so supervised dark-hour practice cuts early solo crashes.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: At least how many behind-the-wheel hours must an under-eighteen applicant log in bad weather?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Handling rain, snow, or slick pavement alongside a coach prepares teens before they face storms alone.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: Who is qualified to ride in the front passenger seat to supervise a permit holder?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Letting a nineteen-year-old friend supervise violates permit law because non-guardian coaches must be twenty-one or older.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: How do available seat belts limit passenger numbers for any driver under age eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Every single rider needs a dedicated restraint because sharing belts or crowding extra friends multiplies crash injuries.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: What waiting period and signed hour breakdown must a young learner complete before taking the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Both the calendar hold and the certified night and weather logs are checked before any examiner starts your test.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: Which form handles extending, replacing, or updating a non-commercial permit after expiration or three road-test failures?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Knowing the dedicated extension and correction form saves you from redoing the initial medical application unnecessarily.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: Who should you check with before practicing in another state on a Pennsylvania learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Neighboring states set different teen supervision ages, and unverified out-of-state practice can create coverage or citation headaches.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: What must an applicant bring to the examiner if details on the learner permit need correcting?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Examiners cannot update misspelled names or wrong dates on your record without seeing official supporting paperwork.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: How many times can you take the knowledge test in a single day, even if you drive to another center?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: Statewide computer systems log every attempt instantly, so driving across town for a second same-day try will not work.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: Why must you hang on to your returned application and consent sheets if you do not pass the knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: Throwing away stamped paperwork forces you to chase down fresh signatures before you can try the exam again.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: What optional designation are drivers asked about whenever they renew a Pennsylvania license?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Every renewal cycle gives drivers a fresh opportunity to add life-saving donor status right onto their card.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: What happens on your card when you say yes to organ donation at the Photo License Center?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Printing the indicator directly on the plastic license alerts medical teams immediately without searching separate paperwork.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: What requirement must an applicant under eighteen meet to get the organ-donor designation?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: State law requires an authorized parent, guardian, or adult spouse to sign off before placing donor status on a minor.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: Where can an adult mark organ-donor permission for an applicant under eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Using the dedicated checkbox on the teen consent sheet handles both testing permission and donor approval together.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: How can you add organ-donor status through PennDOT online between renewals, and what does the site provide?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Updating your record online lets you carry a printable confirmation slip right away instead of waiting years for renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: How does an applicant include a voluntary organ-donation awareness contribution when licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Checking the contribution box on your application bundles the optional donation right into your licensing checkout.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: What service and discharge standard qualifies an applicant for the veteran designation on a license?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Reserve and National Guard members qualify alongside active-duty veterans so long as separation was other than dishonorable.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How is a voluntary Veterans' Trust Fund contribution handled alongside your regular licensing fee?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: The trust gift sits on top of standard state charges and only gets routed properly when its form box is checked.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: Why does PennDOT collect your Social Security number, height, and eye color when you apply?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Matching physical traits and federal identity numbers stops impostors from claiming someone else's driving credential.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How is your Social Security number treated when someone views your public Pennsylvania driver record?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Keeping federal tax numbers off public driving histories protects license holders from identity theft during background checks.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: Does your Social Security number appear on the front or back of a Pennsylvania permit or license?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Leaving your nine-digit number off the physical plastic keeps your identity safe if you ever lose your wallet.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: Can someone with poor sight in one eye still get licensed, and what restrictions might apply?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Targeted equipment and daylight restrictions compensate for reduced peripheral sight without automatically barring capable drivers.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.question_text: Which report form does the examiner hand you if your eyesight falls short of screening standards?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.teaching_text: Falling below the counter chart pauses testing until a specialist documents whether prescription lenses fix the issue.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.question_text: Which professionals can examine your eyes and complete the vision report form before you return to test?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.teaching_text: Bringing back the specialist-signed eye report lets the center set proper lens restrictions and resume your exam.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.question_text: How long can a visitor drive in Pennsylvania using a valid foreign driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.teaching_text: If the home-country credential expires three months after arrival, legal driving privileges end right then rather than lasting a year.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.question_text: Is an international driving permit mandatory for someone driving in Pennsylvania on a valid foreign license?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.teaching_text: Carrying the translated booklet helps officers read non-English credentials smoothly during a stop even though law does not mandate it.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.question_text: Holders of valid non-commercial licenses from which four places skip knowledge and road tests via reciprocity, and what test stays?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.teaching_text: Even drivers transferring from France, Germany, Korea, or Taiwan still have to pass the counter eyesight check.

sec01-card-sec01-R18.question_text: License transfers from which three jurisdictions cannot be wrapped up on the exact same day?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.teaching_text: Extra credential verification steps mean applicants from those three places should plan ahead rather than expecting instant walk-out cards.

sec01-card-sec01-R19.question_text: What credential do Pennsylvania residents sixteen and older need if they want to drive a motor vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-R19.teaching_text: Living in the state means holding proper state authorization before operating any motor vehicle on public streets.

sec01-card-sec01-R20.question_text: How soon after moving in must a new resident with an out-of-state or Canadian license switch to Pennsylvania, and what happens to the old card?
sec01-card-sec01-R20.teaching_text: Test questions love pairing thirty or ninety days here, and you cannot keep both state licenses in your wallet.

sec01-card-sec01-R21.question_text: What do Armed Forces or stationed reserve members with a Pennsylvania legal address need to drive non-military vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-R21.teaching_text: Military duty status covers tactical fleet equipment on orders, not personal cars driven off base on public roads.

sec01-card-sec01-R22.question_text: How long does a junior learner permit remain valid, and when does that clock start?
sec01-card-sec01-R22.teaching_text: Check the printed issue date right away so your permit does not lapse before you finish your road test.

sec01-card-sec01-R23.question_text: Where must a junior learner's licensed supervisor sit, and what age rules apply?
sec01-card-sec01-R23.teaching_text: Back-seat coaching is illegal because the supervising adult needs immediate reach and clear forward sightlines.

sec01-card-sec01-R24.question_text: What passenger limit applies to a junior learner regarding the vehicle's seat belts?
sec01-card-sec01-R24.teaching_text: Unbelted extra riders distract novice learners and turn minor fender-benders into severe cabin injuries.

sec01-card-sec01-R25.question_text: Between which hours does a junior license normally ban driving unless an authorized adult rides along or an exception applies?
sec01-card-sec01-R25.teaching_text: Late-night fatigue and low visibility spike teen crash rates, making eleven at night to five in the morning off-limits.

sec01-card-sec01-R26.question_text: Which activities let a junior driver drive during nighttime curfew, and what document must stay in the car?
sec01-card-sec01-R26.teaching_text: Driving home from a late shift without signed chief or employer proof in the glovebox still risks a curfew ticket.
sec01-card-sec01-R26.must_match_memory_hook: Carry notarized work or volunteer proof

visual_sync.text_span: Carry notarized work or volunteer proof

sec01-card-sec01-R27.question_text: Even after passing the road test, how do seat belts cap passenger numbers on a junior license?
sec01-card-sec01-R27.teaching_text: Earning solo driving privileges never lifts the strict one-seat-belt-per-person cap for teen license holders.

sec01-card-sec01-R28.question_text: During the start of a junior license without a qualifying adult aboard, how many non-immediate-family passengers under eighteen may ride along?
sec01-card-sec01-R28.teaching_text: Each additional teen friend in the cabin sharply raises distraction and fatal crash risk during early solo months.

sec01-card-sec01-R29.question_text: After six clean months on a junior license without an adult aboard, what does the under-eighteen non-family limit become, and what blocks that increase?
sec01-card-sec01-R29.teaching_text: Any at-fault crash involvement or traffic conviction locks you out of the higher passenger allowance.

sec01-card-sec01-R30.question_text: Which two point or speeding triggers hand a junior driver a mandatory ninety-day suspension?
sec01-card-sec01-R30.teaching_text: A single heavy speeding ticket at twenty-six over sidelines a junior driver for three full months automatically.

sec01-card-sec01-R31.question_text: After one year on a junior license, what three requirements let a teen upgrade early to a regular license?
sec01-card-sec01-R31.teaching_text: Skipping approved driver education or picking up a single violation keeps junior curfew and passenger rules active until eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R32.question_text: Which PennDOT form does an eligible junior driver submit to convert early to a regular license?
sec01-card-sec01-R32.teaching_text: Submitting the proper conversion application clears junior restrictions at seventeen and a half once every requirement checks out.

sec01-card-sec01-R33.question_text: When does a Pennsylvania junior license automatically turn into a regular driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-R33.teaching_text: Turning eighteen lifts junior curfews and teen passenger caps automatically even if you never took formal driver training.

sec01-card-sec01-R34.question_text: What determines which driver license class you need in Pennsylvania?
sec01-card-sec01-R34.teaching_text: Operating motorcycles or heavy rigs requires specialized testing beyond an everyday passenger car credential.

sec01-card-sec01-R35.question_text: Which non-commercial license class and everyday vehicles does the Pennsylvania driver manual cover?
sec01-card-sec01-R35.teaching_text: Standard sedans, pickups, and family vans all fall under non-commercial Class C rather than commercial truck tiers.

sec01-card-sec01-R36.question_text: What minimum age and vehicle boundary define a Pennsylvania Class C driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-R36.teaching_text: Class C covers standard four-wheel vehicles from age sixteen while heavy combinations and motorcycles belong in separate classes.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: Which three core subjects does the Pennsylvania knowledge examination test you on?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Skipping any one of those three areas leaves easy points on the table because questions pull evenly across signs, statutes, and judgment.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: Which two delivery formats can you request for the knowledge exam at Pennsylvania Driver License Centers?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Requesting headphone narration helps learners who process spoken questions more clearly than reading dense text on a screen.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: Besides English and Spanish, what broad set of eighteen languages can applicants request for the knowledge exam?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Testing in your strongest language prevents tricky wording misunderstandings when evaluating road rules under pressure.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: How soon can you take another shot at the knowledge exam if you do not pass today?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Unlike the seven-day wait for teen road tests, a missed written exam only holds you back until the next open workday.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: What exam milestone has to be completed before you can receive a valid learner permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Finishing paperwork and eye checks alone never authorizes practice until you clear the eighteen-question exam.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: How many questions are on the Pennsylvania knowledge exam, and what format do they use?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: With fewer than twenty items total, every single rushed click carries major weight toward passing or failing.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: How many questions do you have to answer right to pass the Pennsylvania knowledge examination?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Missing a fourth question ends the attempt right away, leaving you a slim three-error cushion across the entire exam.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: How far in advance can a driver under eighteen schedule a Pennsylvania skills test?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Booking right after earning your permit secures a preferred testing slot as soon as your six-month waiting period finishes.
sec02-card-sec02-F08.must_match_memory_hook: Schedule up to six months ahead

visual_sync.text_span: Schedule up to six months ahead

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: Can you take a non-commercial road examination as a walk-in, or what is required first?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Showing up unannounced for behind-the-wheel testing gets you turned away because examiners run strictly booked schedules.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: Where online can you reserve a Pennsylvania road-test appointment?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Using the state Driver and Vehicle Services portal lets you compare open dates and testing sites twenty-four hours a day.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: How can an applicant without internet access book a Pennsylvania road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Keeping a dedicated eight-hundred scheduling line ensures households without web access can still reserve behind-the-wheel slots.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: Who besides PennDOT centers can give the exact same skills test, and how is pricing set?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: State-approved private testing centers follow identical grading standards while setting their own service rates for convenience.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: What personal driving credential must every road-test applicant hand to the examiner before starting?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Arriving with an expired or forgotten permit cancels your road test before the examiner even inspects the car.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: Which signed certification form proving sixty-five practice hours must an under-eighteen applicant present at the road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Without a parent or guardian signature on that certification sheet, examiners cannot test a junior applicant.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: What ownership and tag card must be inside the test vehicle for the examiner to inspect?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: An expired registration card disqualifies the car on the spot even if every light and signal works.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: What financial coverage proof do you have to show for the car used on your road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Examiners verify active liability coverage before stepping inside any test car to protect everyone on public streets.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: Whose driver license gets checked alongside yours at the road test, and what age rule must that person meet?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Because you drove there on a learner permit, the examiner verifies your accompanying coach was legally qualified to ride along.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: Are copies of required road-test documents accepted, or what rule applies at check-in?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: Photocopied permits or registration slips fail verification and cost you your scheduled driving appointment.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: Which four paperwork and windshield sticker items does the examiner verify before your road test starts?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Peeling or expired state safety or county emissions stickers cancel your drive before you ever turn the key.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: Which nine exterior and cabin equipment items does the examiner check for safe operation before your road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Doing a quick driveway check of bulbs, horn, wipers, mirrors, doors, seats, and tread prevents an avoidable cancellation.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: What happens to your road test if any vehicle part is unsafe or misses state inspection standards?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: A single burned-out brake bulb or bald tire ends your appointment in the lot before driving begins.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: When the test car has seat belts, what condition must they be in and who has to buckle up?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Jammed latches or filthy straps stop the test because both you and the examiner must stay buckled throughout.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: When does the examiner move forward to grade your behind-the-wheel driving?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Clearing the pre-drive safety walk-around is mandatory before an examiner rides onto the test course with you.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: Which five on-road problems or mistakes can cause an applicant to fail the Pennsylvania road test?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Even without a collision, ignoring an examiner direction or stacking minor point deductions ends a pass run.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: What cabin task might the examiner ask you to perform before pulling out for the road test?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Practicing in an unfamiliar borrowed car backfires fast if you have to hunt around the dash for switches.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: Which eight cabin switches and features could be included in the pre-drive control demonstration?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Many applicants remember signals and horn yet freeze when asked for parking lights, high beams, hazards, parking brake, or defroster.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: What happens to your road-test score if you operate any vehicle control the wrong way?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Fumbling wipers or defrosters in traffic pulls eyes off the road, so examiners treat control mistakes as automatic failures.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: How long and how wide is the Pennsylvania parallel-parking space between the two uprights?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Practicing inside cones set to exact twenty-four-by-eight dimensions builds muscle memory before test day.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: Where inside the parallel-parking space should your car end up once you finish the maneuver?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Leaving a bumper hanging outside the painted line or hugging one upright costs points even after a smooth entry.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: Which three contact or boundary mistakes are strictly forbidden during the parallel-parking task?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Bumping a marker post, crossing the outer line, or climbing the curb mimics hitting parked cars or sidewalks.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: How many tries and how many positioning adjustments do you get during parallel parking?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Pulling completely out to restart or shifting past three small corrections fails the parking portion.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: Under what strict condition can you test in a car equipped with an automatic self-parking feature?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Examiners grade your own steering and mirror judgment, so automated parking assist must stay disabled the whole drive.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.question_text: Who is allowed to ride inside the vehicle with you during the Pennsylvania road test?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.teaching_text: Parents, instructors, and friends wait outside so the cabin stays distraction-free while the examiner evaluates you.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.question_text: What does the examiner explain to you right at the start of the road test?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.teaching_text: Examiners give clear route and maneuver directions up front rather than trying to trick you into illegal turns.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.question_text: Compliance with which three roadside traffic controls does the examiner closely watch during your drive?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.teaching_text: Rolling past a stop sign or rushing a yellow light shows unsafe intersection habits and triggers heavy deductions.

sec02-card-sec02-R14.question_text: Alongside smooth vehicle control, what driver-to-driver communication habit is graded throughout the road test?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.teaching_text: Signaling every lane move, pull-out, and parking step tells surrounding traffic what you plan before your wheels turn.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.question_text: When do you receive your driver license if you pass the road test at a PennDOT Driver License Center?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.teaching_text: Passing at a state licensing center lets you walk out holding your new credential that very visit.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.question_text: How many days must a driver under eighteen wait before retaking a failed road test?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.teaching_text: A mandatory one-week pause gives teen drivers time to fix weak maneuvers instead of rushing straight back.

sec02-card-sec02-R17.question_text: How many road-test tries does a single learner permit give you before it expires?
sec02-card-sec02-R17.teaching_text: Practicing thoroughly before booking keeps you from burning through all three tries on one permit.

sec02-card-sec02-R18.question_text: What must an applicant do if they fail the road test a third time?
sec02-card-sec02-R18.teaching_text: Using up your third attempt invalidates further testing until PennDOT processes a permit extension.

sec02-card-sec02-R19.question_text: Which specific PennDOT form handles an expired non-commercial permit or three failed road-test attempts?
sec02-card-sec02-R19.teaching_text: Filing the proper extension request restores road-test eligibility without starting a brand-new medical physical right away.

sec02-card-sec02-R20.question_text: What happens if you still have not taken or passed the road test three years after your medical physical?
sec02-card-sec02-R20.teaching_text: Letting thirty-six months pass after your doctor exam wipes your progress and requires a fresh application and written test.

sec02-card-sec02-R21.question_text: How does skipping turn signals affect your Pennsylvania road-test outcome?
sec02-card-sec02-R21.teaching_text: Applicants often forget signals inside parking lots or parallel boxes, turning an otherwise clean drive into a fail.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: Which two types of intersection movements do traffic signals regulate?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Remembering that intersection lights direct foot traffic alongside cars prevents right-of-way blind spots when turning across busy crosswalks.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: Where are red and green positioned on a vertical traffic light?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Standardized vertical lens placement lets drivers with color-vision deficiency or sun glare read stop and go cues instantly.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: Where do red and green appear on a horizontal traffic light?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Knowing left-to-right lens order keeps you from misreading sideways overpass signals in bright glare or low visibility.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt at a steady red light?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Rolling past the painted line or into an unmarked intersection entrance blocks pedestrians and exposes your bumper to cross traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: Once stopped at a steady red light, how long must you wait if no lawful turn on red applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Anticipating a signal change and creeping into cross traffic before green appears is a classic cause of intersection T-bone crashes.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: Under what conditions may you turn right at a steady red light in Pennsylvania?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Rolling through a right on red without a full halt and pedestrian scan is one of the fastest ways to fail or hit someone.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: When does Pennsylvania allow a left turn on a steady red light?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Knowledge tests love trapping drivers with two-way streets, where turning left on red would cut straight across opposing lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: What upcoming signal change does a steady yellow light warn you about?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Treating yellow as a speed-up challenge instead of an imminent red warning puts you in the box right as cross traffic launches.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: How should you respond when approaching a steady yellow light, and when may you continue through?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Slamming the brakes when too close triggers rear-end collisions, while gunning it from far back risks running a fresh red.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: When does a steady green light allow you to drive straight through an intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Green grants permission rather than physical protection, so charging forward before lingering cross traffic clears causes avoidable crashes.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: What restrictions and yield duties apply when turning on a steady green light?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Even with a solid green ball, cutting off oncoming cars or crosswalk pedestrians already in the intersection puts fault squarely on you.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: After stopping for a steady red arrow in Pennsylvania, what turn-on-red rule applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Unlike states that ban all red-arrow turns, Pennsylvania treats a steady red arrow like a steady red ball for lawful turns after stopping.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: What specific sign, lane, and yield limits govern turning after stopping at a steady red arrow?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Missing a turn-prohibition plaque or turning left from anything other than one-way to one-way turns a legal maneuver into a ticket.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: What does a steady yellow arrow tell drivers about the current turn phase?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Assuming your turn arrow stays open invites a head-on collision right as the phase closes to red.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: What must you do when facing a steady yellow arrow, and when can you finish your turn?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Stopping before the line keeps you out of conflict, while calmly clearing an already-started turn prevents stranding your car mid-intersection.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: Why can you turn in the direction of a green arrow without oncoming conflict?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Knowing oncoming lanes are held by red lets you clear the turn lane smoothly while still scanning for stray hazards.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: How do your right-of-way duties shift when a green turn arrow switches to an ordinary green ball?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Once the arrow disappears, oncoming traffic gets released too, making left-turn collisions a major risk if you keep following the car ahead.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: What three actions are required when approaching a flashing yellow traffic light?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Flashing yellow marks high-conflict spots where maintaining full speed leaves zero margin for sudden cross traffic or turning cars.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: What steps must you take before driving through a flashing red light?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Rolling a flashing red is identical to blowing a stop sign, often where cross-street traffic has a flashing yellow and never stops.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: What must you do before completing a turn under a flashing yellow arrow?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Drivers often confuse any arrow with a protected phase, forgetting they must wait for both crosswalk users and oncoming vehicles.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: Why is turning on a flashing yellow arrow considered an unprotected maneuver?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Oncoming drivers are moving at full road speed on green, so misjudging their gap leads to severe angled collisions.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: How must drivers handle an intersection when its traffic signals stop working?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Breezing through dark signals during a power outage guarantees a wreck when cross-street drivers assume they can keep rolling too.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: What do highway ramp-metering signals regulate, and when do they typically run?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Breaking up platoons of merging cars during peak congestion prevents freeway traffic waves and merge-zone rear-enders.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: When may you pull past a highway ramp-metering signal toward the freeway?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Jumping a red ramp signal disrupts freeway spacing and catches the driver ahead braking for a highway gap.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: How many vehicles may proceed on each green cycle of a single-lane ramp meter?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Piggybacking behind another car on one quick green flash triggers violations and packs two vehicles into a single merge gap.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: How are ramp-metering lights arranged when an entrance ramp has more than one lane?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Watching the wrong lane's light makes you launch on red right beside another accelerating driver.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: Does a green ramp-meter light give you right-of-way when merging onto the highway?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Freeway traffic never stops for ramp meters, so blindly merging on green without matching speed and checking gaps causes sideswipes.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: What does a downward-pointing green arrow suspended over a highway lane indicate?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Reversible roadways switch flow by time of day, and downward green confirms traffic in your direction owns that lane.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: What warning does an overhead steady yellow X give, and how should you react?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: Staying under a steady yellow X leaves you stranded in a lane about to flip toward oncoming traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: What rule applies to any travel lane marked overhead by a steady red X?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: A steady red X closes the lane to your direction, often because opposing rush-hour traffic or emergency crews occupy it.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: What maneuver restriction does an overhead steady white one-way left-turn arrow enforce?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Using a dedicated left-turn lane to jump straight ahead surprises turning drivers and triggers intersection sideswipes.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: How is a lane marked by an overhead steady white two-way left-turn arrow used?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Drivers from both directions enter this center lane to turn left, so cruising or passing inside it creates a head-on trap.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: Which word and symbol displays govern pedestrians at signalized crosswalks?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Modern intersections pair or replace lettered displays with walking-person and raised-hand icons that carry identical legal weight.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Which signals must pedestrians follow when an intersection has no dedicated walk displays?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Without dedicated crosswalk icons, standard red, yellow, and green traffic balls dictate when foot traffic can safely cross.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: What must a driver do if a pedestrian ignores a crosswalk signal and steps into the street?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Having a green light never excuses hitting someone on foot, and knowledge tests always prioritize human safety over technical right-of-way.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: What does a steady WALK display allow, and what hazard must the pedestrian still watch for?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Vehicles turning on green share the same signal phase and frequently overlook people stepping off the curb.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: What should a pedestrian already in the crosswalk do when the raised hand or DON'T WALK starts flashing?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Flashing clearance intervals are timed long enough for people already off the curb to reach the far sidewalk without panicking or turning back.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: What rule applies to a pedestrian still standing on the curb when the raised hand begins flashing?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Stepping out late during the countdown leaves you stranded in live lanes when cross traffic gets its green light.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.question_text: What does a steady DON'T WALK message or steady raised hand mean for pedestrians?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.teaching_text: A solid raised hand means conflicting vehicle lanes actively hold the intersection, making any step into the roadway illegal and dangerous.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.question_text: How must you drive near a blind pedestrian carrying a white cane or walking with a guide dog?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.teaching_text: Visually impaired pedestrians rely on sound cues rather than eye contact, so honking or edging close can disorient them in traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.question_text: What is Pennsylvania's maximum speed limit when school-zone yellow lights flash or posted hours are active?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.teaching_text: Children dart unpredictably between buses and crosswalks, and dropping to fifteen drastically shortens your stopping distance.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.question_text: Besides a fine, how many driving-record points are added for speeding in a Pennsylvania school zone?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.teaching_text: Pennsylvania hits school-zone speeders immediately with both financial penalties and three license points on the very first offense.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.question_text: How should you check for danger every time you approach a railroad grade crossing?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.teaching_text: Warning devices can malfunction and second trains can hide on parallel tracks, so visual and audio checks save lives.

sec03-card-sec03-R17.question_text: Which four railroad-crossing warnings require you to come to a stop?
sec03-card-sec03-R17.teaching_text: Trains take over a mile to halt, so any active visual, human, or audible alert demands an immediate stop.

sec03-card-sec03-R18.question_text: Are you ever allowed to drive around a lowered railroad gate or ignore an active train warning?
sec03-card-sec03-R18.teaching_text: Trains look slower than their true speed, and weaving around lowered arms is both illegal and frequently fatal.

sec03-card-sec03-R19.question_text: How must you handle a railroad crossing that has no lights or gates?
sec03-card-sec03-R19.teaching_text: Passive rural crossings give no automated flash or bell, leaving your own speed reduction, eyes, and ears as the only defense.

sec03-card-sec03-R20.question_text: After a train passes, when is it safe and legal to drive across railroad tracks?
sec03-card-sec03-R20.teaching_text: Starting across the moment the caboose clears can put you straight into a second train coming the opposite way on adjacent rails.

sec03-card-sec03-R21.question_text: Even without gates, which two train-approach cues require you to stop at a railroad crossing?
sec03-card-sec03-R21.teaching_text: Whether you hear a horn first or spot a locomotive closing fast, stopping clear of the crossing keeps you out of the impact zone.

sec03-card-sec03-R22.question_text: May you ever stop your vehicle directly on railroad tracks if no train appears nearby?
sec03-card-sec03-R22.teaching_text: A stalled engine or pinned traffic queue on empty-looking rails leaves zero escape time once a fast train rounds the bend.

sec03-card-sec03-R23.question_text: Where must you wait when traffic ahead backs up near a railroad crossing?
sec03-card-sec03-R23.teaching_text: Wait behind the crossing until full vehicle-length space opens on the far side so your rear bumper never overhangs the track zone.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: What are the three primary categories of highway signs in Pennsylvania?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Sorting roadside panels into rules, hazards, and directions helps you process unfamiliar intersections in a split second.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: What kind of legal message do regulatory signs communicate to drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Unlike yellow hazard warnings, regulatory panels post binding traffic laws you must obey immediately on the spot.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: Which four common driving behaviors can regulatory signs control?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: Spotting regulatory panels early keeps you out of wrong-way lanes, illegal turns, speed traps, and tow zones.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: What two penalties can follow if you ignore a posted regulatory sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Treating regulatory panels like optional suggestions hits both your wallet and your Pennsylvania driving record.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: What shapes and color combinations do most regulatory signs use?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Recognizing upright black-and-white or red-accented panels from a distance tells you a mandatory rule applies ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: What unique shape and side count set the highway STOP sign apart from every other road sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Even from the back of an intersection or under heavy snow, eight sides unmistakably identify a mandatory stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: What must you do at a STOP sign before pulling into the intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Scanning both sidewalks and cross lanes from a standstill prevents pulling out in front of fast cross-street vehicles.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: Is slowing down at a STOP sign without bringing your wheels to a full halt legal?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Coasting through a stop bar fails road tests instantly and hides approaching cars behind windshield pillars.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: Where must the front of your vehicle stop when a stop line or crosswalk is painted on the road?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Stopping past the first white stripe blocks foot traffic and crowds large vehicles turning onto your street.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: How should you proceed if buildings or parked cars block your view after stopping at a STOP sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Stop legally first for crosswalk safety, then inch out slowly so cross traffic can spot your nose before you commit.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: Who stops at an all-way stop intersection, and which driver goes first?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Tracking arrival order as you roll up prevents hesitation standoffs and surprise fender-benders in the box.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: When two drivers reach an all-way stop at the exact same moment, who yields?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Permit exams love testing simultaneous arrivals, so always glance right and let that car move first on a tie.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: How may two drivers facing each other across an all-way stop proceed?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Two straight-through opposing cars never cross paths, whereas an unannounced left turn cuts directly across the other driver.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: What geometric shape and number of sides identify a highway YIELD sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: A downward-pointing three-sided silhouette lets you spot a yield obligation from behind or in foul weather.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: What actions are required when approaching a YIELD sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: A yield panel never guarantees a rolling merge, so cover the brake and be ready to halt completely for traffic or walkers.
sec04-card-sec04-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Slow, check, yield, stop if needed

visual_sync.text_span: Slow, check, yield, stop if needed

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: What kind of traffic opening do you need before pulling past a YIELD sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: If cross-street drivers have to tap their brakes or swerve when you enter, your gap was too small.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: What requirement do STOP signs and YIELD signs share before you enter cross traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Stopping first never buys you right-of-way, because both signs require waiting until cross lanes have safe spacing.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: What exact roadway feature does a white X-shaped crossbuck sign mark?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Unlike round yellow advance warnings placed upstream, the crossbuck stands right at the rails themselves.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: Which regulatory instruction should you treat a railroad crossbuck as giving?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Even without flashing lights, a crossbuck legally requires easing off the gas and stopping whenever a train is visible or audible.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.question_text: What does the supplemental plaque paired with YIELD at a one-lane bridge or underpass require?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.teaching_text: Only one direction fits through a narrow span at once, so yielding before the bottleneck prevents a head-on standoff.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: What hazard does a DO NOT ENTER sign warn you against?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Posted at exit ramps and one-way street mouths, ignoring it puts your car nose-to-nose with oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: Where are WRONG WAY signs placed, and what mistake do they alert you to?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: If you miss the initial entry restriction on a ramp or one-way street, WRONG WAY panels serve as your urgent second alarm.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: Which travel direction is permitted where a ONE WAY sign is posted?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Checking ONE WAY arrows before turning at unfamiliar city corners prevents turning into oncoming lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: What severe crash type do you risk by driving opposite the flow of a one-way street?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: Head-on impacts combine both vehicles' speeds, making wrong-way entry one of the deadliest urban and highway errors.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: How are the two roadways of a divided highway arranged and separated?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Remembering each half is strictly one-way keeps you turning onto the proper side of the median or guide rail.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.question_text: What kind of intersection ahead does a regulatory DIVIDED HIGHWAY sign announce?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.teaching_text: Spotting the median symbol before reaching the corner keeps you from turning left too early into oncoming lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.question_text: At a signed divided-highway intersection, which turn does each roadway allow?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.teaching_text: Near-side lanes move left-to-right across you, so you must clear the median before turning left onto the far roadway.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.question_text: What rule do NO TRUCKS, NO BICYCLES, and NO PEDESTRIAN CROSSING signs enforce?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.teaching_text: Weight limits, high-speed expressways, or unsafe crossings make certain corridors off-limits to specific travelers.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.question_text: What maneuver does a NO U-TURN sign forbid?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.teaching_text: Swinging a hundred-eighty degrees across tight medians or blind hills traps your side doors broadside in live lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.question_text: What maneuver is illegal at an intersection posted with a NO RIGHT TURN sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.teaching_text: Cities post right-turn bans where one-way cross streets, transit lanes, or heavy pedestrian crossings create conflict.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.question_text: What maneuver is illegal at an intersection posted with a NO LEFT TURN sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.teaching_text: Blocking a through lane to attempt a banned left turn stalls traffic behind you and risks oncoming collisions.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.question_text: What restriction applies wherever a NO PARKING sign is posted?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.teaching_text: Leaving a car in a signed no-parking zone blocks fire hydrants, sightlines, or rush-hour travel lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.question_text: What overtaking move does a DO NOT PASS regulatory sign forbid?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.teaching_text: Hills, curves, and intersections hide oncoming cars, making any attempt to pull around slower traffic ahead a blind gamble.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.question_text: What do directional lane-use signs posted at or near intersections tell drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.teaching_text: Reading lane-control arrows early lets you merge smoothly instead of cutting across solid lines at the corner.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.question_text: How does a left-turn-only lane differ from a neighboring lane signed with both left and straight arrows?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.teaching_text: Going straight from the dedicated turn pocket sideswipes drivers legally curving left from the shared option lane beside you.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: Who shares a center lane signed LEFT TURN ONLY, and which two uses are banned inside it?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Treating a two-way left-turn lane as a passing or travel chute puts you directly into opposing drivers pulling in to turn.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: Which warning sign is frequently paired across the road from a regulatory DO NOT PASS sign?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: When a truck ahead blocks the right-side regulatory rectangle, the left-side yellow pennant still warns you not to pull out.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: On which side of a median island or divider must you drive when facing a KEEP RIGHT sign?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Passing left of a raised island puts your car straight into opposing lanes on the wrong side of the barrier.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: Under what roadway conditions does a posted speed limit represent the maximum legal speed?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Knowledge exams frequently test that posted numbers assume dry pavement, clear daylight, and light traffic rather than every situation.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: How must you adjust your speed when weather, visibility, or traffic conditions deteriorate?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Driving the posted limit on ice, fog, or heavy rain can still earn a driving-too-fast-for-conditions citation and cause a skid.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: What must you do at a red light when a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Blind corners, heavy pedestrian flow, or angled cross streets eliminate safe sightlines for red-light turns at signed junctions.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: What movement choice do you have when your lane sign displays two alternative arrows?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Option lanes split busy traffic streams smoothly, provided you signal early and track into the matching receiving lane.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: What must you do if you accidentally enter a lane marked with a turn arrow and ONLY?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Swinging last-second out of an ONLY lane across neighboring traffic causes far more crashes than taking a thirty-second detour.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: What does a LEFT TURN YIELD ON GREEN sign require before you turn left?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Posted right beside the signal head, this reminder stops drivers from mistaking a green ball for a protected turn phase.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: Does a circular green light protect your left turn where LEFT TURN YIELD ON GREEN is posted?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: Oncoming straight-through drivers hold the exact same green ball and have zero obligation to slow down for your turn.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.question_text: What rule does a LEFT TURN YIELD ON FLASHING YELLOW ARROW sign enforce?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.teaching_text: You may turn left while yellow flashes, provided oncoming lanes and crosswalks are completely clear first.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.question_text: Is a left turn made during a flashing yellow arrow protected or unprotected?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.teaching_text: Only a solid green arrow holds opposing traffic on red, whereas flashing yellow leaves gap judgment entirely on you.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.question_text: What does a RIGHT TURN SIGNAL sign tell drivers approaching a multi-signal corner?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.teaching_text: Channelized right-turn lanes often run on their own separate signal head rather than the main through-lane lights.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.question_text: What intersection hazard does an OPPOSING TRAFFIC HAS EXTENDED GREEN sign warn about?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.teaching_text: Turning left as your light goes yellow or red assuming oncoming cars are also stopping will put you straight into moving traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R15.question_text: Who may legally use spaces marked by a regulatory RESERVED PARKING sign?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.teaching_text: Wider access aisles and close building proximity keep essential mobility routes open for drivers and veterans with qualifying disabilities.

sec04-card-sec04-R16.question_text: What official credential must a vehicle display to park in a reserved disability space?
sec04-card-sec04-R16.teaching_text: Even when transporting an eligible passenger, parking without displaying the issued plate or hangtag counts as an unauthorized violation.

sec04-card-sec04-R17.question_text: What two consequences apply if an unauthorized vehicle parks in a reserved disability space?
sec04-card-sec04-R17.teaching_text: Pulling into a blue-and-white accessible stall "just for a minute" risks both a steep ticket and an impounded car.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: What job do roadway warning signs perform for approaching drivers?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Waiting until you reach a hidden hazard leaves too little space to adjust steering or speed smoothly.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: What shape and color combination do most roadway warning signs use?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Spotting a yellow diamond from a distance tells you a hazard is coming even before you read the legend.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: What shape is the NO PASSING ZONE warning, and where is it posted?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Tests love asking where the pennant sits because left-side placement stays visible when a truck blocks the right shoulder.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: What do chevron alignment plaques tell you about the road ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Chevrons trace the exact path of a tight curve so you do not overdrive a sudden change in alignment.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: Where do chevron alignment plaques appear in relation to an advance curve warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Seeing multiple chevrons strung through the bend helps you judge how long the curve keeps turning.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: How should you adjust speed and lane position for a LEFT CURVE warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Hugging the inside line on a left bend puts your mirrors dangerously close to oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: How should you adjust speed and lane position for a RIGHT CURVE warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Permit questions contrast left and right bends because drifting left on a right curve crosses toward opposing vehicles.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: What speed change and lane position does a SHARP LEFT TURN warning require?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: A ninety-degree bend demands much heavier braking beforehand than a gentle curve so tires keep grip.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: What speed change and lane position does a SHARP RIGHT TURN warning require?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Carrying highway pace into a sharp right bend swings wide into the opposing lane mid-corner.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: Where can an advisory speed appear with a sharp-turn warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Scanning beneath the main warning keeps you from missing the recommended cornering speed plaque.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: What roadway layout and driver action does a SET OF CURVES warning announce?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Braking before the first bend keeps weight balanced when steering immediately reverses into the second curve.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: How should you respond to a warning for successive sharp right and left turns?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Back-to-back tight corners multiply weight transfer, making late braking inside the first turn especially risky.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: How many consecutive bends ahead does a WINDING ROAD warning indicate?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Exam questions regularly pit two-curve reverse warnings against the three-curve threshold for a winding road.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: What does a ONE DIRECTION LARGE ARROW warn of, and how much must you slow?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Treating an extreme directional bend like an intersection corner prevents running off the outside edge.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: What road geometry does the handbook's ROAD ENTERING CURVE warning describe?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Reading the diagram accurately shows which direction your main lane bends versus where cross traffic joins.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: Why must you use extra caution at a ROAD ENTERING CURVE warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Sightlines around a curve are short, so a side-road motorist may pull out thinking the lane is empty.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: What specific danger does a TRUCK ROLLOVER warning identify?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Passenger drivers near tall rigs on tight ramps should leave extra space instead of riding beside a trailer.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Which type of roadway sign may be paired with an advisory-speed plaque?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Advisory plaques never raise the legal limit; they pair with yellow or orange diamonds to flag safe hazard speeds.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: What speed should you maintain on a sharp left curve posted with a twenty-five miles per hour advisory?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Exceeding the posted curve advisory cuts tire traction margin, especially if pavement is damp or uneven.
