sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: What does a MERGING TRAFFIC warning posted on a major road announce?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Checking right mirrors early lets you adjust speed or change lanes smoothly before ramp cars arrive.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: Who must yield when vehicles enter a major roadway from a ramp or side road?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: A classic permit trap claims highway traffic must yield, when entering drivers carry the legal duty to wait for a gap.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: What does an ADDED LANE warning tell drivers about merging at the junction?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Confusing an added-lane diagram with a merge sign causes unnecessary braking when ramp traffic gets its own lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: What conflicting traffic movements happen inside a warned WEAVE AREA?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Two streams swapping lanes in a short span demand calm speeds, early signals, and careful blind-spot checks.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: What roadway change does a TWO-WAY TRAFFIC AHEAD warning announce?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Forgetting that a one-way street is ending can leave you cruising head-on in the left lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Where must you position your vehicle after passing a TWO-WAY TRAFFIC AHEAD warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Moving into the right lane immediately keeps oncoming traffic safely separated once the two-way section begins.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: What upcoming roadway change does a LANE ENDS warning announce?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Spotting the lane-drop warning early prevents last-second squeeze merges where pavement tapers away.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: Which way must drivers merge when a warning indicates the right lane ends?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Signaling early and matching left-lane speed avoids braking to a stop at the end of the taper.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: What two things can intersection warning diagrams show an approaching driver?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Reading the stem shapes tells you whether cross streets angle in or your own lane ends at a tee.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: How should you approach an intersection marked by an advance warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Cross traffic at rural junctions may have poor visibility or miss their stop, so cover your brake early.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: What does a TWO DIRECTION LARGE ARROW on the far side of a T-intersection tell you?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Seeing the two-headed arrow across the intersection warns that continuing straight ahead drives off the roadway.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: What roadway conditions and driver actions go with a NARROW BRIDGE OR UNDERPASS warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Without escape room on the right edge, steady steering and reduced speed keep mirrors clear of bridge walls.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: When should you wait before entering a narrow bridge or underpass?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Squeezing onto a tight span alongside a farm rig or wide truck invites a head-on sideswipe.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: What two adjustments do wet conditions require at a SLIPPERY WHEN WET warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Rain mixes with road oil to stretch stopping distances, so extra cushion ahead prevents rear-end skids.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: How should you handle pedals and turns on a wet, slippery roadway?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Sudden throttle, hard braking, or brisk steering snaps wet tires loose into a hydroplaning spin.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: What does DIVIDED HIGHWAY BEGINS warn of, and which side must you take?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Mistaking the opening of a center island at night can guide a car straight into the wrong-way lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: What changes at DIVIDED HIGHWAY ENDS, and how must you adjust?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Drivers conditioned by miles of divided lanes often forget oncoming traffic will soon be inches across yellow paint.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: Why is a DEER CROSSING warning posted on a stretch of roadway?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Deer move unpredictably at dawn and dusk and rarely travel alone, so scan ditches whenever one appears.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: When must you refuse to drive under a LOW CLEARANCE warning?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Box trucks, campers, and roof-mounted cargo that exceed posted height will strike bridge beams with violent force.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: What two roadside edge hazards do shoulder warnings identify?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Dropping tires onto sunken gravel or soft dirt tugs the steering wheel toward the ditch.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: Up to how far below the road surface can a LOW SHOULDER drop be?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Permit questions test the exact three-inch figure that separates a low shoulder from a steeper drop-off.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: How does a SHOULDER DROP OFF warning compare with a LOW SHOULDER warning?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: A deep pavement lip can scrub a tire sidewall hard enough to flip or spin an impatiently steered car.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: What two mistakes must you avoid if a wheel drops onto a low or soft shoulder?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel or slamming brakes catches the pavement lip and slingshots the car across oncoming lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: What actions should you take when you pass a HILL or DOWNGRADE warning?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Engine braking holds downhill pace steady so friction brakes do not overheat and fade on long grades.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: Why is TRAFFIC SIGNAL AHEAD posted, and how must you respond?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Cresting a hill or rounding a bend at full speed leaves zero room if the unseen light is red.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: Why might stopped vehicles still block your lane past a hidden traffic signal?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Even after a hidden light turns green, the back of the waiting line takes several seconds to start moving.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: What hazards does STOP SIGN AHEAD warn of, and what action is required?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Waiting cars can extend well back from an obscured stop line, requiring gradual braking before the sightline opens.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: What does a BICYCLE CROSSING AHEAD warning alert motorists to expect?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Trail crossings bring quick-moving cyclists across travel lanes where bushes or fences can hide their approach.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: Which two background colors are permitted on a bicycle-crossing warning?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: High-visibility yellow-green stands out against shady trees and glare where vulnerable road users cross.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: What must you start doing at a RAILROAD CROSSING AHEAD warning?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: Rural crossings often lack gates or flashing bells, making early sight and sound checks essential before the tracks.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.question_text: What does an advance intersection-and-railroad diagram tell you about the side road?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.teaching_text: Knowing tracks sit right off the main road prepares you before you commit to turning onto that side street.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.question_text: What must a turning driver be ready to do when tracks cross a side road just past an intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.teaching_text: Swinging briskly onto the cross street leaves almost no buffer between the corner and an approaching train.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.question_text: What does a bicycle and motor-vehicle SHARE THE ROAD plaque at a narrow spot require?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.teaching_text: Pinching past a rider where shoulders vanish creates wind blast and mirror hazards with zero margin for error.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.question_text: Where can a PEDESTRIAN CROSSING warning stand, and what readiness does it require?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.teaching_text: Pedestrians have no crash protection, so covering the brake near marked or upcoming crossings prevents tragedy.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.question_text: Which two background colors may pedestrian-crossing warnings use?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.teaching_text: Fluorescent yellow-green highlights foot, bike, and school crossings in low light or cluttered city blocks.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.question_text: What shape is the SCHOOL advance sign, and what does it warn?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.teaching_text: Recognizing the house-like five-sided silhouette spots a school zone even when snow covers the lettering.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.question_text: What three actions are required when you encounter a school warning?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.teaching_text: Young students often dart between buses or parked cars without checking oncoming lanes first.

sec05-card-sec05-R22.question_text: Which two background colors can a school warning display?
sec05-card-sec05-R22.teaching_text: Both colors carry identical school-zone caution, though fluorescent yellow-green grabs attention faster in fog or rain.

sec05-card-sec05-R23.question_text: What roadway activity do HORSE-DRAWN VEHICLE warnings identify?
sec05-card-sec05-R23.teaching_text: Closing speed behind a horse-drawn buggy at highway pace is startlingly fast over hill crests.

sec05-card-sec05-R24.question_text: What two types of roadside dangers do striped hazard markers identify?
sec05-card-sec05-R24.teaching_text: Bridge abutments, culverts, and steep ditches right off the fog line leave zero room for lane drift.

sec05-card-sec05-R25.question_text: How do the angled stripes on a roadside hazard marker tell you which way to steer?
sec05-card-sec05-R25.teaching_text: Picture rain sliding down the angled bars straight onto the safe travel lane to nail every marker test question.

sec05-card-sec05-R26.question_text: On which side do you pass a marked hazard on the right edge versus the left edge?
sec05-card-sec05-R26.teaching_text: Keeping your vehicle toward the center of the pavement clears obstacles sitting on either shoulder.

sec05-card-sec05-R27.question_text: Which side may you take past a marker posted on a center roadway hazard?
sec05-card-sec05-R27.teaching_text: Stripes sloping downward toward both outer edges show traffic splits legally around either side of the obstacle.

sec05-card-sec05-R28.question_text: How do work-zone warning diamonds differ visually from standard roadway warnings?
sec05-card-sec05-R28.teaching_text: Bright orange immediately signals temporary construction or utility hazards where lane patterns may differ from yesterday.

sec05-card-sec05-R29.question_text: What activities do work-zone warnings mark, and how must drivers respond?
sec05-card-sec05-R29.teaching_text: Workers and heavy machinery operate feet from live traffic where narrow temporary lanes leave tiny safety margins.

sec05-card-sec05-R30.question_text: When must your headlights be turned on inside a posted Pennsylvania work zone?
sec05-card-sec05-R30.teaching_text: Test questions bait you with sunny afternoons or empty inactive sites, yet Pennsylvania requires headlights every single trip.

sec05-card-sec05-R31.question_text: What extra penalty applies if police stop you for a work-zone violation with headlights off?
sec05-card-sec05-R31.teaching_text: Daytime running lights may not light taillights, so click full headlights on whenever orange boundary signs start.

sec05-card-sec05-R32.question_text: What makes a Pennsylvania work zone count as an active work zone?
sec05-card-sec05-R32.teaching_text: Penalties escalate sharply whenever crews are physically exposed on the pavement or adjacent shoulder.

sec05-card-sec05-R33.question_text: How do drivers know exact limits of an active work zone?
sec05-card-sec05-R33.teaching_text: Watching for both the white entry and end plaques tells you precisely where active-zone enforcement applies.

sec05-card-sec05-R34.question_text: What does a ROAD WORK AHEAD warning announce and call for?
sec05-card-sec05-R34.teaching_text: Easing off the accelerator at the first orange diamond prepares you for sudden merges, shifts, or flaggers.

sec05-card-sec05-R35.question_text: What two details does a LANE CLOSED AHEAD warning give approaching traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-R35.teaching_text: Knowing both which lane shuts down and how far away the cones start lets you merge calmly.

sec05-card-sec05-R36.question_text: What does a work-zone diamond reading RIGHT LANE CLOSED one thousand feet announce?
sec05-card-sec05-R36.teaching_text: At highway speeds one thousand feet disappears in roughly twelve seconds, leaving no time to procrastinate merging.

sec05-card-sec05-R37.question_text: Who does FLAGGER AHEAD warn you to watch for, and what tools do they use?
sec05-card-sec05-R37.teaching_text: A flagger's paddle or red flag overrides normal lane habits when two-way traffic shares one open lane.

sec05-card-sec05-R38.question_text: Where must you pay particular attention to flaggers?
sec05-card-sec05-R38.teaching_text: Rear-end crashes happen when distracted drivers stare at construction equipment instead of the person holding the paddle.

sec05-card-sec05-R39.question_text: Why does a WORKERS AHEAD warning demand special care from motorists?
sec05-card-sec05-R39.teaching_text: Only plastic cones separate crews on foot from passing mirrors, so widen your buffer and drop speed.

sec05-card-sec05-R40.question_text: What can happen if highway workers observe speeding or unsafe driving in a work zone?
sec05-card-sec05-R40.teaching_text: Even without a patrol car in sight, documented work-zone violations bring mailed citations with fines and license points.

sec05-card-sec05-R41.question_text: What does ROAD CLOSED FLOODING mean, and what must a driver do?
sec05-card-sec05-R41.teaching_text: Shallow-looking floodwater hides washed-out pavement and floats cars quickly, so never drive around closure barricades.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: What do electronic flashing arrow panels warn of and direct drivers to do?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Bright flashing arrows cut through glare and night traffic so you spot a closed lane from far back.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: When should you start merging as you approach an electronic arrow panel?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Racing all the way to the trailer traps your car at the cones and forces abrupt highway braking.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: What does an electronic panel indicate when showing a caution display instead of a directional arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Even when your travel lane stays open, crews and trucks right beside the fog line need extra awareness.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: What role do work-zone barrels, tubes, cones, and vertical panels serve?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Temporary orange markers trace shifted lane boundaries where old painted stripes might lead straight into equipment.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What four kinds of helpful information do roadway guide signs identify?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Clear route and service cues let drivers plan lane choices calmly instead of swerving across exits late.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: What geometric shape do roadway guide signs usually take?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Wide horizontal boards hold town names, exit numbers, and lane arrows without blocking overhead bridge clearance.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What lettering and background colors appear on highway and expressway guide signs?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Permit exams pair sign colors with function, and green always means directional guidance rather than rules or warnings.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: How many times is a typical highway exit posted in advance and at the ramp?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Expecting two advance notices before the gore point gives you plenty of breathing room to move over.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: How do repeated advance exit boards help motorists in fast or heavy traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Tall trailers can block a single roadside board, so repeated overhead warnings prevent panicked last-second swerves.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: What roadside posts do exit numbers match, and what can you estimate with them?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Subtracting your current exit number from your target exit instantly tells you how many miles remain.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: How many miles separate Exit ninety-five and Exit twenty in the handbook's example?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Simple subtraction turns mile-based exit tabs into a quick mental fuel and travel-time gauge without touching a phone.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: What happens to a travel lane marked overhead with an EXIT ONLY panel?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Staying in a dropped lane by mistake pulls you onto the off-ramp instead of carrying you past the interchange.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: What options does a motorist in an EXIT ONLY lane have?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Never cut across the painted gore at the last moment; if no safe gap opens left, take the exit.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: What does an exit-number panel mounted at the top left of a green guide board indicate?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Spotting a left-aligned number tab warns through drivers not to camp in a fast lane that peels off.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: What does an exit-number panel mounted at the top right of a green guide board indicate?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Panel position mirrors ramp geometry, confirming at a glance that your upcoming off-ramp leaves from the right edge.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: Where do white arrows on a green highway guide board point?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Following the angled or downward white arrow lines your vehicle up with the exact ramp lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: Which class of highway uses the red, white, and blue route shield?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Test questions contrast the colorful interstate shield against black-and-white United States and Pennsylvania keystone markers.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: Which compass directions do one-digit or two-digit even-numbered interstates generally run?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Knowing even routes run cross-country helps you orient yourself quickly at unfamiliar multi-highway splits.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: Which compass directions do one-digit or two-digit odd-numbered interstates generally run?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Pairing odd route shields with north-south travel prevents taking the wrong ramp when compass tabs flash by fast.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: How do east-west interstate route numbers climb across the national map?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Higher even interstate numbers always sit farther north, making regional route geography predictable nationwide.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: How do north-south interstate route numbers climb across the national map?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Rising odd numbers from the Pacific coast to the Atlantic coast prevent mixing up interstate grid order.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: Where in Pennsylvania does the handbook locate I-seventy-six versus I-eighty and I-eighty-four?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: State routes follow the national grid, placing lower even I-seventy-six below northern I-eighty and I-eighty-four.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: Where in Pennsylvania does the handbook locate I-seventy-nine versus I-ninety-five?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Western Pittsburgh-area I-seventy-nine carries a lower odd number than eastern Philadelphia-area I-ninety-five.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: What general function do three-digit interstate highways serve?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Auxiliary three-digit routes carry urban traffic around or into metro corridors off a main parent interstate.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: What route pattern does a three-digit interstate with an even first digit usually form?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: An even prefix tells through travelers the highway reconnects at both ends to bypass downtown congestion.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Which Philadelphia route does the handbook give as an even-first-digit three-digit interstate?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Starting with the even number two signals a connecting bypass route linked to major interstates around Philadelphia.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: What route pattern does a three-digit interstate with an odd first digit usually form?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Mistaking an odd-prefix spur for a bypass can lead long-distance traffic straight into a city center.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: Which Williamsport highway does the handbook cite as an odd-first-digit spur?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Leading with odd digit one flags a single-ended feeder spur heading toward Williamsport rather than looping back.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: From what two starting points do Pennsylvania highway mile markers measure distance?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Notice that mileposts reset at the Pennsylvania state line rather than counting continuously from another state.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: At which compass ends does mile-marker numbering start at zero?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Remembering west and south as zero anchors lets you deduce travel direction solely from changing milepost numbers.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: When do highway mile-marker numbers rise, and when do they fall?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Watching two consecutive green mileposts confirms immediately whether you took the right compass ramp at night.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: What mile markers do you pass first when entering Pennsylvania from the west on I-eighty?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Crossing the Ohio line onto eastbound I-eighty starts at Mile one and climbs steadily across Pennsylvania.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: How does reading roadside mile markers help during a vehicle breakdown or emergency?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Giving dispatchers your route number, travel direction, and exact milepost gets tow trucks or troopers there faster.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: Which highway does a black-and-white United States shield displaying twenty-two identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Distinguishing the classic federal shield from an interstate or state keystone keeps route turns accurate.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: Which highway does a keystone-shaped marker displaying thirty-nine identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Pennsylvania frames numbered state highways inside a keystone silhouette, a favorite symbol question on knowledge tests.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: What does a JCT plate mounted above a numbered route marker announce?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Spotting the junction plaque early gives you time to check following mirrors and move into your turn lane.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: What does a WEST plate mounted above a U.S. Route twenty-two shield tell you?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Reassurance assemblies after intersections confirm you picked the westbound leg rather than heading the opposite way.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: What does a right-turn arrow placed beneath a WEST U.S. Route twenty-two assembly mean?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Numbered routes often bend through town intersections, so missing the lower arrow sends you off your highway.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: What does a TO plate with a U.S. Route twenty-two shield and upward arrow direct?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: A trailblazer TO plaque means you are not on that route yet, only following feeder streets toward it.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What colors and shapes do motorist service signs use, and what do they identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Scanning blue panels ahead of an exit prevents unnecessary off-ramp detours when looking for fuel or medical care.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: Which six traveler needs can blue motorist service symbols identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Simple white icons communicate gas, diesel, food, lodging, phone, or hospital access much faster than long text lists.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: What shapes and color combinations do tourist directional signs use?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Brown and blue attraction boards separate cultural or park turns from green main-highway route guidance.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: What kinds of destinations do tourist directional signs guide motorists toward?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Visitors unfamiliar with local roads often brake unexpectedly near park or museum turns, so leave extra space.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: What four roadway features do permanent pavement markings identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Painted stripes keep traffic organized continuously between upright posts, especially in rain, fog, or heavy traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: What traffic separation does yellow pavement paint always indicate?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Confusing yellow with white on a multi-lane street risks turning or merging straight into head-on traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: Where do yellow lines sit on two-lane roads versus divided highways, one-way streets, and ramps?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Seeing solid yellow along your right door means you entered a ramp or divided roadway the wrong way.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: What two boundaries do solid white pavement lines mark?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: In glare or heavy rain, tracking the right-edge white fog line keeps you centered without staring into headlights.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: What is the general crossing rule for broken traffic lines versus solid traffic lines?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Solid paint locks lane discipline near hazards and intersections while still letting vehicles turn across into driveways.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.question_text: When does a single broken yellow centerline on a two-lane road allow passing?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint grants permission only when sight distance is long and oncoming pavement is completely clear.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.question_text: Which lane does your vehicle occupy while passing across a broken yellow centerline?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.teaching_text: Every second spent left of yellow closes head-on distance at the combined speed of both vehicles.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.question_text: What passing rule applies at a double solid yellow centerline when no sign is posted?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.teaching_text: Exam questions test whether missing roadside pennants excuse passing, and painted double yellow alone forbids it completely.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.question_text: When a centerline pairs one solid and one broken yellow stripe, who may pass?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.teaching_text: Only the lane directly touching the dashed yellow stripe has enough forward sight distance to overtake safely.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.question_text: What is the rule for the driver on the solid-line side of a mixed yellow centerline?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.teaching_text: Hills or curves hide oncoming cars from the solid-stripe side even though opposing traffic has clear view.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.question_text: How may drivers use a shared center lane framed by solid outer and broken inner yellow lines?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.teaching_text: Using a two-way left-turn lane as a passing chute invites head-on crashes with opposing drivers slowing to turn.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.question_text: When may you cross broken white lane lines on an undivided multilane road?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.teaching_text: Mirrors miss cars sitting beside your rear quarter panel, so pair every lane change with a shoulder check.

sec06-card-sec06-R23.question_text: What rule and hazard apply to the double yellow centerline on an undivided multilane road?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.teaching_text: Overtaking belongs strictly in same-direction lanes; crossing central double yellow puts you head-on into fast oncoming lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-R24.question_text: Which paint colors mark the right and left edges of each roadway on a divided highway?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.teaching_text: Matching yellow on your driver side and white on your passenger side confirms legal travel direction instantly.

sec06-card-sec06-R25.question_text: May drivers cross broken white lines separating same-direction lanes on a divided limited-access highway?
sec06-card-sec06-R25.teaching_text: Dashed white stripes allow normal expressway lane changes once mirrors, blind spots, and signals are checked.

sec06-card-sec06-R26.question_text: How do painted pavement words and arrows work alongside roadside signs?
sec06-card-sec06-R26.teaching_text: Markings right in your forward scan reinforce lane rules when trucks or glare obscure post-mounted signs.

sec06-card-sec06-R27.question_text: What upcoming traffic control does STOP AHEAD pavement wording announce?
sec06-card-sec06-R27.teaching_text: Large letters painted across asphalt warn you to start braking early when trees or bends hide the octagon.

sec06-card-sec06-R28.question_text: What duty do YIELD pavement letters or a row of white triangles across your lane indicate?
sec06-card-sec06-R28.teaching_text: White triangle rows mark the exact yield point at roundabouts, channelized right turns, and mid-block crosswalks.

sec06-card-sec06-R29.question_text: What zone does large SCHOOL wording painted on the roadway announce?
sec06-card-sec06-R29.teaching_text: Lane-wide lettering grabs your eyes downward toward crosswalks where children and crossing guards step out.

sec06-card-sec06-R30.question_text: What hazard does R X R lettering painted on the lane announce?
sec06-card-sec06-R30.teaching_text: Spotting the painted crossbuck code early gives you room to listen and stop short of the rails.

sec06-card-sec06-R31.question_text: What does BIKE LANE wording painted on a roadway lane identify?
sec06-card-sec06-R31.teaching_text: Motor vehicles must not cruise or park inside a dedicated bike lane, keeping cyclists clear of doorings and bumpers.

sec06-card-sec06-R32.question_text: What rule applies when ONLY is painted with a left or right lane arrow?
sec06-card-sec06-R32.teaching_text: Driving straight out of a mandatory turn pocket sideswipes adjacent through cars expecting you to turn off.

sec06-card-sec06-R33.question_text: Where do large white pavement arrows show legal travel direction?
sec06-card-sec06-R33.teaching_text: Seeing large white arrowheads pointing back toward your hood warns immediately against a deadly wrong-way ramp entry.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: What two tire conditions should you verify before getting behind the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Bald or underinflated rubber loses grip fast on wet Pennsylvania pavement and spikes blowout risk.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: Where do you find the recommended tire pressure for your vehicle, and how should you measure it?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Sidewall numbers list maximum tire limits rather than the vehicle maker's target inflation, which trips up new drivers.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: When are tires considered cold enough for an accurate air-pressure reading?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Rolling friction heats trapped air and raises readings, hiding dangerous underinflation if you measure right after parking.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: How should you correct tire pressure when your gauge reads higher or lower than the specified number?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Both overinflation and underinflation shrink your tire contact patch, hurting braking grip and causing uneven tread wear.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: How often should you inspect your tires for wear and visible damage?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Catching sidewall bulges, cuts, or uneven wear early prevents high-speed highway blowouts far from help.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: How do you position a penny when checking tire tread depth?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Testing a deep outer rib instead of the most worn spot masks bald patches that hydroplane in rain.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: What visual result on the penny test tells you your tire still has a safe amount of tread?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Seeing all of Lincoln's head means grooves are too shallow to channel water out from under the tire.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: What happens to vehicle handling when tire tread wears below the penny-test threshold?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Worn grooves cannot clear rain or slush, turning routine braking and cornering into sudden skids.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: What roadside tools and gear should stay in your vehicle in case you get a flat tire?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: A spare tire alone will not help on a dark shoulder without lifting tools, wheel chocks, and visibility gear.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Which three vehicle fluids should you routinely check and top off according to the owner's manual?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Running dry on washer spray blinds you in winter road salt, while low oil or fuel strands you in traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: How should you position the driver's seat before shifting out of park?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Sitting too far back or too low forces awkward lunges for the brake pedal and hides hazards ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: Which parts of the seat belt system must you wear every time you drive?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Tucking the shoulder strap behind your back leaves your upper body unrestrained to slam into the steering wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: Why are unrestrained items inside the cabin dangerous during a sudden collision?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: When the car stops abruptly, unbuckled cargo keeps moving forward at highway speed and can strike occupants.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: Where should you stow heavy items, and what should you do if they must ride in the cabin?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Locking heavy gear in the trunk or strapping it down stops it from flying forward during emergency braking.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: Why should you keep the rear window shelf completely clear of stored items?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Items on the back ledge block your rearview sightline and launch straight toward heads in a hard stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: Which cabin adjustment must come first: setting the mirrors or positioning the driver's seat?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Moving your seat afterward shifts your eye angle and ruins every mirror alignment you just dialed in.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: What view should your inside rearview mirror frame once you finish adjusting it?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Tilting the inside mirror to watch passengers or yourself leaves you blind to fast-closing tailgaters behind you.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: How far outward should you angle your side mirrors to minimize blind spots?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Showing half your own car door in the glass wastes mirror width and widens adjacent-lane blind zones.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: Why can you not rely on the previous driver's mirror angles when sharing a car?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Height and posture differences change your line of sight, leaving hidden blind pockets unless you readjust.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: What is the rule on hanging air fresheners, charms, or other items from the rearview mirror while driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Swinging mirror ornaments create a moving blind spot right where pedestrians and cross traffic enter intersections.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: When is it legal to hang parking tags, permits, or placards from your rearview mirror?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Forgetting to take down a parking placard before pulling away blocks forward visibility and violates Pennsylvania law.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: What restriction applies to mounts, stickers, or accessories placed on the windshield?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Phone mounts or decals stuck in your sweep zone can hide cyclists, signals, or braking cars ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: What two hazards does keeping fresh air circulating inside the cabin help prevent?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Stale warm cabin air makes eyelids heavy, while odorless exhaust leaks can silently poison occupants without airflow.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: How high should you set the top of your head restraint?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Leaving the headrest down near your neck acts like a pivot point instead of catching your head.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: What specific protection does a properly adjusted head restraint provide in a collision?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: Rear-end impacts snap an unsupported head backward violently, causing severe whiplash when the restraint sits too low.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: When must you wear your prescription glasses or contact lenses behind the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Skipping your glasses even on a short neighborhood errand blurs street signs, brake lights, and crossing pedestrians.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: Why must you avoid sunglasses and tinted contact lenses when driving after dark?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Darkened lenses cut incoming light even further, hiding unlit pedestrians, dark pavement hazards, and lane edges.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: How do locked doors work together with your seat belt during a serious crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: Locked latches are less likely to pop open on impact, keeping occupants safely inside the protective cabin.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: Besides crash protection, how does locking your doors protect you at red lights and parking lots?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Stopping in urban traffic or dim parking areas exposes unlocked doors to strangers trying to force entry.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: What three core things can a driving distraction pull away from operating the vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Knowledge items test all three categories—cognitive, visual, and manual—because losing even one breaks safe vehicle control.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: How do eating, drinking, or smoking behind the wheel affect your ability to handle sudden hazards?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Juggling hot coffee, wrappers, or ashes ties up a steering hand right when traffic brakes hard ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: How does the Pennsylvania handbook classify tuning the radio or changing playlists while moving?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Glancing down at a touchscreen for just two seconds at highway speed sends you blind across half a football field.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: Under what strict limits may a Pennsylvania driver wear an earpiece or headphone while driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Covering both ears or blasting music blocks sirens, horns, and train bells before hazards enter your sightline.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: Does switching a phone call to speaker or Bluetooth eliminate driver distraction?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Your hands stay on the wheel, yet mental focus drifts into the conversation and causes inattention blindness.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: How can friends or other passengers riding in the car hurt your driving performance?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Turning to talk or laugh with friends pulls both your eyes and attention away from changing traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: Why should you pull over instead of reaching for a dropped or sliding item while driving?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Leaning over to grab a fallen phone pulls your eyes below the dash and yanks the steering wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.question_text: Why must tasks like texting, reading notes, or fixing hair wait until the car is parked?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.teaching_text: Composing a text or checking makeup combines visual, manual, and mental distraction at the worst possible moment.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.question_text: What danger comes from rubbernecking at a roadside crash, work crew, or activity off the roadway?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.teaching_text: Fixing your gaze on flashing lights beside the highway blinds you to brake lights stacking up directly ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.question_text: Which three essential driving abilities deteriorate when you drive tired?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.teaching_text: Drowsy brains process speed and distance late while blurry eyes miss subtle lane drift until the rumble strips hit.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: To what well-known form of impairment does the handbook compare drowsy driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Exhaustion slows reflexes and clouds risk decisions much like alcohol, even when a driver has had zero drinks.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: Staying awake for eighteen straight hours produces driving impairment comparable to what blood alcohol level?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Waking at six in the morning and driving home at midnight hits your reflexes like measurable blood alcohol.
sec07-card-sec07-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Eighteen hours equals point zero five

visual_sync.text_span: Eighteen hours equals point zero five

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: Going twenty-four straight hours without sleep impairs a driver roughly like what blood alcohol concentration?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: An all-nighter leaves you worse off behind the wheel than an adult above Pennsylvania's legal alcohol limit.
sec07-card-sec07-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Twenty-four hours equals point one zero

visual_sync.text_span: Twenty-four hours equals point one zero

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Can an exhausted driver always tell the exact moment they are about to nod off?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Willpower cannot beat microsleeps because the brain shuts down for brief seconds without sending a final warning.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: How long does a driver need to doze off for a crash to turn deadly?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Four seconds with eyes closed at highway speed sends an unsteered car across oncoming lanes or into trees.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Below how many hours of nightly sleep do teen drivers see a higher crash risk?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Chronic school-week sleep debt stacks up fast in young drivers, dulling hazard detection on early commutes.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: What does the handbook say to do if you start feeling drowsy behind the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Blasting cold air or loud music only masks fatigue briefly instead of fixing your brain's need for rest.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: How often does the handbook recommend having your eyesight professionally checked?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Gradual eyesight shifts sneak up unnoticed until routine exams catch blurry distance reading or shrinking side vision.
sec07-card-sec07-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Eye check one to two years

visual_sync.text_span: Eye check one to two years

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: Which three visual skills can health conditions or aging quietly degrade without you realizing it?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Because visual decline happens slowly day by day, drivers rarely notice missing side hazards or misjudged gaps.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: If your license carries a corrective-lens requirement, how often must you wear your glasses or contacts?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Driving without a mandated lens restriction violates your license terms and leaves hazards blurred at speed.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: What critical road warnings can your sense of hearing catch before you ever see them?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Buildings, hills, and blind corners often hide ambulances or locomotives long after their sirens and horns sound.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: How can everyday aches like a stiff neck or sore knee affect your driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: Painful movement tempts drivers to skip shoulder checks or hesitate when stomping hard on the brake pedal.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.question_text: Which three major medical conditions does the handbook highlight as serious risks for safe driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.teaching_text: Sudden blackouts, blood-sugar crashes, or cardiac episodes can incapacitate a driver mid-lane without warning.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.question_text: What legal duty do Pennsylvania doctors have when they diagnose a patient with a driving-impairing condition?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.teaching_text: Mandatory reporting lets state reviewers evaluate medical fitness before an untreated condition causes a highway blackout crash.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration is a driver under age twenty-one legally considered under the influence in Pennsylvania?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.teaching_text: Pennsylvania enforces near-zero tolerance for underage drivers, meaning even part of one drink can trigger DUI charges.
sec07-card-sec07-R15.must_match_memory_hook: Under twenty-one limit point zero two

visual_sync.text_span: Under twenty-one limit point zero two

sec07-card-sec07-R16.question_text: How much alcohol does it take to start weakening your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.teaching_text: Impairment starts long before slurred speech appears, quietly eroding mental sharpness after a modest amount of alcohol.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.question_text: What happens to your driving mistakes and core control skills as blood alcohol concentration climbs?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.teaching_text: Rising blood alcohol attacks vision, timing, and steering together, compounding small lane mistakes into severe crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.question_text: What dangerous mismatch does alcohol create between how capable a driver feels and how well they actually drive?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.teaching_text: Impaired judgment tricks drinkers into believing they are totally fine to drive right as their coordination falls apart.

sec07-card-sec07-R19.question_text: What is Pennsylvania's legal blood alcohol limit for adult drivers aged twenty-one and older?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.teaching_text: Do not confuse the adult threshold of point zero eight percent with the strict underage point zero two rule.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.question_text: Does staying under the legal blood alcohol limit guarantee that you are safe to drive?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.teaching_text: Reaction speed and hazard perception begin slipping well below illegal per-se numbers, making sub-limit driving hazardous.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.question_text: According to the Pennsylvania handbook, how much alcohol is genuinely safe to drink before driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.teaching_text: Every drink chips away at split-second judgment and braking speed, leaving zero as the lone risk-free choice.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.question_text: What personal and situational factors change how high your blood alcohol level rises from drinking?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.teaching_text: Counting drinks fails because stomach food, body size, health, and medicines alter how quickly alcohol enters your bloodstream.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.question_text: Why can two people who each have one drink still consume very different amounts of pure alcohol?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.teaching_text: Craft beers, mixed cocktails, and heavy pours often pack far more pure alcohol than a standard serving.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.question_text: What serving sizes of eighty-proof liquor, regular beer, and wine each count as one standard drink?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.teaching_text: Learners often assume beer or wine is milder, forgetting each standard pour carries equivalent pure alcohol.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.question_text: Roughly how long does it take an average-weight person's body to process the alcohol in a single standard drink?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.teaching_text: Your liver clears alcohol at a slow fixed pace, so back-to-back drinks stack up rapidly in your blood.

sec07-card-sec07-R26.question_text: What caution does the handbook attach to the one-drink-per-hour pacing rule for legal-age drinkers?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.teaching_text: Smaller bodies, stronger pours, and slower metabolism mean one-per-hour pacing can still leave a driver dangerously impaired.

sec07-card-sec07-R27.question_text: How does smaller body size affect alcohol concentration in the bloodstream?
sec07-card-sec07-R27.teaching_text: Less body water means the exact same drink reaches a higher blood concentration than in a heavier person.

sec07-card-sec07-R28.question_text: If a woman and a man weigh the same and drink identically over the same timeframe, how can their blood alcohol levels compare?
sec07-card-sec07-R28.teaching_text: Biological differences in body composition and enzymes mean matching a male friend drink-for-drink pushes blood alcohol higher.

sec07-card-sec07-R29.question_text: Do strong coffee, energy drinks, or a cold shower actually lower your blood alcohol concentration?
sec07-card-sec07-R29.teaching_text: Caffeine or icy water only creates a wide-awake impaired driver while blood alcohol stays completely unchanged.

sec07-card-sec07-R30.question_text: What dual responsibility do you have regarding driving after drinking—both for yourself and for others?
sec07-card-sec07-R30.teaching_text: Refusing to drive impaired and arranging safe rides for friends keeps impaired cars off the road entirely.

sec07-card-sec07-R31.question_text: Which categories of drugs and medications are capable of impairing your driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R31.teaching_text: Drivers often forget that legal pharmacy prescriptions and everyday allergy tablets can impair reflexes just like street drugs.

sec07-card-sec07-R32.question_text: What happens when someone mixes medications or other drugs with alcohol before driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R32.teaching_text: Alcohol and drugs amplify each other's sedating or dizzying effects rather than merely adding together mildly.

sec07-card-sec07-R33.question_text: How does marijuana impair the specific skills needed to control a vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-R33.teaching_text: Delayed braking reflexes and distorted gap perception cause drivers to misjudge speeds at intersections and highway merges.

sec07-card-sec07-R34.question_text: How can stimulants like cocaine or methamphetamine alter a driver's behavior in traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-R34.teaching_text: Harsh central nervous system stimulants trigger erratic speeding, weaving, and hostile risk-taking behind the wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-R35.question_text: What two side effects from sedative medications make driving dangerous?
sec07-card-sec07-R35.teaching_text: Calming medications depress nervous-system alertness, leaving drivers lightheaded and prone to nodding off mid-trip.

sec07-card-sec07-R36.question_text: How can opioid pain medications affect a driver behind the wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-R36.teaching_text: Prescription painkillers dull central nervous responses, stretching stopping distances when sudden traffic hazards appear.

sec07-card-sec07-R37.question_text: Which common household or pharmacy remedies can unexpectedly hurt your driving skills?
sec07-card-sec07-R37.teaching_text: Everyday cold syrups and allergy pills carry lingering grogginess or jitteriness that catches daytime drivers off guard.

sec07-card-sec07-R38.question_text: What quick check should you perform on any medication container before getting in the driver's seat?
sec07-card-sec07-R38.teaching_text: Fine-print warnings alert you to hidden drowsiness, blurred vision, or dizziness before you merge into fast traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-R39.question_text: Who should you consult before driving if you are unsure how a medicine might affect you?
sec07-card-sec07-R39.teaching_text: Medical professionals can spot risky drug interactions and tell you whether you should stay off the road.

sec07-card-sec07-R40.question_text: What does a medication label warning against operating heavy machinery mean for drivers?
sec07-card-sec07-R40.teaching_text: Many people picture factory equipment, forgetting a two-ton passenger car moving at highway speed counts directly.

sec07-card-sec07-R41.question_text: What precaution should you take with your doctor whenever you start a brand-new prescription?
sec07-card-sec07-R41.teaching_text: Your body's reaction to a first dose can be unpredictable, so knowing side effects upfront prevents mid-commute surprises.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: Why should you drop your speed before starting a turn rather than braking mid-corner?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Carrying too much speed into a corner pushes the car wide into adjacent lanes and leaves zero braking margin.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: What should you scan for on the street you are turning onto, and what lane directions must you obey?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Drivers focused solely on signal lights often miss pedestrians stepping off the curb or mandatory lane-arrow markings.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Where within your lane should you position your car for a left turn versus a right turn on a two-lane, two-way road?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Swinging wide before turning invites impatient drivers behind you to squeeze past on the side you are turning toward.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: Which lanes must you start from when turning left or right on a multilane road without special turn-lane arrows?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Cutting across an adjacent travel lane mid-turn causes classic sideswipe crashes with straight-moving traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: Which lane must you enter first when turning onto a road that has multiple lanes moving your way?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Drifting wide into a far lane during a turn puts you right into the path of opposite-side turners.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: When is it safe to move over into a different lane after making a turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Switching lanes halfway through an intersection hides your move in blind spots and surprises fast cross-street traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: What is the sole legal use of a center lane bordered by solid yellow outer lines and broken inner lines?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Treating a two-way center turn lane as a passing or cruising lane sets up a head-on crash.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Which directions of traffic are allowed to pull into a shared center turn lane to start a left turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Remembering that oncoming cars have equal rights to enter the same middle strip keeps your eyes scanning ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: How may a driver turning left out of a side street legally use a shared center turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Using the middle refuge lets you cross one direction of traffic first and merge smoothly when a gap opens.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Which two sources of conflicting vehicles must you watch for as you pull into a shared center turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: An oncoming driver braking for a left or a car nosing out from a driveway can claim that same space.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: What traffic streams must you check before turning left out of a driveway into a shared center turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: You must clear fast through lanes coming from your left while making sure neither direction already occupies the center.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: How many seconds ahead should you signal left before moving into a shared center turn lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Early blinker notice warns following drivers you are slowing and moving left before your wheels cross the line.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: Why is it dangerous to pull into a shared center turn lane far ahead of your turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Cruising down the shared middle strip raises the odds of meeting an oncoming left-turner nose to nose.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: How should your vehicle sit inside the center turn lane while waiting to turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Leaving your rear bumper jutting into the travel lane invites high-speed rear-corner hits from passing traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What two checks must be clear before you complete your left turn out of a shared center lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Rushing a tight gap can trap your car broadside across oncoming lanes if a driveway or crosswalk slows you.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: What four steps summarize executing a clean, legal turn from start to finish?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Skipping any link in that four-step sequence causes unpredictable lane swings or sudden braking surprises.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: What overarching safety condition must always be met before making a U-turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Because swinging across both directions takes time and road width, any conflict with approaching cars makes it illegal.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: How far away must approaching vehicles be—and what visibility is required—to make a legal U-turn in Pennsylvania?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Five hundred feet gives fast oncoming and following drivers enough sight distance to spot your wide turnaround.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: At which three road locations or posted zones are U-turns strictly prohibited?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Curves and hillcrests hide fast oncoming traffic until impact is unavoidable, while regulatory signs ban tight-spot turnarounds.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: What conditions must you satisfy before turning right at a steady red light?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Rolling through a red right turn without stopping first is a top road-test failure and endangers crosswalks.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: When is turning left at a steady red light legal in Pennsylvania?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Watch out for the classic trap of turning left on red from a two-way street, which remains illegal.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: Which three real-time conditions determine how big a traffic gap you need to cross a roadway safely?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Wet or icy pavement spins your tires on takeoff, demanding a much wider gap than dry summer asphalt.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: Under what single condition is it safe to stop halfway while crossing a divided street?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Waiting in a narrow median break leaves your hood or trunk sticking out into high-speed through lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: What should you confirm about your exit path before committing to cross or turn through an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Getting halted mid-turn by a crosswalk pedestrian leaves the side of your car stranded across live traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: What must you do at a green light if backed-up traffic ahead would trap you inside the intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Pulling into backed-up traffic on green causes gridlock when the signal flips and traps you across cross traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: Why should you wait before pulling out in front of an approaching car that has its turn signal on?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Drivers frequently forget an active blinker or plan to turn into the next driveway past yours, causing T-bone collisions.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: Why do intersections near hillcrests or curves require extra caution before pulling across?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Blind crests and bends shorten sightlines in both directions, giving oncoming drivers minimal time to brake for you.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: What do you need in the highway lane beside you before merging into moving traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Forcing your way into a tight cluster makes highway drivers slam their brakes or swerve across lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: What two purposes do highway acceleration lanes serve for entering drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Dawdling or stopping on the entrance strip forces a dangerous slow-speed merge into sixty-mile-per-hour traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: Are you allowed to overtake a slower car ahead of you while still inside a highway acceleration lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Jumping around the car ahead on an entrance ramp puts both vehicles into a blind, competing merge.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: What four actions take you cleanly from an acceleration lane into highway traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Matching highway pace before sliding into your chosen gap prevents sudden speed drops for everyone behind you.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Why must you use extra caution if passing near crossroads or shopping-center entrances?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Drivers pulling out of strip malls often look left only, never expecting an overtaking car in their lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: Why is overtaking on a two-lane, two-way road one of the highest-risk maneuvers in driving?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Closing speed doubles when two cars approach nose-to-nose, turning a slight distance miscalculation into a head-on crash.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: At forty-five miles per hour, how much clear road ahead do you need to safely pass a slower vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Both you and any oncoming vehicle cover ground rapidly during a pass, eating up a quarter mile in seconds.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: What must you confirm ahead of a line of slower cars before trying to pass multiple vehicles?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Pulling out beside a tight line of cars with nowhere to tuck back in strands you facing oncoming traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: How does darkness distort your perception of oncoming vehicles when passing at night?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Without daytime roadside landmarks, twin oncoming beams look deceptively distant until the car closes in fast.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: What road layout allows you to legally pass another vehicle on the right?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Multilane corridors keep right-side overtaking inside marked travel lanes rather than squeezing onto narrow edges.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: How close to an intersection or railroad crossing is passing banned unless traffic controls specifically allow it?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Turning cars at crossroads and trains at tracks create lethal side conflicts if you pull into the oncoming lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: Within what distance of a bridge, elevated roadway, or tunnel must you stay in your lane instead of passing?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Narrowed shoulders, bridge walls, and dark tunnel portals eliminate escape room if an oncoming vehicle appears.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: Why is passing illegal on or near a curve or hillcrest with limited forward visibility?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Passing blind into hidden oncoming pavement gambles your life that nobody is approaching just beyond the crest.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: May you use the paved shoulder of a multilane highway to pass slower traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Highway shoulders hold broken-down cars, road debris, and emergency responders rather than clear passing pavement.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: What legal controls and roadside hazards should you check ahead before starting a pass?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Solid yellow lines, no-passing pennants, or hidden side driveways can turn a routine overtake into an illegal collision.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: Why must you check both your mirrors and blind spot right before pulling out to pass?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: Swinging left while a faster car behind you is already overtaking causes an instant sideswipe in the passing lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: Once behind you is clear, what two steps come right before moving into the passing lane?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: Signaling well ahead alerts both the driver you are overtaking and anyone behind you before you shift laterally.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: What mirror landmark tells you that you have cleared a passed vehicle far enough to return to your lane?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Cutting back in before both headlights appear in your inside mirror clips their front bumper or forces panic braking.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Does Pennsylvania intersection law grant an absolute right to go, or define who must yield?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Permit questions love testing that nobody ever owns the road outright, because traffic statutes only assign yielding duties.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: What must you do if another driver fails to yield when traffic law says they should?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Insisting on technical priority when another car blows a yield turns a minor mistake into a serious collision.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: When must you yield to pedestrians crossing at an intersection without traffic signals?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Every corner has a legal pedestrian crossing zone even when no white paint appears on the asphalt.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: Must you yield to pedestrians inside a marked crosswalk located between intersections?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Trail crossings, campuses, and shopping corridors place painted walkways mid-street where drivers least expect to brake.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: Who goes first when your vehicle crosses a sidewalk to enter or leave an alley or driveway?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Fences, hedges, and parked cars hide joggers and strollers along sidewalks where drivers pull across curb cuts.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Who has priority when you turn across a crosswalk where pedestrians are crossing with the signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Sharing the same green phase makes turning vehicles the primary threat to people legally crossing on walk.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: What is your yielding duty toward a blind pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Guide dogs and white canes signal that a traveler relies on sound and consistent driver yielding to cross unharmed.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: Without a turn arrow or police direction, who must a left-turning driver yield to?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Cutting across opposing straight-through lanes misjudges closing speed and causes severe passenger-side T-bone impacts.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: Who holds priority at the entrance of a roundabout?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Keeping interior traffic moving without interruption prevents sudden stops and gridlock inside the circular roadway.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: When two drivers on different roads reach an uncontrolled intersection at roughly the same time, who yields?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Without signs, lights, or officers, yielding to the car on your right breaks ties cleanly from every approach.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What must you wait for before pulling onto a public highway from a driveway, alley, or private road?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Through traffic on public streets travels at full cruising speed and never expects cars darting out of hidden driveways.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: How is the order of movement decided at a four-way stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Coming to a full halt and noting who reached their stop bar first keeps four-way intersections orderly.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: Who yields when two vehicles stop at a four-way intersection at the exact same moment?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Letting the driver to your right go first settles ties instantly without awkward hand-waving or dual launches.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: Can two opposing vehicles at a four-way stop move at the same time?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Facing cars going straight share parallel paths, though either driver turning across the other requires extra caution.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Why should you scan lane-assignment signs and pavement arrows well ahead of an intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Getting into your turn or through lane blocks ahead avoids dangerous last-second swerves across solid white lines.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: What must you do if you end up in a marked turn-only lane when you meant to go straight?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Forcing your way straight from a turn pocket cuts directly across drivers expecting you to peel off.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: What must you do if you want to turn at an intersection while occupying a through-only lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Hooking a sudden turn from a straight-only lane sideswipes cars beside you in the actual turn lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: How must you steer when turning from one of two side-by-side left-turn lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Drifting wide mid-turn puts your fender straight into the car turning simultaneously right beside you.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: What visual clue from parked cars suggests a cross street is one-way?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Spotting bumpers all pointed the same way along both curbs backs up signage before you accidentally turn wrong-way.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: What makes up a divided highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Treating each side as its own one-way street helps you check traffic from the right direction at median crossings.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: From which direction do you need a safe gap when turning right onto a divided highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Near-side lanes on a divided road carry traffic exclusively from your left, letting you focus gap timing there after scanning.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: How do you check gaps step-by-step when turning left onto a divided highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Breaking a divided crossing into near-side left traffic and far-side right traffic prevents turning into the wrong roadway.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: What happens if you turn left before passing the median divider at a divided highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Mistaking the near roadway for a two-way street puts you head-on against traffic, which WRONG WAY and DO NOT ENTER signs guard against.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: Roughly how big a gap in both directions does crossing a thirty-mile-per-hour street from a two-way stop take?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Judging a full city block or counting six seconds each way gives your car time to accelerate completely clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: What scan order and time gap from the left do you need before turning right onto a cross street?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Turning right requires accelerating up to road speed, which takes roughly two seconds longer than simply driving straight across.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: What two traffic conditions must you confirm before starting a left turn at an intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Verifying both oncoming spacing and halted side-street cars keeps you from getting T-boned mid-arc.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: How many seconds of clearance from the right do you need when turning left from a minor road onto a major road?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Crossing near lanes and accelerating up to major-road speed takes longer than any other turn, demanding nine full seconds.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: How do two opposing drivers both turning left avoid tangling paths in the intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Turning in front of each other into the lane closest to the yellow line keeps sightlines open and paths separate.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: When is it safe to start turning left across multiple oncoming lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Starting a turn while a stopped truck hides an outer through lane is a classic blind-lane crash setup.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does a jughandle ramp let you complete a left turn off a major road?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Routing left-turning traffic off the right side eliminates dangerous stopped queues in fast left-hand highway lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: In which direction does traffic move around a roundabout, and how do drivers enter and exit?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Right-in, counterclockwise, right-out geometry eliminates head-on left turns inside modern circular intersections.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Which two traffic controls mark the entrance to a roundabout?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Spotting the red-and-white triangle and dashed pavement line shows exactly where to wait for circulating vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: How do most roundabouts help approaching drivers identify which leg leads to their route?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Reading destination diagrams before reaching the circle lets you pick the proper lane and count exits calmly.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: How should you approach a roundabout before reaching the circular roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Pedestrian crossings sit one car-length back from the yield line, so easing speed early protects walkers first.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: Which direction do you check at a roundabout yield line, and when may you enter?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Because roundabout traffic flows counterclockwise, all conflicting vehicles inside the ring approach from your left.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: How should you travel once inside a roundabout until reaching your street?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Stopping mid-circle to read street names or wave entrants in causes immediate rear-end collisions behind you.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: Which turn signal should you activate as your roundabout exit comes up?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Blinking right tells waiting drivers on the next leg that you are peeling off rather than crossing their nose.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: At which two points of a roundabout trip must you yield to pedestrians?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Drivers remember the entry crosswalk easily yet often forget another pedestrian crossing waits right across the exit leg.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: What must you do if an emergency vehicle approaches before you enter a roundabout?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Pulling over before the splitter island keeps the narrow circular lane wide open for fire trucks and ambulances.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: What should you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already circulating inside a roundabout?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Stopping inside the curved single-lane ring traps large emergency rigs behind you with nowhere to pass.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: Which two ways may a bicyclist navigate a roundabout, and what rules govern riding in the lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Cyclists who stay on the roadway claim the travel lane and follow identical right-of-way rules as motor vehicles.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.question_text: Are you allowed to pass a bicyclist riding in the travel lane inside a roundabout?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.teaching_text: Curved roundabout lanes are intentionally narrow to slow cars down, leaving zero safe room to squeeze past a bike.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.question_text: Which two roundabout features help pedestrians cross each approach leg safely?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.teaching_text: Raised triangular islands split entering and exiting traffic so walkers only have to judge one direction at a time.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.question_text: What can happen to your vehicle if you enter a curve going too fast?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.teaching_text: Inertia wants to keep two tons of steel moving straight, overpowering tire grip if entry speed is too high.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.question_text: Which combination of road geometry and surface conditions requires the biggest drop in speed?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.teaching_text: Tight bends demand peak sideways tire friction just when rain or ice slashes pavement traction to a fraction.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.question_text: When should you reduce speed for an upcoming curve?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.teaching_text: Braking hard after turning the wheel shifts weight and overloads front tires, triggering skids mid-bend.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.question_text: How do standard curve warning signs differ from warnings for a sharp ninety-degree turn?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.teaching_text: Spotting a wide yellow rectangle with a bold directional arrow warns that the road bends abruptly at a right angle.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.question_text: How do roadside chevron signs help drivers along sharp bends?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.teaching_text: Reflective arrowheads trace the outer edge of tight bends at night or in fog when pavement lines disappear.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.question_text: Where in your lane should you position your vehicle on a right curve versus a left curve?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.teaching_text: Hugging slightly right on a right-hand bend adds buffer from oncoming drivers cutting across the yellow centerline.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.question_text: How should your speed change as a curve gets sharper?
