sec10-card-sec10-R21.teaching_text: Tighter turning radii multiply lateral force rapidly, requiring deeper deceleration before turn-in.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.question_text: Why must you keep a close eye on opposing traffic while rounding a curve?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.teaching_text: An oncoming driver entering too fast can drift across the double yellow right into your path mid-corner.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.question_text: Where should your eyes look to steer smoothly through a curve or series of S-bends?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.teaching_text: Your hands naturally follow your eyes, so scanning far along the inside edge smooths steering through linked bends.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Which three signs help keep you from mistaking a highway exit ramp for an entrance ramp?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Interchange ramps sit side by side, and spotting DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, and ONE WAY panels prevents head-on ramp entry.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: What optional green sign sometimes marks a highway entrance ramp?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Because green HIGHWAY ENTRANCE panels are not posted at every interchange, you still must verify ramp pavement lines and restriction signs.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: How should white and yellow pavement edge lines sit relative to your car on a highway ramp?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Seeing yellow on your right and white on your left is an instant warning that you are heading backward down a one-way ramp.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Who yields when entering and exiting drivers share the same highway weaving lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Drivers leaving the freeway are shedding high speed and need clear room to peel off before new cars merge onto the mainline.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: How should you use an acceleration lane and check traffic before merging onto a highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Building toward freeway speed while combining your side mirror and an over-the-shoulder glance eliminates deadly blind-spot merges.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: When should you move into a highway exit lane, and when should you start slowing down?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Hitting the brakes while still in a fast through lane catches trailing highway traffic completely off guard.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: What is the only safe and legal choice if you overshoot your highway exit?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Stopping, backing up, diving across lanes, or cutting across the median at freeway speed causes catastrophic multi-car pileups.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: What does a yellow warning speed sign posted along an exit ramp tell you?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Tight cloverleaf loops shed highway traction fast, and exceeding the ramp advisory speed risks rolling or sliding off the bend.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Roughly how many feet per second does a vehicle cover at sixty-five miles per hour?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Looking down at a screen for three seconds at sixty-five blinds you across an entire football field of highway.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: How should you handle lane changes and turn signals when passing on a multi-lane highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Sweeping across two or three lanes in one diagonal move hides cars merging into that same middle lane from the opposite side.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: How can a highway driver safely help someone merging from an entrance ramp?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Sliding left opens the right lane smoothly, provided you mirror-and-shoulder check first so courtesy never causes a left-lane sideswipe.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: What visual habit triggers highway hypnosis on long drives?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Locking your gaze straight ahead lulls your brain into a trance, whereas sweeping mirrors and road edges keeps reactions sharp.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: What is the maximum legal distance from the curb when parking parallel along a Pennsylvania street?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Leaving your tires more than a foot off the curb sticks your driver-side doors into active travel lanes and fails road tests.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: Where should you position your vehicle when parking along a road that has no curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Getting all four tires well onto the shoulder keeps fast rural traffic safely clear of your parked vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: What three precautions are required if you have no choice except to leave a vehicle on the roadway?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Stopping below a hill crest or blind bend hides your car until drivers are too close to brake.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: Which way must your parked vehicle face, and what else must you ensure before walking away?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Parking nose-in against oncoming traffic requires crossing live opposing lanes both to park and to pull back out.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Which brake and gear settings secure automatic versus manual vehicles when parked?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Combining the parking brake with Park on an automatic or First or Reverse on a stick prevents runaway rollaways.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking downhill next to a curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Pointing tires toward the curb lets the raised concrete catch the right front tire immediately if the brakes slip.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking uphill beside a curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Uphill with a curb is the lone left-turn case so a backward roll hooks the back of your front tire against the curb.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: Which way must your front wheels point when parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Without a concrete lip to catch a tire, pointing right ensures any rollaway angles off the shoulder instead of into traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: May you stop or park in the street alongside a vehicle already parked at the curb?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Double parking chokes an active travel lane, forces sudden lane changes behind you, and pins the curbed driver in.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Are stopping, standing, or parking allowed on sidewalks, on crosswalks, or inside intersections?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Blocking walkways or corners forces pedestrians out into live moving traffic where drivers cannot see them.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: What rule governs stopping, standing, or parking beside or across from street excavations or roadwork?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Narrowed work lanes leave zero spare width for parked cars without pinching traffic into crews and machinery.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Where is stopping, standing, or parking prohibited on bridges, elevated highways, and tunnels?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Enclosed tunnels and shoulderless spans trap disabled queues with no escape lane for approaching traffic or emergency rigs.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: How far must you stay from the nearest rail when parking near a railroad crossing?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Parking closer than fifty feet blocks crossing warning lights and hides approaching locomotives from other drivers.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: May ordinary drivers stop, stand, or park in the median or crossovers of a divided highway?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Paved median crossovers exist strictly for police and emergency turnarounds, never for civilian rest stops.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: When may you disregard official signs prohibiting stopping or parking?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Outside genuine breakdowns or a uniformed officer's hand signal, posted curb bans apply every single minute.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: What stopping, standing, and parking rule applies across public or private driveways?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Even sitting behind the wheel idling across a curb cut traps residents and emergency access illegally.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: How many feet of clearance must you leave when parking near a fire hydrant in Pennsylvania?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Firefighters need immediate unobstructed hose access, making the fifteen-foot hydrant rule a classic permit test number.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: Within how many feet of an intersection crosswalk are stopping, standing, and parking banned?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Daylighting twenty feet before corners keeps parked SUVs from hiding pedestrians stepping off the curb.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: How far back must you park from a stop sign, yield sign, flashing beacon, or roadside signal?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: Tall vehicles parked closer than thirty feet hide critical stop and yield panels from approaching traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: How close may you park to the driveway entrance of a fire station?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Wide ladder trucks need a twenty-foot swing radius on both sides of the bay apron to turn out fast.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: What parking rule protects urban streetcar and trolley routes?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.teaching_text: Rail-bound trolleys cannot steer an inch around an overhanging bumper, stalling an entire transit line.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.question_text: When are stopping, standing, or parking allowed along a limited-access expressway?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.teaching_text: Freeway shoulders are emergency breakdown zones, never places to check texts, swap drivers, or read maps.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.question_text: Where do you line up beside the front car to begin parallel parking at a right-hand curb?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.teaching_text: Starting level and two feet away gives your front fender room to swing out without clipping the car beside you.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.question_text: How should your front wheels be turned as you start backing slowly into a right-curb parallel spot?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.teaching_text: Cranking right first angles the tail of your car cleanly toward the open curb pocket.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.question_text: At what visual landmark do you straighten your wheels and back straight during a parallel park?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.teaching_text: Straightening right as your front door clears their rear bumper drives your rear tire cleanly toward the curb line.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.question_text: Which way do you steer once your front end clears the leading vehicle's rear bumper?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.teaching_text: Cutting left after clearing their bumper tucks your nose into the stall without scraping their quarter panel.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.question_text: How do you finish and center your vehicle inside a parallel-parking space?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.teaching_text: Pulling ahead with wheels turned right squares the car parallel to the curb with room for neighbors to exit.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.question_text: What steps secure your vehicle and protect passing traffic right before you step out street-side?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.teaching_text: Scanning behind before cracking your door stops cyclists and passing cars from slamming into an open driver door.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: What three types of road operations and what color traffic controls mark a Pennsylvania work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Recognizing orange cones, barrels, and temporary signs right away alerts you that normal lane patterns and speeds are changing.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: At least how far ahead of the work area might warning signs, vehicles, or message boards start appearing?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Spotting advance boards two hundred feet or more upstream gives you breathing room to lift off the gas smoothly.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Once you pass the very first work-zone warning, which four things demand your close attention?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Fixating only on the car ahead blinds you to workers stepping near cones or heavy machines swinging toward lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: When are you allowed to pass a moving road-work operation?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Line-painting or patching convoys shift lanes unpredictably, so overtaking without a crew signal invites a sideswipe.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: What makes a work zone active, and which three roadway changes might you encounter inside one?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Tight concrete barriers, milled grooves, and sudden lane jogs leave zero margin for drifting or speeding near crews.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: Who gets the right-of-way inside a Pennsylvania work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Dump trucks and foot crews enter travel lanes with limited sightlines, so forcing your way past risks deadly collisions.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Why are daytime running lights not enough when driving through a Pennsylvania work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Daytime running lamps often leave your taillights dark, whereas switching on full headlights makes both ends visible in dust.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: How do fines and license consequences escalate for speeding or certain violations inside an active work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Active-zone tickets hit twice as hard financially and can strip your driving privilege outright when workers are endangered.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: What simple route choice does the handbook suggest to dodge work-zone backups?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Detouring onto an alternate road keeps traffic volume lower around roadside crews and saves you stop-and-go frustration.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: Should you use cruise control while driving through a work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Traffic inside orange barrels can stop without warning, and manual pedal control shaves precious split seconds off braking.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: How should you adjust your normal following distance inside a work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Rear-end crashes are the top work-zone collision type because drivers follow too closely when traffic bunches up.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: When should you get ready to move over if a work-zone lane is closing ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Racing to the nose of the cones triggers sudden braking waves and squeezes neighboring drivers who already merged.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: What lane rule applies when you see a solid white line inside a work zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Weaving across solid work-zone stripes puts your car into narrowed chutes where barriers and crews sit inches away.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: How should you keep moving past active road work instead of slowing down to watch?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Gawking at machinery takes your eyes off brake lights ahead and sparks chain-reaction rear-end crashes behind you.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: Why must you never pull up and stop inside a work zone to ask road crews for directions?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Halting in an active chute blocks live traffic and pulls a worker's focus away from moving equipment.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: Whose instructions win when a work-zone flagger contradicts a regular traffic light or sign?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Flaggers see single-lane alternating traffic and backing trucks that fixed lights or permanent signs cannot account for.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: How can a flagger trigger police enforcement against an aggressive, speeding, or unsafe driver?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Even without a patrol car in sight, a flagger's written report can bring a citation straight to your mailbox.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: How should you check railroad tracks as you approach, even when the crossing lights stay dark?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Crossing signals can malfunction or lack gates altogether, so your own eyes are the final safeguard against trains.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: After one train clears a crossing with multiple tracks, when is it safe to pull forward?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: The caboose or tail car of the first train can hide a fast second train barreling down the next track.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: What check should you still make at a single railroad track right after a train passes?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Maintenance railcars or a closely following train on the same line can catch impatient drivers off guard.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: Are you allowed to pass another vehicle as you approach or cross railroad tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Swinging around a slowing car near tracks can blind you to a train or trap you against a lowering gate.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: When traffic ahead is backed up beyond a railroad crossing, where must you hold your car?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Creeping onto the rails behind stopped cars leaves nowhere to go if warning bells start ringing.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: What should you do right away if your car gets trapped on railroad tracks with a train coming?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: No vehicle is worth your life, and getting well away keeps flying crash debris from hitting you.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: Where must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Even unmarked corner crossings carry pedestrian protections, so rolling through turns without yielding violates right-of-way law.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: What must you do before making a permitted right turn on a red light?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Drivers staring left for oncoming cars frequently miss someone stepping off the right-hand curb directly into their bumper.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: How should you adjust your driving whenever children are near the roadway?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Kids chase balls or dart from between parked cars without checking traffic, and smaller bodies hide below hood height.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: How should you respond when older adults or pedestrians with disabilities are crossing the street?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Creeping forward or revving impatiently pressures slower walkers who may need past the signal change to reach the curb.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: Who must you specifically check for before shifting into reverse and backing up?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Rear pillars and high trunks create blind zones directly behind your bumper in driveways and parking lots.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: How must you react when you spot a blind pedestrian with a cane, guide dog, or human guide?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Honking startles guide animals and disorients someone navigating by sound rather than eye contact.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: What should you do before passing a vehicle stopped ahead of you in traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: A stopped car or van in the next lane often screens a pedestrian stepping across right into your path.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: Why should you avoid waving a pedestrian across the street, especially mid-block or at unmarked crossings?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Your polite hand wave can lure a walker straight into the path of a driver in the next lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: On flat pavement, how much longer does passing a large truck take compared with passing a car?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Tractor-trailers stretch far longer than sedans, requiring noticeably more clear road ahead on two-lane highways.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: How do uphill climbs and downhill grades change a large truck's speed when you plan a pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Starting a pass near a crest can backfire when gravity accelerates a heavy rig downhill right beside you.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: How should you position your car, pace your pass, and grip the wheel while overtaking a truck?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Hanging out beside trailer wheels leaves you in a huge No-Zone where wind buffets push light cars sideways.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: When is it safe to pull back in front of a truck you just passed, and what should your speed do?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: Cutting back in early slices off a heavy rig's braking cushion, and lifting off the gas invites a rear-end hit.
sec12-card-sec12-F35.must_match_memory_hook: See headlights in rearview, hold speed

visual_sync.text_span: See headlights in rearview, hold speed

sec12-card-sec12-F36.question_text: At highway speeds, up to how long can a complete, safe pass around a large truck take?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.teaching_text: Half a minute at highway speed covers nearly half a mile, so never start a tight pass near exits.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.question_text: What speed adjustment should you make as you approach or pass someone riding a bicycle?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.teaching_text: High-speed wind blasts from passing mirrors can knock a lightweight bicycle off balance toward your tires.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.question_text: What braking mistake must you avoid right after overtaking a bicyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.teaching_text: Overtaking a rider only to slam the brakes for a driveway or turn forces the cyclist straight into your rear.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.question_text: When is the only time you should sound your horn close to a bicyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.teaching_text: A sudden close horn blast startles an unprotected rider and can make them swerve directly into traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.question_text: How much lane width are motorcycles and mopeds entitled to use on the road?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.teaching_text: Squeezing beside a rider inside the same lane leaves them nowhere to swerve around potholes, gravel, or wind.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.question_text: Why shouldn't you pull out in front of a motorcycle just because its turn signal is blinking?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.teaching_text: Many motorcycle blinkers do not self-cancel after lane changes, so pulling out on a leftover flash causes T-bone crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.question_text: Why might a motorcycle or moped change speed or lane position without warning ahead of you?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.teaching_text: Oil slicks, railroad grates, or small road debris that cars barely feel can dump a two-wheeled rider instantly.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.question_text: What minimum following time cushion belongs behind a motorcycle or moped, and when should you add more?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.teaching_text: Light bikes stop faster than passenger cars and lose traction quicker on wet leaves, gravel, or rain.

sec12-card-sec12-F44.question_text: How should you position your car and manage your speed while a large truck overtakes you?
sec12-card-sec12-F44.teaching_text: Hugging the outer lane edge buffers wind push, and speeding up traps you longer in the rig's blind zone.
sec12-card-sec12-F44.must_match_memory_hook: Keep right, hold steady, never speed

visual_sync.text_span: Keep right, hold steady, never speed

sec12-card-sec12-F45.question_text: What should you do if a truck starts merging into your lane while you are in its blind spot?
sec12-card-sec12-F45.teaching_text: Panicking locks your options, whereas calmly braking, accelerating clear, or using a safe side shoulder prevents underride crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-F46.question_text: How should you place your car and spacing when meeting an oncoming truck on an undivided road?
sec12-card-sec12-F46.teaching_text: Staying right counters opposing air blasts and gives you braking space if trailer wheels drift toward the centerline.

sec12-card-sec12-F47.question_text: How far behind a large truck should you stay so the driver knows you are back there?
sec12-card-sec12-F47.teaching_text: Tailgating tucked behind trailer doors puts you inside a massive rear blind zone and blocks your forward road view.

sec12-card-sec12-F48.question_text: What does it mean if you cannot see the side mirrors on a truck or bus ahead of you?
sec12-card-sec12-F48.teaching_text: Large trailers have no center rearview mirror, so losing sight of the cab's side glass guarantees you are invisible.

sec12-card-sec12-F49.question_text: Why should you leave extra room when stopping behind a large truck on an uphill grade?
sec12-card-sec12-F49.teaching_text: Manual heavy transmissions can drift back several feet as the driver releases the brake and engages the clutch.

sec12-card-sec12-F50.question_text: How must you set your headlights when following behind a truck or any other vehicle after dark?
sec12-card-sec12-F50.teaching_text: Oversized truck side mirrors bounce bright high-beam glare straight into the cab driver's eyes at night.

sec12-card-sec12-F51.question_text: What minimum time cushion should you hold behind a truck, and how do you measure it?
sec12-card-sec12-F51.teaching_text: Starting your count as the trailer clears a roadside post ensures your front bumper reaches it at least four seconds later.

sec12-card-sec12-F52.question_text: Why must you hold back instead of passing a turning truck before it finishes the corner?
sec12-card-sec12-F52.teaching_text: Long trailers off-track sharply, forcing cab drivers to swing wide into neighboring lanes just to clear tight curbs.

sec12-card-sec12-F53.question_text: Why should you never try to squeeze between the curb and a truck signaling or making a right turn?
sec12-card-sec12-F53.teaching_text: A rig swinging left first to set up a right turn will crush any car sneaking into that curbside gap.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: How should you drive when you spot pilot cars with warning signs and flashing lights escorting an oversized load?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Pilot vehicles warn you early that wide, slow, heavy cargo with huge blind spots and swing paths is right nearby.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: Why might an oversized load cross over a painted lane line ahead of you?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Bridge rails, signs, or guardrails force extra-wide trailers across lane stripes, so never crowd beside them.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: What should you never do when a truck is lining up to back into a loading dock or bay?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Once a trailer angles toward a bay, the driver loses rear sightlines and cannot spot a car darting behind.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: At sixty-five miles per hour on clear dry pavement, how many feet does a loaded truck need to stop versus a passenger car?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Needing two hundred extra feet—roughly two-thirds of a football field—explains why loaded rigs cannot stop like cars.
sec12-card-sec12-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Six hundred feet versus four hundred

visual_sync.text_span: Six hundred feet versus four hundred

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: Why is pulling out or changing lanes right in front of a large vehicle so dangerous?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Stealing the open buffer ahead of a heavy truck or bus leaves its driver physically unable to avoid rear-ending you.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: Who are runaway escape ramps on steep downhill highways reserved for?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Deep gravel arrestor beds are engineered specifically to catch out-of-control heavy rigs experiencing mountain brake fade.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: Where must you never park or stop along a steep mountain descent?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: A parked car at the mouth of an escape ramp sits directly in the path of a brakeless runaway rig.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: Which road-sharing rules apply when you drive near transit or tour buses?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Buses share the same wide turns, blind No-Zones, and long stopping distances as heavy commercial trucks.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: What do flashing amber lights on a school bus tell surrounding drivers?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Accelerating to beat yellow school-bus flashers puts your car right into the crossing zone as red lights activate.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: Unless separated by a physical highway divider, how far must you stop from a school bus with red flashers and stop arm out, and from which approaches?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Drivers approaching a side street at the bus's intersection get cited too if they creep closer than ten feet.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: Which three things must happen before you move again after stopping for a school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Moving the instant red lights click off can still hit a child who dropped something near the bumper.
sec12-card-sec12-R11.must_match_memory_hook: Lights off, arm in, kids safe

visual_sync.text_span: Lights off, arm in, kids safe

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: What rule applies to oncoming drivers across a physical highway median from a stopped school bus?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Painted yellow lines or center turn lanes do not count—only raised barriers, concrete walls, or grass medians excuse stopping.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.question_text: What three penalties hit your record and wallet for illegally passing a stopped school bus with red lights and arm out?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.teaching_text: One single school-bus violation immediately suspends your license for two months and stacks five heavy points.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.question_text: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches from any direction using a siren or red or red-and-blue lights?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.teaching_text: Stopping inside an intersection blocks the exact turning room fire trucks and ambulances need to get through.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.question_text: Where should you pull over and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle on a one-way street?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.teaching_text: Splitting cleanly to whichever curb is closest opens a wide middle lane instead of tangling cars across lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.question_text: Once an emergency vehicle passes you, what distance and safety check apply as you pull back out?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.teaching_text: Emergency units often run in pairs, and tailgating closer than five hundred feet risks colliding when the rig stops.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.question_text: Whose traffic directions must you obey at an emergency scene?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.teaching_text: Fire police, sheriffs, constables, and uniformed responders hold full legal authority to route cars around crash hazards.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.question_text: What lane action is required when approaching an emergency-response area or a marked disabled vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.teaching_text: Putting an empty buffer lane between highway traffic and roadside flare or hazard scenes saves responders and stranded drivers.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.question_text: Can you get cited for a Move Over violation if no police officer is parked at the scene?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.teaching_text: Road crews and responders can log your plate and turn it in for a police citation even without patrol cars nearby.

sec12-card-sec12-R21.question_text: What maximum fines does the handbook list for first, second, and third or later Move Over offenses?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.teaching_text: Maximum penalties double with each repeat offense, climbing rapidly from five hundred dollars up to two thousand.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.question_text: How many points go onto your Pennsylvania driving record for a Move Over conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.teaching_text: Alongside steep fines, every conviction tacks two points onto your license history and raises insurance risk.

sec12-card-sec12-R23.question_text: Why should you leave plenty of room behind horse-drawn carriages or buggies?
sec12-card-sec12-R23.teaching_text: Carriages lack brake lights and enclosed boxes hide a tailgating car from the driver holding the reins.

sec12-card-sec12-R24.question_text: How should you pass horses or horse-drawn buggies and merge back into the lane?
sec12-card-sec12-R24.teaching_text: Revving engines, blasting horns, or cutting back close can spook a thousand-pound animal straight into traffic.
sec12-card-sec12-R24.must_match_memory_hook: Easy speed, zero horn, wide return

visual_sync.text_span: Easy speed, zero horn, wide return

sec12-card-sec12-R25.question_text: Why should you hang well back when following a working snowplow?
sec12-card-sec12-R25.teaching_text: Swirling snow clouds blind plow mirrors while salt spinners pelt close windshields and hoods with rock salt and anti-skid.

sec12-card-sec12-R26.question_text: Why must you never try to pass a snowplow on either the left or the right?
sec12-card-sec12-R26.teaching_text: Side-mounted wing plows jut several feet past the truck cab and stay hidden beneath blowing snow spray.

sec12-card-sec12-R27.question_text: How should you respond when another driver cuts you off or drives aggressively?
sec12-card-sec12-R27.teaching_text: Brake-checking or chasing an angry motorist turns a minor traffic annoyance into dangerous road rage.

sec12-card-sec12-R28.question_text: How should you handle lane position and speed when an aggressive driver wants past you?
sec12-card-sec12-R28.teaching_text: Camping in the left lane or hitting the gas to block someone escalates tension right beside your doors.
sec12-card-sec12-R28.must_match_memory_hook: Let pass, never block or race

visual_sync.text_span: Let pass, never block or race

sec12-card-sec12-R29.question_text: How should you handle eye contact and rude hand gestures from an angry motorist?
sec12-card-sec12-R29.teaching_text: Staring back or returning gestures personalizes the conflict and invites an unstable driver to escalate.

sec12-card-sec12-R30.question_text: What is the safe way to report an aggressive driver to police or nine one one while traveling?
sec12-card-sec12-R30.teaching_text: Fumbling with a handheld phone in fast traffic makes you a distracted hazard right alongside the aggressive driver.

sec12-card-sec12-R31.question_text: Where should you drive—and where must you avoid going—if an aggressive driver follows your car?
sec12-card-sec12-R31.teaching_text: Pulling into your own driveway traps you alone and reveals your address, whereas police stations or busy stores bring help.

sec12-card-sec12-R32.question_text: When choosing between braking or steering to dodge a crash—especially above twenty-five miles per hour—which usually works better?
sec12-card-sec12-R32.teaching_text: At higher speeds your car can swerve into an open space in far less distance than it needs to stop completely.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: How should you hold the steering wheel so you are ready for sudden emergency maneuvers?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Driving one-handed leaves you unable to make balanced, split-second swerves when a hazard pops into your lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: How does higher road speed affect how much steering input you need to move sideways?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Yanking the wheel hard at highway pace overcorrects violently and can spin or roll the vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: Which two clock-face hand positions and thumb placement does the Pennsylvania handbook recommend?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Resting thumbs along the front rim instead of hooked inside prevents broken thumbs if an airbag deploys.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: Even though ten-and-two is still acceptable, what injury risk rises when your hands sit that high?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: An inflating steering-wheel airbag blasts outward directly into hands resting high across the upper rim.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: How do your hands move across the wheel during hand-over-hand steering?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Crossing over cleanly to grab the opposite rim delivers quick turning angle during tight parking or skid recovery.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: How do your two hands alternate during push-pull steering?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Keeping arms uncrossed in front of your chest protects your face and wrists if the airbag fires mid-turn.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: Besides buckled seat belts and adjusted head restraints, how far should your chest sit from the airbag?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Hunching closer than ten inches puts your chest inside the explosive opening zone of the steering-wheel bag.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: How should you find out ahead of time whether your car has conventional brakes or ABS?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Emergency stopping technique flips completely between anti-lock and conventional systems, leaving zero time to guess mid-panic.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: How should you work the brake pedal during an urgent stop in a car without ABS?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Slamming non-ABS brakes locks the tires into a straight slide where turning the steering wheel does nothing.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: How do you use the brake pedal for an urgent stop when your car has ABS?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Pumping anti-lock brakes defeats the computer pulsing that keeps your front tires rolling and steerable.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: What should you make of grinding noises and slight pedal pulsing during hard ABS braking?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Drivers startled by pedal chatter often lift their foot right when they need maximum stopping force most.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: Where should you look and turn the wheel when your rear tires skid sideways on wet or icy pavement?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Matching your wheel turn to the direction the tail slides realigns the front tires with where you want to go.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: What secondary slide must you stay ready for right after correcting an initial skid?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Late or heavy steering fixes often whip the tail the other way, demanding a quick counter-steer back.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: Why must you stay off the brake pedal while steering out of a skid?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Hitting the brakes mid-slide locks low-traction tires and wipes out the front grip needed to steer straight.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: How little standing or moving floodwater does it take to make small cars lose control or float?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Water reaching the bottom of low car doors steals tire weight off the asphalt faster than drivers expect.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: What depths of moving floodwater can float many sedans and sweep away most SUVs and pickups?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Four-wheel drive and high ground clearance mean nothing once two feet of current lifts heavy frames sideways.
sec13-card-sec13-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Twelve inches cars, two feet trucks

visual_sync.text_span: Twelve inches cars, two feet trucks

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: What must you do when you reach a flooded road or a flood closure barricade?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Going around road-closed horses puts you into washed-out currents and endangers rescue crews sent after you.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: What road-surface dangers can muddy floodwater hide underneath, especially after dark?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Calm-looking brown water can mask collapsed culverts or undermined asphalt that drops out under your front wheels.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: What is your immediate priority if your vehicle stalls and gets stuck in floodwater?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Flash floods rise in seconds, so waiting inside a stalled cabin risks getting swept downstream with the car.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: If your accelerator sticks down, how may you try freeing it while keeping your eyes up—and what must you never do?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Ducking under the dash to pull a stuck pedal blinds you to traffic at high speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: What gear and brake move should you make immediately if tapping fails to free a stuck gas pedal?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Disconnecting the transmission stops engine revving from pushing the wheels so your brakes can slow the car.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: Once you slow down under control from a stuck accelerator, what four steps finish the stop safely?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Waiting until you are safely stopped off the pavement before killing the engine preserves power steering during your exit.
sec13-card-sec13-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Pull off, stop, shut engine, hazards

visual_sync.text_span: Pull off, stop, shut engine, hazards

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: If a stuck accelerator forces an immediate stop while moving, which ignition setting do you use and what changes?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Turning all the way to LOCK freezes the steering wheel, while switching to OFF merely stiffens steering and brake assist.
sec13-card-sec13-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Switch OFF never LOCK, push harder

visual_sync.text_span: Switch OFF never LOCK, push harder

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: What braking capability and pedal changes remain when a split-system brake warning light comes on?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Dual hydraulic circuits keep one front and one rear brake alive, though the pedal sinks lower and stopping stretches out.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: How should you slow down and where should you head if half of your split brake system fails?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Letting lower gears help slow the car spares your remaining two brakes from overheating while exiting traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: What are your first two moves if the brakes fail completely in an older vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Engine compression immediately trims road speed while your eyes pick out a flat, open escape path.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: Why should you pump the brake pedal rapidly when brakes fail in an older vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Quick repeated strokes can push remaining brake fluid enough to squeeze the pads for one controlled stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: If pumping fails to bring back hydraulic brakes, how must you apply the parking brake safely?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Keeping your thumb or hand on the release lets you back off instantly if the rear wheels lock into a spin.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: When an older brakeless car still faces an imminent crash, what last-resort ignition and gear sequence applies?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Risking transmission damage beats a high-speed crash, provided you never twist the key into steering-wheel LOCK.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: What must you do—and refuse to do—once you get a car with failed brakes stopped?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Even if pedal feel briefly returns after cooling, a leaking brake line will fail again at the next light.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: What routine upkeep lowers your chance of suffering a highway tire blowout?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Underinflated sidewalls flex excessively at highway speed, building heat until the tread separates or bursts.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: How does a front-tire blowout feel from the driver's seat compared with a rear-tire failure?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Recognizing whether the nose tugs sideways or the tail fishtails helps you brace the wheel without panicking.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: How should you handle the wheel and gas pedal the moment a tire blows out?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel or snapping off the pedals upsets weight balance while a shredded tire drags one corner.
sec13-card-sec13-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Grip firm, ease gas, steer smooth

visual_sync.text_span: Grip firm, ease gas, steer smooth

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: How should you treat the brake pedal during a tire blowout as you work toward the shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: Stomping the brakes right after a burst pitches heavy load onto the bare rim and spins the car.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: When is it okay to keep rolling slowly on a flat tire instead of stopping immediately?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Ruining an aluminum wheel rim costs nothing compared with getting struck changing a tire in a narrow travel lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R11.question_text: Because jack points and spare setups differ across models, what should you check and keep in the trunk?
sec13-card-sec13-R11.teaching_text: Discovering a missing lug key or run-flat kit on a dark shoulder turns a simple flat into a tow.

sec13-card-sec13-R12.question_text: What kind of surface and location do you need before jacking up a car to change a tire?
sec13-card-sec13-R12.teaching_text: Soft dirt or sloped shoulders let a narrow roadside jack tip over once the wheel comes off.

sec13-card-sec13-R13.question_text: Before lifting the car with a jack, how do you stop the remaining tires from rolling?
sec13-card-sec13-R13.teaching_text: Blocking both sides of a grounded tire keeps the vehicle from creeping forward or backward off the jack.

sec13-card-sec13-R14.question_text: What trim step comes first if your wheel has a hubcap or lug cover?
sec13-card-sec13-R14.teaching_text: Popping off plastic covers on the ground exposes the lug nuts without rocking a raised car on its jack.

sec13-card-sec13-R15.question_text: When should you crack the lug nuts loose, and how far do you unscrew them at first?
sec13-card-sec13-R15.teaching_text: Ground friction holds the wheel still against wrench force, whereas spinning them completely off early drops the hub.

sec13-card-sec13-R16.question_text: Where must the jack sit under the car, and roughly how high do you lift the flat tire?
sec13-card-sec13-R16.teaching_text: Jacking against thin floorpans punches through metal, and a fully inflated spare needs extra clearance than a flat.

sec13-card-sec13-R17.question_text: Once the tire is raised off the ground, how do you handle the lug nuts and remove the wheel?
sec13-card-sec13-R17.teaching_text: Keeping loose lug nuts together prevents losing hardware in grass while two hands steady the heavy wheel.

sec13-card-sec13-R18.question_text: After sliding the spare onto the studs, how should you start and snug the lug nuts?
sec13-card-sec13-R18.teaching_text: Starting threads by hand prevents cross-threading studs, and heavy wrench force while elevated could topple the jack.

sec13-card-sec13-R19.question_text: How do you bring the vehicle down before giving the lug nuts their final tightening?
sec13-card-sec13-R19.teaching_text: Resting tire weight back onto the pavement keeps the wheel from spinning while you apply full wrench pressure.

sec13-card-sec13-R20.question_text: Where do you find the proper lug-nut tightening order and torque rating for your vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-R20.teaching_text: Tightening in the manufacturer's criss-cross pattern seats the rim flat and stops brake rotors from warping.

sec13-card-sec13-R21.question_text: What should you do with the flat wheel, jack, wrench, and roadside triangles once the spare is tight?
sec13-card-sec13-R21.teaching_text: Loose metal jacks or heavy tires left sliding in the trunk turn into lethal projectiles in a sudden stop.

sec13-card-sec13-R22.question_text: What last check applies to hubcaps or center caps before pulling back onto the road?
sec13-card-sec13-R22.teaching_text: Some temporary compact spares do not take full wheel covers, and a loose cap can fly off into traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-R23.question_text: If an oncoming car drifts into your lane, what warning and escape side should you use?
sec13-card-sec13-R23.teaching_text: Heading toward the right shoulder or ditch beats a head-on impact and keeps you clear of opposing lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-R24.question_text: Why must you never swerve into the left lane to dodge an oncoming car in your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R24.teaching_text: When a distracted oncoming driver looks up, their natural reflex snaps them right back into that lane.

sec13-card-sec13-R25.question_text: If a head-on crash is unavoidable, how should you brake in the final moments?
sec13-card-sec13-R25.teaching_text: Every mile per hour scrubbed off before contact dramatically drops the crash force absorbed by the cabin.

sec13-card-sec13-R26.question_text: What is your immediate pedal and steering move if your right tires drop off the pavement edge?
sec13-card-sec13-R26.teaching_text: Yanking back onto high asphalt right away catches the tire sidewall and slingshots you into oncoming traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-R27.question_text: If a mailbox or guardrail ahead forces you to brake with tires off the road, how do you press the pedal?
sec13-card-sec13-R27.teaching_text: Split traction between dry asphalt on the left and loose gravel on the right spins cars that lock their brakes.

sec13-card-sec13-R28.question_text: How should you steer while rolling with two wheels on pavement and two on the shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-R28.teaching_text: Rubbing the right tire along a raised asphalt lip hooks the steering and destabilizes the car.

sec13-card-sec13-R30.question_text: Once slowed and clear behind, how do you signal and steer your right wheels back onto the road?
sec13-card-sec13-R30.teaching_text: Easing across the lip gently and straightening right away stops you from shooting across the centerline.

sec13-card-sec13-R31.question_text: After a shoulder drop-off recovery, when should you accelerate back up to traffic speed?
sec13-card-sec13-R31.teaching_text: Getting all four tires settled straight in your lane first prevents wheelspin on gravel or sudden fishtailing.

sec13-card-sec13-R32.question_text: How must outside drivers treat a funeral procession, and when is cutting through allowed?
sec13-card-sec13-R32.teaching_text: Only a police officer or authorized procession director can wave cross traffic through an active line of cars.

sec13-card-sec13-R33.question_text: Which lights and markers identify vehicles traveling in a Pennsylvania funeral procession?
sec13-card-sec13-R33.teaching_text: Watching for hazard flashers, pennants, and purple beacons keeps you from mistaking closely spaced cars for regular traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-R34.question_text: How may cars inside a funeral procession proceed through red traffic lights or stop signs?
sec13-card-sec13-R34.teaching_text: Once the lead car enters on green or makes a full stop at a sign, trailing cars stay together safely.

sec13-card-sec13-R35.question_text: Who outranks even an active funeral procession at intersections and along the road?
sec13-card-sec13-R35.teaching_text: Life-saving ambulances, fire engines, and patrol responses always take priority over every other group on the road.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: What agency maintains each licensed Pennsylvania motorist's record, and what reports go into it?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Every traffic conviction forwarded by police and courts builds a permanent safety history tied to your license.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: At how many accumulated record points does PennDOT start corrective action?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Permit exams love testing the six-point trigger because even two moderate speeding tickets can cross that line.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: What happens the very first time your driving record reaches six or more points?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Ignoring that mailed exam notice leads to suspension, whereas passing promptly helps protect your driving privilege.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: What is required if your record drops below six points and later climbs to six again?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Repeat point spikes show a pattern of risky driving, escalating from a written test to an in-person review.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: What consequences can follow additional accumulations of six or more points?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Repeatedly rebounding past six points risks losing your license entirely rather than merely taking another class.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: Which two triggers automatically suspend a Pennsylvania driver younger than eighteen?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Junior drivers lose privileges on a single high-speed ticket that an adult might survive with points alone.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: How long are the first and later suspensions for those under-eighteen point or speeding triggers?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Memorize ninety days then one hundred twenty days because teen suspension lengths appear frequently on Pennsylvania exams.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: How many points come off your record for each clean twelve-month stretch, and what keeps it clean?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Even one point-carrying ticket or suspension resets the twelve-month clock before any three-point credit drops.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: How is a future point accumulation treated once your record stays at zero for twelve consecutive months?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Holding zero points for a full year earns back first-time status instead of escalating straight to a hearing.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: Which impaired, violent, or aggressive driving convictions directly cause suspension or revocation?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Severe offenses bypass the six-point ladder completely and strip your driving privilege upon conviction.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: Which four evasion, flight, or invalid-driving convictions bring license sanctions?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Trying to outrun police, hide in the dark, drive suspended, or leave a crash compounds trouble fast.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: When does driving without a license trigger a suspension or revocation?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Getting caught unlicensed a second time inside five years locks out future licensing eligibility.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: What license suspension follows failing to stop for a school bus with red flashers and stop arm?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Beyond heavy fines and points, passing loading school children costs two full months off the road.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: How long is your license suspended for disregarding a railroad crossing gate or barrier?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Weaving around lowered crossing gates gambles your life against a train and triggers an automatic month-long ban.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: What does a mailed sanction notice specify, and what items must be returned by that date?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Holding onto your plastic license, permit, or camera card past the start date violates surrender rules.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: When does a Pennsylvania driving sanction officially take effect?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Driving on or after the effective date counts as driving under suspension even if you have not mailed the card.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: Does turning in your license ahead of time make a suspension start earlier?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Test writers bait learners into thinking early mail-in shaves days off the back end, which is false.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: Where and within how many days must a driver file an appeal of a sanction notice?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Note that the thirty-day appeal clock runs from the notice's mailing date, not the day you open the envelope.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: What two conditions must you satisfy to restore suspended driving privileges?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Privileges never snap back automatically on the final day until fees, forms, and proof requirements clear.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: How many points normally remain on a restored record, and which two suspensions are exceptions?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Returning at five points leaves almost zero cushion before hitting six again and facing another sanction.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: What insurance obligation applies to every registered Pennsylvania vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Canceling insurance before returning your license plate triggers state penalties even if the car sits parked.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: What suspensions result from a thirty-one-day insurance lapse or letting an uninsured car be driven?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Letting coverage lapse past thirty days benches the vehicle registration, and driving it benches your license too.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: What two items are required to restore privileges lost for an uninsured vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: PennDOT holds both registration and driving privileges locked until active insurance proof and restoration payments arrive.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: What core rule governs your behavior during a police traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Clear, cooperative compliance keeps roadside stops calm and predictable alongside fast-moving traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: How and where should you pull over when signaled for a police stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Using your turn signal acknowledges the officer while pulling well off the travel lane protects everyone from passing cars.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: What three vehicle steps should you take right after coming to a stop for police?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Shutting down the motor and stereo while lowering your window lets both sides hear instructions clearly.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: What extra step should you take during a nighttime traffic stop before the officer walks up?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Lighting the interior in the dark reassures the approaching officer that everyone's hands are empty and calm.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: How should the driver and passengers manage movements and hands during a traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Sudden rummaging in consoles or under seats looks alarming from outside the car, so stay still with visible hands.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: What must you tell the officer right away if a firearm is inside the vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Calmly informing the officer up front prevents dangerous misunderstandings before anyone reaches near storage areas.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: What should you do with your doors and seat belt when pulled over by police?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Unbuckling before the officer arrives can earn an avoidable seat-belt ticket even when you wore it while driving.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: When should you reach for documents, and how should you hand them to the officer?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Waiting to be asked prevents sudden reaching, and handing only the cards avoids misunderstandings over cash or wallets.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: How should you handle a traffic citation that you believe is unfair?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Roadside shoulders are never courtrooms; arguing on the curb never voids a ticket and only escalates tension.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: Where can you report a concern about an officer's conduct during a stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Completing the stop calmly and calling a department supervisor later addresses misconduct safely through official channels.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: What should you do if you are unsure whether a vehicle signaling you to stop is genuine police?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: Flashing four-ways and slowing signals compliance rather than flight while you reach a bright, populated spot.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.question_text: When should you request official identification during a traffic stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.teaching_text: Asking to see official credentials verifies legitimate authority whenever standard markings or uniforms are absent.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.question_text: Which flashing light colors identify Pennsylvania police versus a blue-only light?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.teaching_text: Volunteer firefighters in Pennsylvania use courtesy blue lights, so blue alone never authorizes a police stop.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: When should you avoid stopping at a roadside crash scene?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Rubbernecking or parking unnecessarily near wreckage blocks fire trucks and causes secondary rear-end pileups.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: Where must you stop and position your vehicle if you are involved in a crash?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Pulling drivable cars onto the shoulder prevents oncoming highway traffic from slamming into stalled wreckage.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: Which three crash conditions require calling police, and what must witnesses do if drivers are hurt?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Prompt emergency dispatch saves injured lives and clears disabled cars that cannot roll away safely.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: What five pieces of driver, vehicle, and insurance information must be exchanged after a crash?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Gathering complete registration and policy details at the scene prevents claim delays or disputes afterward.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: Whose names and addresses should you write down besides the other drivers?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Independent bystanders often leave within minutes, yet their statements resolve disputed fault accounts later.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: What steps are required if you damage unattended parked property and cannot find the owner?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Driving off without leaving date, time, name, phone number, and a police report turns a bump into hit-and-run.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: What must you file if police do not investigate a crash involving injury, death, or towing?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Know both Form AA-six hundred and the strict five-day deadline whenever an officer does not investigate a reportable crash.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration does a driver twenty-one or older meet the DUI threshold?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Alcohol slows judgment and reaction well before you feel drunk, making zero point zero eight a strict legal line.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: Can an adult driver be convicted of DUI with a BAC below zero point zero eight?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Blowing under the per-se number offers no shield if weaving, slurred speech, or unsafe driving shows impairment.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: What blood alcohol concentration triggers DUI for a driver younger than twenty-one?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: Even trace alcohol from half a drink can hit zero point zero two and trigger underage DUI sanctions.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: What testing agreement comes automatically with holding a Pennsylvania driver's license?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: Accepting a Pennsylvania license legally binds you in advance to submit to lawful alcohol or drug testing.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.question_text: How does refusing a breath or blood test after a DUI arrest affect your license?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.teaching_text: Administrative refusal suspension runs on its own track completely separate from criminal DUI court.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.question_text: What happens to a first chemical-test refusal suspension if you win a not-guilty verdict on DUI?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.teaching_text: Beating the DUI charge in court will not erase the one-year implied-consent suspension for refusing testing.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.question_text: Which three factors make Pennsylvania DUI sanctions escalate in severity?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.teaching_text: Pennsylvania's tiered system multiplies jail, fines, and license loss as blood alcohol, crash damage, or repeat offenses climb.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.question_text: When is Alcohol Highway Safety School mandatory in Pennsylvania DUI cases?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.teaching_text: Every impairment tier triggers mandatory safety classes on a first or second conviction without exception.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.question_text: What treatment orders and maximum community-service hours can courts impose for DUI at any tier?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.teaching_text: Judges can combine clinical alcohol treatment with up to one hundred fifty hours of unpaid community work.

sec14-card-sec14-R17.question_text: What does an ignition-interlock restricted license generally require regarding vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.teaching_text: You cannot borrow an unequipped family car during an interlock restriction without violating PennDOT rules.

sec14-card-sec14-R18.question_text: Which diversion program may a first DUI at high or highest impairment still qualify for?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.teaching_text: Supervised diversion lets eligible first-time offenders complete strict conditions under court oversight.

sec14-card-sec14-R19.question_text: Which four alcohol actions are illegal for anyone under twenty-one, including inside their car?
sec14-card-sec14-R19.teaching_text: Even unopened cans riding in the trunk of a teen's car count as unlawful underage possession and transport.

sec14-card-sec14-R20.question_text: Does police chemical testing of an arrested minor require parental consent, and are parents told?
sec14-card-sec14-R20.teaching_text: Implied consent applies to young drivers immediately upon arrest, though officers still notify parents afterward.

sec14-card-sec14-R21.question_text: What follow-up programs may courts order after an underage drinking offense?
sec14-card-sec14-R21.teaching_text: Judges routinely pair fines with mandatory alcohol assessment, classes, intervention, or counseling sessions.

sec14-card-sec14-R22.question_text: Who can face legal penalties for knowingly and intentionally supplying alcohol to a minor?
sec14-card-sec14-R22.teaching_text: Hosting or buying drinks for teens exposes adults and parents alike to serious legal consequences.

sec14-card-sec14-R23.question_text: What jurisdictions cooperate under the Driver's License Compact, and why?
sec14-card-sec14-R23.teaching_text: Interstate data sharing stops unsafe drivers from hiding tickets or suspensions simply by crossing state borders.

sec14-card-sec14-R24.question_text: What happens to your out-of-state license under the compact's one-license concept when moving?
sec14-card-sec14-R24.teaching_text: No driver may hold two state licenses to spread points across separate cards.

sec14-card-sec14-R25.question_text: What does the compact's one-record concept maintain in your home state?
sec14-card-sec14-R25.teaching_text: Consolidating every multistate event in one home file determines ongoing driving eligibility everywhere.

sec14-card-sec14-R26.question_text: What events do compact jurisdictions report back to a driver's home licensing agency?
sec14-card-sec14-R26.teaching_text: Traffic convictions and license bans from road trips travel electronically straight back to PennDOT.

sec14-card-sec14-R27.question_text: How does Pennsylvania treat specified compact offenses committed in another member jurisdiction?
sec14-card-sec14-R27.teaching_text: Major violations out of state trigger the exact home-state license loss you would face inside Pennsylvania.

sec14-card-sec14-R28.question_text: Which three major violations are examples of specified offenses under the Driver's License Compact?
sec14-card-sec14-R28.teaching_text: Impaired driving, fleeing an injury or fatal crash, and vehicle felonies bring guaranteed home-state action.

sec14-card-sec14-R29.question_text: What happens to your Pennsylvania license if you ignore an out-of-state traffic citation?
sec14-card-sec14-R29.teaching_text: Tossing an out-of-state ticket in the glovebox freezes your Pennsylvania license indefinitely until you resolve it.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: Within how many days must you report a name or address change, including moving out of state, to PennDOT?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Missing the fifteen-day window can send renewal or sanction notices to an old mailbox while deadlines tick.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: Does Pennsylvania issue driver-license products to nonresidents?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Once you establish residency elsewhere, you must transfer into your new home state's licensing system.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: Which PennDOT form requests a non-commercial license name change, correction, or replacement?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Permit questions test exact form numbers, so pair DL-eighty with non-commercial replacements, fixes, and name updates.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: What must you carry alongside your plastic license after receiving a license update card?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Keeping the update slip tucked beside your photo card shows officers your current legal address during stops.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: Who must wear seat belts in the front seats of cars, light trucks, and motorhomes?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Front occupants sit closest to the windshield and dashboard, making belt use mandatory across every trip.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: Which passenger age group must buckle up in every seating position, front or rear?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: Teens riding unbuckled in the back row become dangerous projectiles and earn tickets in any seat.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: How do working seat belts limit passenger count for a driver younger than eighteen?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Cramming extra friends into a five-belt car leaves someone unrestrained and violates junior-driver rules.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: What happens to an unrestrained occupant's body the instant a crashing vehicle stops?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Even when bumpers crumple to zero, an unbuckled rider slams ahead at the car's pre-crash speed.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: How do seat belts protect your body from rapid deceleration during a collision?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Channeling crash energy across your chest, shoulders, and pelvis prevents concentrated blows against glass or steering columns.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: Do factory airbags eliminate the need to buckle your seat belt?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Airbags deploy violently for frontal hits only and cannot hold you in place during rollovers or side impacts.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: Where do seat belts help keep vehicle occupants during a violent crash?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Being thrown through a window onto pavement or under rolling metal multiplies fatal injury risk dramatically.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: How must a child younger than two ride, and when may they outgrow that orientation?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Rear-facing shells cradle fragile infant necks and spines until height or weight exceeds manufacturer limits.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: Where must a rear-facing child safety seat never be installed?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: An inflating front airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing infant shell right where the baby's head rests.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: How should required child seats or boosters for children under eight be installed and fitted?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Loose base mounting or slack harness straps let a child submarine forward during hard braking or impact.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: May you leave a child or pet alone inside a parked car if the windows are cracked open?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Cracked glass barely slows greenhouse heating, allowing parked cabin temperatures to turn lethal within minutes.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: What rule applies to letting children play inside an unattended parked vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Curious kids can knock a shifter into neutral, get trapped in trunks, or overheat inside locked doors.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: What two simple habits help prevent accidentally forgetting a quiet child in the rear seat?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Putting your phone, bag, or shoe in back guarantees opening the rear door whenever you park.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: Why are bulky winter coats risky inside a child-seat harness, and how must straps fit?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Crash forces crush puffy winter padding flat in milliseconds, opening dangerous harness slack that lets a child slip out.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: What restraint and anchoring methods are required for children younger than four in any seat?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Toddlers under four need five-point federally approved shells anchored firmly by LATCH or vehicle belt in every row.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: What restraint setup is required for children aged four up to under eight in any seat?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Boosters lift small frames so adult lap-and-shoulder webbing sits over strong pelvic and chest bones rather than stomachs.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: What restraint rule covers ages eight to under eighteen, and who carries legal responsibility?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: If a minor rides unbuckled anywhere in your car, the ticket lands directly on you as the driver.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: Where should the lap belt and shoulder strap rest across your body?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: Tucking a shoulder strap behind your back or riding a lap belt high on your belly causes severe crash injuries.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: How far back from the steering wheel and airbag should a driver sit?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: Keeping ten inches or more between your breastbone and the hub lets an airbag inflate fully before cushioning you.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.question_text: Which clock hand positions and thumb placement does the handbook recommend on the steering wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.teaching_text: Lower balanced hands with thumbs along the outer rim keep an inflating airbag from flinging arms into your face.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.question_text: Up through what age does the handbook recommend that children ride in the rear seat?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.teaching_text: Back-row seating shields growing kids from frontal crumple zones and high-speed passenger airbags.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.question_text: Why do lap and shoulder belts stay necessary in vehicles equipped with airbags?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.teaching_text: Engineers calibrate airbags assuming a belted rider; unbuckled bodies hit the bag too early and violently.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.question_text: What testing accommodations does PennDOT provide for applicants with hearing impairments?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.teaching_text: Requesting interpreter support ahead of your exam ensures clear communication throughout licensing steps.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.question_text: What should applicants requesting sign-language assistance specify in advance?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.teaching_text: Naming ASL, PSE, SEE, or oral interpretation up front matches you with the exact specialist you understand best.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: What testing option can applicants who have difficulty reading request at PennDOT?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Audio delivery reads permit questions aloud through headphones so reading barriers do not block safe drivers.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: What two conditions must both be met to park legally in a reserved disability space?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Borrowing a relative's placard to run solo errands is illegal whenever the eligible person is not riding or picked up.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: What can happen to a vehicle parked unlawfully in a reserved disability space?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: Blocking access aisles strands wheelchair users and sticks violators with impound and towing bills on top of fines.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: Where is discarding trash or waste from a vehicle prohibited?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Tossed debris shatters windshields, sparks roadside brush fires, and pollutes Pennsylvania streams and private yards.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: Who can be fined if a passenger throws trash out of a moving car?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Operators answer for waste tossed from any window of their vehicle, not solely trash dropped from the driver seat.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: How often does a Pennsylvania vehicle need an authorized safety inspection, and what marks the due date?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Yearly brake, tire, lighting, and steering checks catch dangerous mechanical wear before parts fail at highway speed.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: How early before expiration may you complete your vehicle's next safety inspection?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Scheduling within the three-month window avoids last-day shop backlogs without losing months off your next sticker.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: How many days may an officer give you to repair faulty vehicle equipment and avoid a citation?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Replacing a burned-out bulb or broken mirror within five days proves compliance and spares you a court fine.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: What check and minimum side clearance are required before overtaking a bicyclist?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: Pennsylvania's four-foot buffer gives riders room to dodge potholes or wind gusts without clipping your mirror.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.question_text: May you cross a double solid yellow centerline to give a cyclist four feet of passing space?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.teaching_text: Knowledge tests love this exception: clear sightlines let you straddle double yellow rather than buzzing a cyclist.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.question_text: When is a slower cyclist's normal keep-right rule waived on a roadway?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.teaching_text: Where only one lane goes your way, riders legally claim space so cars wait for a safe pass.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.question_text: Why may a cyclist ride in any part of a single travel lane?
