sec15-card-sec15-R12.teaching_text: Broken glass, storm grates, and swinging car doors hug the curb, forcing riders toward the lane center.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.question_text: What turning mistake must you avoid near a cyclist riding straight on the road or shoulder?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.teaching_text: Overtaking a bike and immediately hooking right cuts straight across a rider moving faster than expected.

sec15-card-sec15-R14.question_text: What legal consequence can follow forcing a bicyclist off the roadway?
sec15-card-sec15-R14.teaching_text: Crowding or intimidating an unprotected rider with a two-ton car crosses from a traffic ticket into criminal prosecution.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.question_text: How do traffic laws and minimum-speed rules apply to bicyclists?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.teaching_text: Pedal power naturally climbs hills slower than cars, so cyclists cannot be ticketed for impeding minimum speed.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.question_text: Must bicyclists ride on a paved shoulder or berm when one exists?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.teaching_text: Shoulders collect gravel, glass, and rumble strips, so riders always keep the legal right to use travel lanes.

sec15-card-sec15-R17.question_text: What is prohibited at a hazardous-road closure sign or traffic-control barrier?
sec15-card-sec15-R17.teaching_text: Barricades guard downed power lines, bridge washouts, or swift floodwaters that look deceptively passable.

sec15-card-sec15-R18.question_text: What points and maximum fine apply for driving past a hazardous-road closure?
sec15-card-sec15-R18.teaching_text: Sneaking around cones adds two record points and up to two hundred fifty dollars even if nothing goes wrong.

sec15-card-sec15-R19.question_text: How do penalties jump if bypassing a road closure triggers an emergency rescue response?
sec15-card-sec15-R19.teaching_text: Getting stranded past flood barricades sticks you with up to a five-hundred-dollar fine plus the entire rescue bill.

sec15-card-sec15-R20.question_text: What mirror checks and hand choice should precede opening a parked car's street-side door?
sec15-card-sec15-R20.teaching_text: Reaching across your chest with your right hand naturally pivots your shoulders to spot bikes in your blind zone.

sec15-card-sec15-R21.question_text: What two safety benefits does the Dutch Reach technique create when exiting a parked car?
sec15-card-sec15-R21.teaching_text: Rotating your torso puts approaching riders in view while limiting how far the door can swing out suddenly.

sec15-card-sec15-R22.question_text: How much clearance should cyclists keep beside parked cars to stay out of the door zone?
sec15-card-sec15-R22.teaching_text: An open car door extends roughly three feet into the street, even inside painted curbside bike lanes.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.question_text: Which toxic gas do gasoline-powered vehicles emit from their exhaust pipe?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.teaching_text: Every running combustion engine produces toxic exhaust continuously, even while idling quietly in park.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.question_text: Why is carbon monoxide so dangerous to detect with your senses?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.teaching_text: Because you cannot smell fumes creeping into the cabin, lethal concentrations build without triggering any odor alarm.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.question_text: What sleepy state behind the wheel can warn of carbon monoxide poisoning?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.teaching_text: Brushing off sudden heavy eyelids as ordinary boredom keeps you breathing poisoned cabin air until consciousness fades.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.question_text: Which two energy-draining body sensations appear on the handbook's carbon monoxide symptom list?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.teaching_text: Carbon monoxide starves blood of oxygen, draining physical strength rapidly even during a short commute.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.question_text: Which lightheaded, room-spinning sensation is listed as a carbon monoxide symptom?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.teaching_text: Feeling lightheaded inside a closed car ruins steering control seconds before fainting becomes a crash risk.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.question_text: What painful head symptom is a listed indicator of carbon monoxide exposure?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.teaching_text: When multiple riders develop dull headaches on the same drive, suspect leaking exhaust rather than coincidence.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.question_text: Which two stomach-related reactions can indicate carbon monoxide exposure inside a vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.teaching_text: Mistaking sudden cabin queasiness for food poisoning or carsickness delays opening doors and escaping toxic fumes.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.question_text: What change in heart rhythm appears among the handbook's carbon monoxide exposure symptoms?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.teaching_text: Your heart races harder trying to circulate scarce oxygen when exhaust gas hijacks red blood cells.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.question_text: What change in your breathing pattern is included among carbon monoxide symptoms?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.teaching_text: Uneven or labored breaths while sitting still in a vehicle demand pulling over into outdoor air immediately.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.question_text: Which two mental-clarity warning states can signal carbon monoxide exposure?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.teaching_text: Clouded thinking makes exposure doubly dangerous because poisoned drivers struggle to recognize why they feel lost.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.question_text: Which airway irritation reflex is included on the handbook's carbon monoxide warning list?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.teaching_text: Exhaust leaks carry irritating combustion gases alongside odorless carbon monoxide that trigger unexplained coughing fits.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.question_text: What upper-body pain symptom appears on the handbook's carbon monoxide exposure list?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.teaching_text: Oxygen deprivation stresses heart muscle quickly, causing chest tightness or ache that requires emergency care.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.question_text: Which underside vehicle parts should be inspected and maintained regularly to prevent carbon monoxide leaks?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.teaching_text: Road salt and potholes rust Pennsylvania exhaust pipes, letting fumes seep upward through floorboard seams.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.question_text: What should you do right away if you notice exhaust holes or defects?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.teaching_text: Loud exhaust rumble under the floor often means rusted holes are venting deadly gas directly beneath passengers.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.question_text: What precaution is critical when parking a keyless-ignition vehicle inside an attached garage?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.teaching_text: Walking indoors with a fob in your pocket while a quiet push-button engine idles fills attached bedrooms with fumes.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.question_text: What exterior check must you perform on snowy days to prevent cabin exhaust buildup?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.teaching_text: Backing into a snowbank plugs the tailpipe solid, forcing lethal exhaust backward into the passenger cabin within minutes.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.question_text: What portable device does the handbook suggest adding inside your vehicle for extra protection?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.teaching_text: A compact battery-operated alarm sounds an early warning long before odorless gas causes dizziness or sleepiness.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.question_text: When each year should you test or replace batteries in a carbon monoxide detector?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.teaching_text: Tying battery checks to semi-annual daylight-saving clock shifts guarantees your detector never dies silently.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.question_text: What must you do with the vehicle right away if carbon monoxide poisoning is suspected?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.teaching_text: Every extra breath inside a contaminated cabin deepens blood poisoning, so park safely and get everyone out.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.question_text: What environment do you need immediately when vehicle carbon monoxide poisoning is suspected?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.teaching_text: Breathing clean open air right away halts further gas intake and starts clearing carbon monoxide from your bloodstream.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.question_text: What medical follow-up is required right away for suspected carbon monoxide poisoning?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.teaching_text: Even if symptoms ease outside, emergency clinicians provide high-flow oxygen and check for hidden heart or brain injury.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: What three driver shortcomings does Pennsylvania highlight as common contributors to traffic crashes?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Misjudging how your vehicle responds or drifting into distraction turns ordinary traffic moments into preventable wrecks.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: How many surrounding space areas must you manage around your vehicle, and where should you keep a buffer?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Maintaining open breathing room ahead, behind, and on every corner gives you time and space to dodge surprises.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: On dry asphalt, how many seconds of following distance give enough space to steer or brake past a highway hazard?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Many drivers guess two or three seconds, making Pennsylvania's four-second dry baseline a classic permit-exam trap.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: What happens to your crash-avoidance options if you follow too closely and the lead vehicle suddenly slows or stops?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Riding a rear bumper eats up your reaction window before your foot even moves from accelerator to brake.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: How does keeping a safe forward following gap protect you from being struck from behind?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Gradual deceleration lets trailing traffic match your slowing pace instead of slamming into your trunk during a panic stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: How do you measure your following time using a fixed roadside object, and what count means you are too close?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Counting from the moment the lead bumper clears a signpost or shadow tells you immediately if you crept under four seconds.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Why must you stretch your following gap beyond four seconds on wet, slippery, or unpaved surfaces?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Water, ice, and loose gravel cut tire traction sharply, stretching the pavement your brakes need to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: How should you adjust your forward space when a vehicle behind you wants to pass?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Leaving a wider pocket ahead gives an overtaking driver a safe landing spot to tuck back into your lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: Why should you drop farther back behind a driver whose rearward view is blocked?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: A driver who cannot spot your car in an inside mirror may brake suddenly without knowing you are behind them.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: Why do you need extra following distance behind a large truck or bus that blocks your view ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Tailing a tall trailer blinds you to brake lights and debris up ahead until it is too late to react.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: How should you adjust following space behind a heavily loaded vehicle or one pulling a trailer?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Loaded trucks and towed trailers accelerate sluggishly and react differently on grades or bumps than empty passenger sedans.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: How should your following cushion change when approaching slow-moving road users, including bicycles?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Closing rapidly on a bicycle shrinks space much faster than car-to-car traffic, and riders have no brake lights.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: Why must you keep extra room behind school buses, transit buses, taxis, and hazardous-material trucks?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Buses and placarded hazmat haulers stop at railroad tracks even without flashing gates, and taxis pull curbward abruptly.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Why should you open a larger following space on downhill grades, especially at high speeds?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Gravity pushes your vehicle's mass downhill against the brakes, making speed harder to shed quickly.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: Why must you stop with extra space behind the vehicle ahead when waiting on an uphill slope?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Cars and heavy trucks often roll backward slightly as drivers shift from brake to throttle when traffic restarts.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: What safety advantage does keeping open space beside your vehicle give you in traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: An open pocket next to your doors lets you steer cleanly away if another driver cuts into your lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: Why should you avoid driving directly alongside other vehicles on multilane highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Pacing door-to-door blocks your side view, seals off escape lanes, and parks your car inside blind spots.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: How much room should you keep between your car and oncoming traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Opposing vehicles close at combined speeds, so holding generous centerline separation protects against distracted lane drifters.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: How should you make room for vehicles entering a highway from an on-ramp when conditions allow?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Checking mirrors, signaling, and sliding one lane inward clears the merge zone smoothly without surprising fast inside traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: Which three sudden curbside hazards require keeping extra side space next to parked vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Swinging car doors, pedestrians stepping between bumpers, and cars nosing out leave zero braking distance up close.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: How wide must a usable side escape path be, and how do you compensate if neither side offers one?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: When guardrails, curbs, or traffic pinch both sides narrower than eight feet, extra forward time becomes your sole buffer.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: Where do you normally steer inside a lane, and how do you adjust when parked cars line your right and oncoming cars approach left?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Easing off the gas and steering a balanced middle line divides clearance evenly between swinging doors and oncoming mirrors.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: What two speed and signaling habits help you preserve a safe cushion behind your vehicle before turning?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Activating your turn signal before touching the brakes alerts trailing drivers early so they slow smoothly with you.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: When a driver tailgates you on a multilane road, what lane choice solves the problem first?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Shifting safely into the right lane lets an impatient driver pass cleanly ahead instead of riding your bumper.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: If there is no right lane to move into, how should you encourage a tailgater to pass?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Waiting for an open stretch ahead and lightly tapping the brakes lowers speed gradually without triggering a rear-end hit.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: What should you look for beside your vehicle before slowing down or stopping?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Identifying an open shoulder or adjacent gap ahead of time gives you an instant bailout if trailing brakes screech.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: What two details should you track in rear-quarter traffic, and how must you verify blind spots before changing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Monitoring how fast rear-quarter cars close in and turning your head catches vehicles hidden outside mirror glass.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: How does the Pennsylvania driver's manual define a blind spot?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Mirrors leave rear-side pockets hidden unless you physically turn your head to sweep past the roof pillars.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: Which position near another vehicle puts you in its blind spot, and what two speed choices move you clear?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Hovering beside and slightly behind another car hides you right where a sudden lane change will clip your fender.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: While overtaking another vehicle, how should you handle time spent in that driver's blind spot?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Moving decisively past the other driver's rear quarter cuts the window where they might drift over without seeing you.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: How many seconds ahead — and roughly how far in city versus highway driving — should you search for trouble?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Looking a city block ahead in town or a quarter mile on highways catches brake waves early.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: Where should your eyes roam as you drive instead of fixing only on the middle of your lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Scanning curb to shoulder spots children, cyclists, and nose-out cars long before they enter your travel path.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: Which four traffic and sign clues should you actively watch for when scanning down the road?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Spotting slow entrants, paused turners, warning diamonds, and exit signs early prevents abrupt braking or late lane dives.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: Which three roadside junctions require extra side-to-side scanning because traffic streams converge?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Drivers pulling from shopping-center aprons, cross streets, or entrance ramps can misjudge your speed and nose into your path.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: Why must you look left, right, and left again before pulling into an intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Vehicles from your left cross your path first, and a second left glance catches fast cars masked earlier.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: After you begin entering an intersection, why should you check both sides one more time?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Never trust green bulbs or cross-street stop signs blindly when a red-light runner could still barrel through.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.question_text: How should you proceed at an intersection when shrubs, buildings, or parked vehicles hide cross-street traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.teaching_text: Creeping forward inches at a time lets you lean into a clear view before committing your hood into traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.question_text: Besides routine mirror sweeps, before which two maneuvers is checking rear traffic especially important?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.teaching_text: Frequent mirror checks keep an updated mental map so lane changes and backing maneuvers never surprise closing traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.question_text: How does Pennsylvania treat entering a highway from a ramp or pulling onto a road from a curb or shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.teaching_text: Every merge from an entrance ramp or parked curb requires the exact same signal, mirror, and shoulder-check routine.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.question_text: Before shifting lanes, what signal, mirror, and overtaking checks must you complete?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.teaching_text: Verifying nobody behind has already started passing prevents cutting straight across a faster vehicle's front bumper.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.question_text: Along with mirrors or blind-spot sensors, what physical check is still required before moving lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F41.teaching_text: Turning your chin quickly toward your shoulder confirms no motorcycle or small car slipped past mirrors and radar.

sec08-card-sec08-F42.question_text: How long at most should a blind-spot shoulder check take your eyes away from the road ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-F42.teaching_text: Looking over your shoulder longer than one second leaves you driving blind if lead traffic suddenly slams its brakes.

sec08-card-sec08-F43.question_text: On a road with three or more lanes, why must you scan across every lane before moving into an open gap?
sec08-card-sec08-F43.teaching_text: A driver two lanes over can dive into the exact same center opening at the exact same moment.

sec08-card-sec08-F44.question_text: Before climbing into your vehicle to back up, what check should you make behind the rear bumper?
sec08-card-sec08-F44.teaching_text: Small children, pets, and toys sit inside a low rear blind zone that driver-seat glass cannot reveal.

sec08-card-sec08-F45.question_text: Before backing up, how should you position your view rather than trusting only mirrors or backup sensors?
sec08-card-sec08-F45.teaching_text: Looking directly out the rear window gives wide peripheral awareness that narrow mirrors and proximity chimes cannot match.

sec08-card-sec08-F46.question_text: Which four factors must guide your speed choice since no single speed stays safe all the time?
sec08-card-sec08-F46.teaching_text: Blending posted signs with surface grip, visibility, and surrounding flow keeps your pace matched to changing hazards.

sec08-card-sec08-F47.question_text: What responsibility do you have toward nearby drivers whenever you plan to change speed?
sec08-card-sec08-F47.teaching_text: Early brake taps or turn signals warn following drivers before your gap shrinks unexpectedly.

sec08-card-sec08-F48.question_text: What driving conditions does a posted maximum speed sign assume?
sec08-card-sec08-F48.teaching_text: Maximum speed plaques reflect dry pavement, clear weather, and light traffic rather than rain, glare, or congestion.

sec08-card-sec08-F49.question_text: What is Pennsylvania's highest posted speed limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F49.teaching_text: Seventy miles per hour is the absolute top posted ceiling anywhere on Pennsylvania interstates or turnpikes.

sec08-card-sec08-F50.question_text: Where along an interstate highway does Pennsylvania post maximum-speed signs?
sec08-card-sec08-F50.teaching_text: Mounting a speed sign right after each entrance interchange tells newly merged drivers the legal cap immediately.

sec08-card-sec08-F51.question_text: Approximately how often do maximum-speed signs appear along non-interstate Pennsylvania highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F51.teaching_text: Checking roadside signs every half mile keeps you alert when rural speed zones step down near villages.

sec08-card-sec08-F52.question_text: What is Pennsylvania's school-zone speed limit when warning lights flash or during posted hours?
sec08-card-sec08-F52.teaching_text: Slowing to fifteen miles per hour gives darting children survival margin and spares you steep school-zone penalties.

sec08-card-sec08-F53.question_text: How must you adjust speed in wet, slick, or low-visibility conditions — and can police ticket you below the posted limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F53.teaching_text: Driving at the posted number through downpours or ice still violates Pennsylvania's safe-speed law and earns a citation.

sec08-card-sec08-F54.question_text: Which two aggressive pedal habits should you skip for economical driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F54.teaching_text: Accelerating smoothly and easing off early saves fuel at every green light while extending brake and tire life.

sec08-card-sec08-F55.question_text: Why can avoiding trips during the hottest hours of the day help fuel mileage?
sec08-card-sec08-F55.teaching_text: Cooler air carries denser oxygen into the engine for cleaner power and reduces peak air-conditioning strain.

sec08-card-sec08-F56.question_text: Why should you consult your dealer when the dashboard onboard-diagnostics lamp turns on?
sec08-card-sec08-F56.teaching_text: An illuminated diagnostics warning signals engine or sensor trouble that can quietly burn extra gas and raise exhaust pollution.

sec08-card-sec08-F57.question_text: Which three engine and climate functions does a vehicle's ECO button adjust to boost efficiency?
sec08-card-sec08-F57.teaching_text: Turning on ECO mode softens jumpy pedal inputs, refines gear shifts, and trims air-conditioner compressor drag.

sec08-card-sec08-F58.question_text: What does the Pennsylvania manual advise about idling — and which gears reduce engine load if you must wait running?
sec08-card-sec08-F58.teaching_text: Idling gets zero miles per gallon, and shifting out of drive takes torque-converter strain off a waiting engine.

sec08-card-sec08-F59.question_text: Which five travel or trip-planning habits cut total driving miles, fuel burn, and travel costs?
sec08-card-sec08-F59.teaching_text: Linking errands into one trip or sharing rides trims fuel bills and keeps extra cold-start wear off your car.

sec08-card-sec08-F60.question_text: Alongside reduced visibility, what glare and driver-condition risks grow more common after dark?
sec08-card-sec08-F60.teaching_text: Nighttime shrinks sight distance right when oncoming headlight glare and drowsy or impaired drivers peak on roadways.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Which three visual abilities drop in dim light and make unexpected walkers or cyclists harder to notice?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Twilight and darkness flatten depth perception and dull peripheral sight right where unlit pedestrians step off curbs.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: What two-sided visibility job do your headlights perform on the road?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Switching headlamps on early helps oncoming drivers and waiting cross traffic spot your approach from blocks away.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: How frequently at minimum does Pennsylvania recommend cleaning your headlights?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Splashed road film and winter salt quietly dim headlamp reach long before a bulb ever burns out.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: When should you turn on headlights during gloomy daylight or against gray roadside backgrounds?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Neutral-colored vehicles blend straight into wet pavement and overcast skies unless headlamps cut through the haze.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: During storms like rain, snow, sleet, or hail — plus fog, smoke, or smog — what must be on and which beam belongs?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: High beams bounce blinding white glare off airborne water drops, snowflakes, and smoke right back at your windshield.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: At what forward visibility distance for spotting people or vehicles does Pennsylvania require headlights?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Whenever mist, dusk, or heavy spray hides pedestrians inside one thousand feet, state law requires full headlamps.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: Between which two daily sun events must your headlights remain on in Pennsylvania?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Dusk and dawn twilight hide unlit cars even when the sky overhead still looks partly bright.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: What headlight rule applies whenever you travel through a Pennsylvania work zone?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Lit headlamps help roadside crews and flaggers spot live traffic clearly amid flashing beacons and dust.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: What does Pennsylvania law require whenever weather forces continuous or intermittent windshield-wiper use?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Even intermittent wiper sweeps in light mist trigger the state mandate to switch on your headlamps.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Why aren't daytime running lamps legal substitutes when headlights are required, and what rear lights must glow?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Daytime front LEDs leave the rear of your car completely dark inside rain spray, tunnels, or dusk.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: What starting fine and total cost with fees does the manual note for Pennsylvania headlight violations?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Mandatory court costs and fees push a twenty-five-dollar base headlight citation close to one hundred dollars.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: Within what distance of an oncoming vehicle — or behind a vehicle ahead — must you switch to low beams at night?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Keeping those five-hundred and three-hundred-foot cutoffs straight avoids dazzling oncoming eyes or blinding lead mirrors.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.question_text: Where should you look if an oncoming driver leaves high beams on despite a few brief reminder flashes?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.teaching_text: Guiding off the right pavement edge protects your night-adapted vision while keeping your tires safely inside your lane.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.question_text: How should you treat your high-beam switch if another driver refuses to dim glaring headlights?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.teaching_text: Flashing high beams back in anger blinds the oncoming driver too and doubles the risk of a head-on wreck.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.question_text: What adjustment tames uncomfortable glare from bright headlights directly behind your vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.teaching_text: Flipping the rearview mirror tab angles out harsh beam reflection while keeping rear traffic visible.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.question_text: What rule links your nighttime travel speed to the stretch of road lit by your headlights?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.teaching_text: Driving faster than your beams reach guarantees you cannot stop before striking an unlit obstacle ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.question_text: Roughly how far ahead do standard low-beam headlights illuminate the road?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.teaching_text: Two hundred fifty feet passes in barely three seconds at highway speed, leaving tight margin after dark.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour on dry pavement, how does total stopping distance compare to two hundred fifty feet?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.teaching_text: Even on bone-dry asphalt, fifty-five miles per hour needs more than two hundred fifty feet to halt completely.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.question_text: To avoid outrunning your headlights on a dark road at night, what top speed does the Pennsylvania manual advise?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.teaching_text: Holding forty-five miles per hour or less keeps your dry stopping distance safely inside low-beam sightlines.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.question_text: How should you adjust speed over poor pavement and when taking slippery curves or turns?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.teaching_text: Braking gently before entering a slick bend keeps cornering forces below the point where tires break traction.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.question_text: During which minutes of a rainfall does pavement often turn most slippery?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.teaching_text: Initial rain mixes with accumulated motor oil and dust into a slick film before steady rain rinses it off.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.question_text: What substance does rain lift to the top of asphalt, and how does hot weather affect that hazard?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.teaching_text: Hot sunshine bakes oils toward the pavement surface, making summer cloudbursts unexpectedly greasy under braking.

sec08-card-sec08-R23.question_text: In cold, wet conditions, how do tree-shaded or hillside-shaded spots compare with sunlit pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.teaching_text: Drivers cruising confidently on dry sunlit bends often hit surprise frost patches hidden beneath evergreens or overpasses.

sec08-card-sec08-R24.question_text: What happens to your tires when your vehicle begins hydroplaning?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.teaching_text: Lifted onto a thin wedge of water, tires lose direct asphalt contact needed to steer or brake.

sec08-card-sec08-R25.question_text: At how low a speed and in what water depth can hydroplaning begin?
sec08-card-sec08-R25.teaching_text: Just one-tenth of an inch of rain at thirty-five miles per hour can float tires off the road.

sec08-card-sec08-R26.question_text: What tire condition raises hydroplaning danger, and what driver adjustment lowers it?
sec08-card-sec08-R26.teaching_text: Deep tread grooves channel water away, whereas bald rubber floats easily unless you drop your speed.

sec08-card-sec08-R27.question_text: If your tires start hydroplaning, what should you do with the wheel and gas pedal — and what must you avoid?
sec08-card-sec08-R27.teaching_text: Letting speed bleed off naturally restores tire contact smoothly, whereas hard braking or jerking the wheel causes spins.

sec08-card-sec08-R28.question_text: While hydroplaning, how should you steer to stay on the road and how should you brake if forced to?
sec08-card-sec08-R28.teaching_text: Minimal steering inputs and feather-light braking keep wheels pointed straight down the lane when grip snaps back.

sec08-card-sec08-R29.question_text: How do snow and ice affect road grip and your two main vehicle controls?
sec08-card-sec08-R29.teaching_text: Slippery winter pack robs front tires of turning bite and stretches stopping distances across every vehicle type.

sec08-card-sec08-R30.question_text: Why does rain or sleet near thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit create pavement slicker than dry, solid ice?
sec08-card-sec08-R30.teaching_text: A thin film of liquid water over thirty-two-degree ice acts like grease under rubber, cutting grip below subzero ice.

sec08-card-sec08-R31.question_text: What combination of road sheen and tire spray warns you that black ice may coat the lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R31.teaching_text: When shiny cold asphalt stops throwing mist off tires ahead, invisible black ice has frozen the surface solid.

sec08-card-sec08-R32.question_text: What pre-trip winter cleanup does PennDOT urge before driving after snowfall or freezing rain?
sec08-card-sec08-R32.teaching_text: Leaving snow piled on roofs or hoods sends blinding white sheets flying across windshields at highway speed.

sec08-card-sec08-R34.question_text: How much should you reduce your speed when driving on packed snow?
sec08-card-sec08-R34.teaching_text: Cutting normal speed in half keeps braking and cornering demands inside packed snow's reduced friction budget.

sec08-card-sec08-R35.question_text: What pace should you drop down to when driving on ice?
sec08-card-sec08-R35.teaching_text: On sheer ice, anything faster than a slow crawl carries enough momentum to slide straight past turns or stops.

sec08-card-sec08-R36.question_text: About how many times your normal following space should you leave on snow-covered or icy roads?
sec08-card-sec08-R36.teaching_text: Multiplying your usual dry cushion by ten gives long winter stopping runs room to finish without impact.

sec08-card-sec08-R37.question_text: Why must you never engage cruise control on slippery pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-R37.teaching_text: Cruise control keeps applying engine power if a tire slips, sustaining wheelspin instead of letting tires regain grip.

sec08-card-sec08-R38.question_text: How can smart speed pacing lower crash risk near slippery shaded patches or frosty bridges?
sec08-card-sec08-R38.teaching_text: Adjusting speed early avoids passing oncoming traffic right on narrow icy bridge decks where cars slide sideways.

sec08-card-sec08-R39.question_text: How should you approach a red signal on icy or packed-snow roads so you preserve traction?
sec08-card-sec08-R39.teaching_text: Timing a gentle coast so queued cars start rolling before you arrive avoids polished-ice wheelspin from a dead stop.

sec08-card-sec08-R40.question_text: Why must you leave a generous gap before starting up a wintry hill behind another vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R40.teaching_text: If the lead driver slows on the grade, extra space lets you keep rolling rather than stalling mid-hill.

sec08-card-sec08-R41.question_text: What gear choice before cresting a wintry downhill helps hold your vehicle under control?
sec08-card-sec08-R41.teaching_text: Shifting down before the slope starts lets smooth engine braking check your speed without locking icy wheels.

sec08-card-sec08-R42.question_text: What should you do before leaving if fog outside is so dense that you cannot see?
sec08-card-sec08-R42.teaching_text: Staying parked until thick fog lifts beats pulling onto roads where stopped vehicles vanish feet ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-R43.question_text: Where should you pull over and wait if blinding fog closes in after your trip is underway?
sec08-card-sec08-R43.teaching_text: Getting completely off the roadway into a parking lot keeps fog-blinded traffic from following your taillights onto shoulders.

sec08-card-sec08-R44.question_text: While parked off-road waiting for dense fog to clear, what two safety items must remain engaged?
sec08-card-sec08-R44.teaching_text: Staying belted with four-way hazard lights blinking protects you if another disoriented driver wanders into the lot.

sec08-card-sec08-R45.question_text: How slow should you drive in fog, and why must you watch your speedometer closely?
sec08-card-sec08-R45.teaching_text: Fog masks roadside speed cues, tricking drivers into creeping faster without noticing unless they check the gauge.

sec08-card-sec08-R46.question_text: Which lights should you use in daytime or nighttime fog — and why are high beams the wrong choice?
sec08-card-sec08-R46.teaching_text: High beams aim upward into suspended mist droplets and bounce blinding white glare straight back at your eyes.

sec08-card-sec08-R47.question_text: Which four glass and body panels must you clear before snowy travel so neither your view nor trailing windshields get blocked?
sec08-card-sec08-R47.teaching_text: Unbrushed hood snow blows up onto your own wipers while roof and trunk slabs smash into drivers behind.

sec08-card-sec08-R48.question_text: Which three sets of exterior lights must you brush free of snow, ice, and road grime?
sec08-card-sec08-R48.teaching_text: Packed slush crusted over lenses hides your beams, brake glow, and turn blinkers right when traction is worst.

sec08-card-sec08-R49.question_text: Why should you let your engine warm before driving off in snowy, icy conditions?
sec08-card-sec08-R49.teaching_text: Giving heater coolant a moment to warm lets the defroster clear stubborn frost instead of refreezing sleet mid-drive.

sec08-card-sec08-R50.question_text: What wiper habit and reservoir fluid rule keep your windshield clean during snowy drives?
sec08-card-sec08-R50.teaching_text: Salty road spray coats glass constantly in winter, and summer fluid freezes solid in lines when you need it.

sec08-card-sec08-R51.question_text: How do you prevent steamed-up windows in cold weather, and what guide explains your car's exact controls?
sec08-card-sec08-R51.teaching_text: Wet winter coats and warm breath fog interior glass fast unless defroster airflow stays dialed per your manual.

sec08-card-sec08-R52.question_text: Why should you switch on low-beam headlights during snowy weather even in the middle of the day?
sec08-card-sec08-R52.teaching_text: Bright white snow swirl camouflages unlit cars in daylight unless low beams and taillights mark your position.

sec08-card-sec08-R53.question_text: How quickly can a snow squall strike dry pavement, and what twin visibility and surface dangers appear?
sec08-card-sec08-R53.teaching_text: Clear dry lanes can vanish into blinding whiteout and flash-frozen ice within seconds during a squall burst.

sec08-card-sec08-R54.question_text: Which two forecast and roadside tools help you spot snow-squall hazards early?
sec08-card-sec08-R54.teaching_text: Weather alerts and overhead highway message boards give critical advance warning before you enter a squall corridor.

sec08-card-sec08-R55.question_text: How should you adjust trip timing or routing around snow squalls, and which roads pose the highest danger?
sec08-card-sec08-R55.teaching_text: High-speed interstate traffic cannot stop inside sudden whiteouts, making schedule or route changes far safer.

sec08-card-sec08-R56.question_text: What action should you take if a snow squall is approaching or reported nearby?
sec08-card-sec08-R56.teaching_text: Leaving the highway before the whiteout wall arrives keeps you out of multi-vehicle chain-reaction crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-R57.question_text: If a snow squall overtakes you on the road, how should you handle speed, hazard lights, and the brake pedal?
sec08-card-sec08-R57.teaching_text: Easing speed smoothly with four-ways blinking warns trailing cars without locking your tires across flash-frozen asphalt.

sec08-card-sec08-R58.question_text: After a collision during a snow squall, where should you stay whenever possible?
sec08-card-sec08-R58.teaching_text: Your car's steel frame shields you far better than standing exposed on icy lanes while blinded traffic slides in.

sec08-card-sec08-R59.question_text: What trip decision does an active snow-squall warning along your route call for?
sec08-card-sec08-R59.teaching_text: Postponing departure or taking another route dodges brief, intense whiteout bands completely.

sec08-card-sec08-R60.question_text: When rain or snow requires continuous or intermittent wipers, which front and rear lights must be on instead of daytime running lamps?
sec08-card-sec08-R60.teaching_text: Daytime running lamps leave your tail dark, so turn the main switch on whenever wipers clear weather.

sec08-card-sec08-R61.question_text: What base fine and approximate total with fees apply to a Pennsylvania wiper-and-headlight violation?
sec08-card-sec08-R61.teaching_text: Forgetting headlamps while running wipers in rain carries a twenty-five-dollar fine that nears one hundred with surcharges.

sec08-card-sec08-R62.question_text: How should you match surrounding traffic speed without breaking Pennsylvania speed law?
sec08-card-sec08-R62.teaching_text: Moving smoothly with traffic avoids speed differentials, but the posted sign always remains your legal ceiling.

sec08-card-sec08-R64.question_text: When a bicyclist rides ahead on your right while oncoming traffic approaches, what order of moves is safest?
sec08-card-sec08-R64.teaching_text: Waiting behind the rider until the opposing lane empties lets you swing left with full passing clearance.

sec08-card-sec08-R65.question_text: At an emergency scene, police stop, or recovery tow truck, what lane move must you make — or how much below the limit must you slow?
sec08-card-sec08-R65.teaching_text: Whenever traffic blocks shifting into a nonadjacent lane, dropping at least twenty miles per hour below posted speed is mandatory.

sec08-card-sec08-R66.question_text: Which three heavy, agricultural, or animal-powered road users build speed slowly when entering traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-R66.teaching_text: Spotting tractors, horse-drawn buggies, or loaded semis pulling out early gives you room to ease off smoothly.

sec08-card-sec08-R67.question_text: How do large trucks typically warn trailing drivers that they have slowed way down on long or steep upgrades?
sec08-card-sec08-R67.teaching_text: Four-way flashers on a mountain grade tell you immediately that you are closing fast on a slow rig.

sec08-card-sec08-R68.question_text: Which vehicles display an orange rear triangle, and what maximum design speed does it signify?
sec08-card-sec08-R68.teaching_text: Recognizing that reflective triangle from afar prevents dangerous highway-speed closures behind farm gear or buggies.

sec08-card-sec08-R69.question_text: How should you follow farm tractors and horse-drawn vehicles, and what horn rule applies before passing?
sec08-card-sec08-R69.teaching_text: Sounding a horn near draft horses can startle the animal into lunging directly across your passing path.

sec08-card-sec08-R70.question_text: When drivers behind may not expect you to slow or stop, how should you use your brake pedal to grab their attention?
sec08-card-sec08-R70.teaching_text: Flashing your brake lights three or four quick taps snaps trailing eyes awake faster than steady braking.

sec08-card-sec08-R71.question_text: Below what speed on a limited-access highway must Pennsylvania drivers switch on hazard flashers?
sec08-card-sec08-R71.teaching_text: Turning four-way flashers on below forty miles per hour warns expressway traffic of a steep speed gap.

sec08-card-sec08-R72.question_text: What does a turn signal communicate to nearby traffic — and does it give you priority to turn?
sec08-card-sec08-R72.teaching_text: Blinking an indicator announces your plan, yet you still owe right-of-way until a safe gap opens.

sec08-card-sec08-R73.question_text: When driving below thirty-five miles per hour, at least how many feet before a turn must you signal?
sec08-card-sec08-R73.teaching_text: Signaling at least one hundred feet early gives town traffic and crosswalk users fair warning before you turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R74.question_text: When traveling thirty-five miles per hour or faster, how many feet before turning must you activate your signal?
sec08-card-sec08-R74.teaching_text: Pennsylvania jumps required signal lead distance from one hundred to three hundred feet once speed hits thirty-five.

sec08-card-sec08-R75.question_text: What must you use to communicate turns and stops if your vehicle's electric turn indicators fail?
sec08-card-sec08-R75.teaching_text: Standardized driver-side arm signals keep surrounding drivers informed safely until faulty bulbs or relays are repaired.

sec08-card-sec08-R76.question_text: Which three maneuvers does the Pennsylvania manual's hand-signal chart cover when electric indicators fail?
sec08-card-sec08-R76.teaching_text: Distinct left-arm positions out the driver window cover left turns, right turns, and slowing or stopping.

sec08-card-sec08-R77.question_text: What real-world pedestrian example does the manual give for sounding your horn when someone may not see your car?
sec08-card-sec08-R77.teaching_text: Tapping the horn immediately when a child starts darting off the curb can freeze their step before impact.

sec08-card-sec08-R78.question_text: How do you separate simultaneous hazards when an oncoming car meets you right behind a bicyclist?
sec08-card-sec08-R78.teaching_text: Handling one conflict at a time — slowing first so oncoming traffic clears — avoids squeezing past the rider.

sec08-card-sec08-R79.question_text: What four actions secure your vehicle and signal for help during a highway breakdown?
sec08-card-sec08-R79.teaching_text: Signaling well off the travel lane in plain sight with flashers blinking and hood raised prevents shoulder strikes.

sec08-card-sec08-R80.question_text: Which two visibility or collision situations justify sounding your vehicle's horn?
sec08-card-sec08-R80.teaching_text: Use the horn to alert an unaware walker or driver, or whenever another vehicle drifts toward hitting you.

sec08-card-sec08-R81.question_text: What should you sound immediately to warn nearby traffic if you lose control of your vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R81.teaching_text: Holding the horn while out of control gives surrounding drivers precious seconds to steer clear of your slide.

sec08-card-sec08-R82.question_text: After oncoming traffic clears, at least how many feet of side space must Pennsylvania drivers leave when passing a cyclist?
sec08-card-sec08-R82.teaching_text: Pennsylvania's four-foot bicycle passing buffer prevents wind blast or mirror clips if the rider dodges road debris.
